#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Spike harness: runs commands, records them with their output, and writes a PASS/FAIL evidence file.
# Any value from ./secrets/credentials is replaced by a visible placeholder before it reaches the file.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../lib.sh"
SPIKE_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/scripts/spikes"
EV_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/docs/evidence"

redact() {
  python3 -I -c '
import glob, os, sys
data = sys.stdin.read()
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "*")):
    value = open(path).read().strip()
    if value:
        data = data.replace(value, "[REDACTED:" + os.path.basename(path) + "]")
sys.stdout.write(data)' "$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"
}

ev_start() { # id title question criteria
  SPIKE=$1; TITLE=$2; QUESTION=$3; CRITERIA=$4; NS="spike-$(echo "$1" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
  BODY=$(mktemp); CHECKS=$(mktemp); FAILS=0; T0=$SECONDS; STARTED=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
  kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl delete ns "$NS" --wait=true >/dev/null
  trap ev_cleanup EXIT
}
ev_cleanup() {
  [ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || kubectl delete ns "$NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
}
section() { printf '\n## %s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; log "== $1"; }
run() { # command string; output is recorded. Returns the command's exit code.
  local out rc=0
  out=$(eval "$1" 2>&1) || rc=$?
  { printf '\n```console\n$ %s\n' "$1"; printf '%s\n' "$out"; [ $rc -eq 0 ] || printf '[exit code %s]\n' "$rc"; printf '```\n'; } | redact >> "$BODY"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | redact | tail -"${TAIL:-12}"
  return $rc
}
note() { printf '\n%s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; }
check() { # description, command...
  local d=$1; shift
  if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '| %s | PASS |\n' "$d" >> "$CHECKS"; log "PASS  $d"
  else printf '| %s | **FAIL** |\n' "$d" >> "$CHECKS"; log "FAIL  $d"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); fi
}
ev_finish() {
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  local f="$EV_DIR/L0-spike-$SPIKE.md"; mkdir -p "$EV_DIR"
  { printf '# L0 spike %s: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$SPIKE" "$TITLE" "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **Question:** %s\n- **Pass criteria:** %s\n' "$QUESTION" "$CRITERIA"
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make spike-%s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$(echo "$SPIKE" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
    printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
    printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$f"
  log "RESULT $SPIKE: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L0-spike-$SPIKE.md"
  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}
wait_job() { # job timeout-seconds; succeeds only if the Job completes
  local end=$((SECONDS+$2)) s f
  while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
    s=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    f=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    [ "${s:-0}" -ge 1 ] && return 0; [ "${f:-0}" -ge 1 ] && return 1; sleep 1
  done; return 1
}
apply_yaml() { sed "s|__IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|g; s|__NS__|$NS|g" | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - ; }

## What changes later phases

1. **L1:** the certs assume namespaces `pg-ha` and `pg-restore` and a headless Service named `pg-headless`. Using other names means reissuing them.
2. **L2:** the 13 s in ADR-006 bounds when Patroni *issues* the demotion. Postgres must then stop within the remaining 7 s, so I added that measurement to `T:split-brain`.
3. **L3:** `pgbackrest verify` can **exit 0 while reporting `status: error`**, so the backup job and alerts must check the reported status.
4. **L4:** `pg_amcheck` needs `--install-missing`, which is fine on the scratch restore but should not run against production.
5. **L6:** API egress policy must allow the API server's **real backend IP and port**. Allowing only the Service IP stays blocked, so the address has to be discovered at deploy time.

Evidence is in `docs/evidence/L0-spike-S1.md` through `L0-spike-S4.md`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Generates credentials into ./secrets. Never overwrites, and never prints a value.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
umask 077
mkdir -p "$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"; chmod 700 "$SECRETS_DIR" "$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"
created=0; kept=0

gen() { # name openssl-rand-args...
  local f="$SECRETS_DIR/credentials/$1" tmp; shift
  if [ -s "$f" ]; then kept=$((kept+1)); return; fi
  tmp=$(mktemp "$f.XXXXXX")
  openssl rand "$@" | tr -d '\n' > "$tmp"
  # ln fails if the target exists, so a concurrent run cannot replace a value.
  if ln "$tmp" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then created=$((created+1)); else kept=$((kept+1)); fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
}

for r in postgres replicator rewind monitor backup app app_ro; do gen "pg-$r-password" -hex 24; done
gen pgbackrest-cipher-passphrase -base64 48
gen garage-rpc-secret -hex 32        # Garage requires exactly 32 bytes in hex
gen garage-admin-token -hex 32
gen garage-metrics-token -hex 32
gen garage-s3-secret-key -hex 32     # Garage requires 32 bytes in hex

# Garage access key IDs are GK + 12 bytes in hex.
f="$SECRETS_DIR/credentials/garage-s3-access-key-id"
if [ -s "$f" ]; then kept=$((kept+1)); else
  tmp=$(mktemp "$f.XXXXXX"); printf 'GK%s' "$(openssl rand -hex 12)" > "$tmp"
  if ln "$tmp" "$f" 2>/dev/null; then created=$((created+1)); else kept=$((kept+1)); fi
  rm -f "$tmp"
fi
log "Secrets: $created created, $kept kept (in ./secrets/credentials, values not shown)"

# Known limitations

This file lists what the system does not protect against or does not implement (R12.5, HC10). Entries are added as each phase confirms them.

## Backups

### Backup repository is not off-site

The in-cluster Garage repository shares the VM and disk with the database, so it is not off-site disaster protection. In production, the pgBackRest repository points at GCS/S3 with bucket versioning and a retention lock, off-site from the cluster, using keyless workload identity where available.

- **Why it is the default:** `make up` must work for any reviewer with no cloud account or credentials.
- **Planned option:** R4.7 adds `BACKUP_TARGET=gcs make up`. It is OPTIONAL and not built yet.
- **Decision:** ADR-014.

# Known limitations

This file lists what the system does not protect against or does not implement (R12.5, HC10). Entries are added as each phase confirms them.

## Backups

### Backup repository is not off-site

The in-cluster Garage repository shares the VM and disk with the database, so it is not off-site disaster protection. In production, the pgBackRest repository points at GCS/S3 with bucket versioning and a retention lock, off-site from the cluster, using keyless workload identity where available.

- **Why it is the default:** `make up` must work for any reviewer with no cloud account or credentials.
- **Planned option:** R4.7 adds `BACKUP_TARGET=gcs make up`. It is OPTIONAL and not built yet.
- **Decision:** ADR-014.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared settings. Sourced by every project script.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT_DIR/versions.env"
set +a

CLUSTER_NAME=pg-ha
API_PORT=6550
BIN_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/bin"
SECRETS_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/secrets"
RUN_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/.run"
export KUBECONFIG="$RUN_DIR/kubeconfig"
export PATH="$BIN_DIR:$PATH"

# Image tag derived from the pinned inputs, so a version change produces a new tag.
pg_version="${POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE#postgres:}"; pg_version="${pg_version%%-*}"
PG_IMAGE="pg-ha-postgres:${pg_version}-patroni${PATRONI_DEB_VERSION%%-*}-pgbackrest${PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION%%-*}"

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
die()  { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
cluster_exists() { k3d cluster list -o json | jq -e --arg n "$CLUSTER_NAME" 'any(.[]; .name == $n)' >/dev/null; }

## Decision

Use **pgBackRest 2.60.1** with the object store from ADR-014:

- A full backup through a CronJob on a **configurable schedule**, defaulting to daily at 20:00 UTC.
- Continuous asynchronous WAL archiving.
- `repo1-retention-full=7`, enforced by automatic `expire`.
- `pgbackrest verify` daily after the backup.
- A single **`make certs`** bootstrap step creates one CA, reused for the pgBackRest TLS server and Postgres TLS.

**Repository settings live in one place.** Every `repo1-*` setting goes in a single `repo.conf`, loaded from pgBackRest's `conf.d` include path. The main config holds only stanza, Postgres and process settings.

- Backup, archive, restore and restore-test workloads all read the same `repo.conf`.
- Credentials never go in `repo.conf`. They come from Kubernetes Secrets at runtime.
- The default `repo.conf` targets Garage with `repo1-type=s3`.
- A later GCS overlay (R4.7) replaces that one file with `repo1-type=gcs`, `repo1-gcs-bucket` and `repo1-gcs-key-type`, and leaves out the Garage workloads. Use `auto` for keyless identity where available. Otherwise use `service`, with a key file supplied at runtime from outside the repo.
- **The overlay is not built yet.**

**The backup schedule is a parameter.** The VM is stopped overnight, so a daily 20:00 UTC run may never fire during testing. Evidence for R4.1 is captured with a short schedule, for example every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`), from a Job the CronJob created itself. The evidence states the schedule that was used.

**Backups follow the primary without config changes.** pgBackRest lists all three Postgres pods as `pg1-host`, `pg2-host` and `pg3-host`, using their stable headless-service DNS names. It determines which one is the current primary at run time, so a backup after failover needs no configuration change.

**Generated secrets survive teardown.** Generated secrets, including the pgBackRest repository cipher passphrase, live in a git-ignored `./secrets/` directory.

- Generation is idempotent and never overwrites an existing value.
- `make down` preserves `./secrets/`.
- Only an explicit **`make clean-secrets`** deletes them, and it warns first that **existing backups become unrecoverable** without the passphrase.

## Consequences

- A check at L3 must confirm that no `repo1-*` setting exists outside `repo.conf`.
- The GCS overlay must also allow egress to GCS in NetworkPolicy and create its stanza in an empty bucket path.
- TLS certificates become a bootstrap dependency, so that work is done once.
- R4.1 needs evidence from a truly scheduled Job, so a cluster must stay up across one schedule.
- The repository cipher passphrase becomes critical: losing it makes backups unrecoverable.

# ADR-012: Security baseline

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

Security is scored, but the brief's FAQ places hardening after replication, backup and monitoring.

## Options considered

- **Minimal:** generated secrets and SCRAM only.
- **Layered baseline:** secrets, TLS, SCRAM, NetworkPolicy, RBAC, hardened pods and separate roles.
- **Full hardening:** adds client certificates, rotation and image scanning.

## Decision

Adopt the **layered baseline, built last**.

- **Bootstrap exceptions:** `make certs` and generated Secrets run first, because pgBackRest depends on them (ADR-009).
- **Auth:** SCRAM, with `hostssl` rules in `pg_hba`.
- **TLS:** one deployment CA for Postgres and pgBackRest. Replication uses `verify-full`.
- **Network:** default-deny NetworkPolicies with explicit allows. k3s includes a policy controller, and enforcement must be proven by test.
- **Kubernetes:** namespaced least-privilege RBAC and Pod Security `restricted` on the database namespace.
- **Database:** separate roles for admin, replication, rewind, monitoring, backup, application and read-only access.

cert-manager is excluded because it is an operator (D1).

## Consequences

- Hardening may be cut in priority order if earlier phases overrun, and any cut is documented.
- Default-deny egress may interfere with API access, which spike S2 tests.
- Object-storage traffic is not TLS-protected (ADR-014).

## R-IDs covered

R8.1, R8.2, R8.3, R8.4, R8.5, R8.6, R8.7, R8.8, R11.7

24	## Split-brain timing argument
25	
26	With `loop_wait=3`, `retry_timeout=5` and `ttl=20`:
27	
28	```text
29	loop_wait + 2 × retry_timeout = 3 + (2 × 5) = 13 s  <  ttl = 20 s
30	```
31	
32	An isolated primary demotes within **13 s** of its last successful lock renewal, before its leader key can expire at **20 s**. No other member can therefore acquire the lock while the old primary may still accept writes.
33	
34	What this rests on, checked against Patroni `v4.1.5` source:
35	
36	- **Expiry cannot start early.** Each replica times the TTL from when it last *observed* the leader record change, using its own clock (`dcs/kubernetes.py`). Observation happens at or after the renewal, so the earliest possible expiry is renewal + 20 s, and no clock synchronisation is needed.
37	- **13 s bounds when demotion is issued, not when Postgres has stopped.** On a failed renewal Patroni calls `demote('immediate-nolock')` (`ha.py`), which stops Postgres in `immediate` mode asynchronously. That stop must finish inside the remaining **7 s margin**. This is an **[Assumption]** until `T:split-brain` measures it.
38	- **The argument needs a running Patroni.** A frozen Patroni never issues the demotion, so the inequality does not protect that case. Synchronous replication is the backstop: once the standbys follow the new leader, the old primary's commits block and are never acknowledged.
39	
40	### What `T:split-brain` must show
41	
42	The fault is `docker network disconnect` on the primary's agent, with a writer running against the old primary throughout. Timestamps are in UTC. The test passes only if all of these hold, in each of its runs:
43	
44	1. **Demotion before expiry:** the old primary stops acknowledging commits no later than 20 s after its last successful renewal. The report states the measured time against the 13 s bound and the 20 s TTL.
45	2. **No overlap:** the last commit acknowledged by the old primary is earlier than the new primary's first acknowledged commit.
46	3. **One lock holder:** the leader key names exactly one member at every sample, and the new leader acquires it only after the old key expired.
47	4. **No lost acknowledged writes:** every commit acknowledged to the client is present on the new primary after failover (RPO 0).
48	5. **Frozen-Patroni case:** with Patroni stopped by `SIGSTOP` on the primary and Postgres still running, commits on the old primary block and none is acknowledged after the standbys leave it.
49	
50	## Consequences

## Split-brain timing argument

With `loop_wait=3`, `retry_timeout=5` and `ttl=20`:

```text
loop_wait + 2 × retry_timeout = 3 + (2 × 5) = 13 s  <  ttl = 20 s
```

An isolated primary demotes within **13 s** of its last successful lock renewal, before its leader key can expire at **20 s**. No other member can therefore acquire the lock while the old primary may still accept writes.

What this rests on, checked against Patroni `v4.1.5` source:

- **Expiry cannot start early.** Each replica times the TTL from when it last *observed* the leader record change, using its own clock (`dcs/kubernetes.py`). Observation happens at or after the renewal, so the earliest possible expiry is renewal + 20 s, and no clock synchronisation is needed.
- **13 s bounds when demotion is issued, not when Postgres has stopped.** On a failed renewal Patroni calls `demote('immediate-nolock')` (`ha.py`), which stops Postgres in `immediate` mode asynchronously. That stop must finish inside the remaining **7 s margin**. This is an **[Assumption]** until `T:split-brain` measures it.
- **The argument needs a running Patroni.** A frozen Patroni never issues the demotion, so the inequality does not protect that case. Synchronous replication is the backstop: once the standbys follow the new leader, the old primary's commits block and are never acknowledged.

### What `T:split-brain` must show

The fault is `docker network disconnect` on the primary's agent, with a writer running against the old primary throughout. Timestamps are in UTC. The test passes only if all of these hold, in each of its runs:

1. **Demotion before expiry:** the old primary stops acknowledging commits no later than 20 s after its last successful renewal. The report states the measured time against the 13 s bound and the 20 s TTL.
2. **No overlap:** the last commit acknowledged by the old primary is earlier than the new primary's first acknowledged commit.
3. **One lock holder:** the leader key names exactly one member at every sample, and the new leader acquires it only after the old key expired.
4. **No lost acknowledged writes:** every commit acknowledged to the client is present on the new primary after failover (RPO 0).
5. **Frozen-Patroni case:** with Patroni stopped by `SIGSTOP` on the primary and Postgres still running, commits on the old primary block and none is acknowledged after the standbys leave it.

## Consequences

3	set -euo pipefail

17	export PATH="$BIN_DIR:$PATH"

14	## Decision
15	
16	Use **pgBackRest 2.60.1** with the object store from ADR-014:
17	
18	- A full backup through a CronJob on a **configurable schedule**, defaulting to daily at 20:00 UTC.
19	- Continuous asynchronous WAL archiving.
20	- `repo1-retention-full=7`, enforced by automatic `expire`.
21	- `pgbackrest verify` daily after the backup.
22	- A single **`make certs`** bootstrap step creates one CA, reused for the pgBackRest TLS server and Postgres TLS.
23	
24	**Repository settings live in one place.** Every `repo1-*` setting goes in a single `repo.conf`, loaded from pgBackRest's `conf.d` include path. The main config holds only stanza, Postgres and process settings.
25	
26	- Backup, archive, restore and restore-test workloads all read the same `repo.conf`.
27	- Credentials never go in `repo.conf`. They come from Kubernetes Secrets at runtime.
28	- The default `repo.conf` targets Garage with `repo1-type=s3`.
29	- A later GCS overlay (R4.7) replaces that one file with `repo1-type=gcs`, `repo1-gcs-bucket` and `repo1-gcs-key-type`, and leaves out the Garage workloads. Use `auto` for keyless identity where available. Otherwise use `service`, with a key file supplied at runtime from outside the repo.
30	- **The overlay is not built yet.**
31	
32	**The backup schedule is a parameter.** The VM is stopped overnight, so a daily 20:00 UTC run may never fire during testing. Evidence for R4.1 is captured with a short schedule, for example every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`), from a Job the CronJob created itself. The evidence states the schedule that was used.
33	
34	**Backups follow the primary without config changes.** pgBackRest lists all three Postgres pods as `pg1-host`, `pg2-host` and `pg3-host`, using their stable headless-service DNS names. It determines which one is the current primary at run time, so a backup after failover needs no configuration change.
35	
36	**Generated secrets survive teardown.** Generated secrets, including the pgBackRest repository cipher passphrase, live in a git-ignored `./secrets/` directory.
37	
38	- Generation is idempotent and never overwrites an existing value.
39	- `make down` preserves `./secrets/`.
40	- Only an explicit **`make clean-secrets`** deletes them, and it warns first that **existing backups become unrecoverable** without the passphrase.
41	
42	## Consequences
43	
44	- A check at L3 must confirm that no `repo1-*` setting exists outside `repo.conf`.
45	- The GCS overlay must also allow egress to GCS in NetworkPolicy and create its stanza in an empty bucket path.
46	- TLS certificates become a bootstrap dependency, so that work is done once.
47	- R4.1 needs evidence from a truly scheduled Job, so a cluster must stay up across one schedule.
48	- The repository cipher passphrase becomes critical: losing it makes backups unrecoverable.
49

15	## Decision
16	
17	- Restore through **Patroni custom bootstrap** in a Kustomize overlay.
18	- Run PITR with `--type=time` and `--target-action=promote`. `TARGET_TIME` must include a timezone offset.
19	- Use **one restore-test Job template** for both a daily CronJob and `make test-restore`. It restores into `emptyDir`, starts Postgres without network exposure, checks marker data and `pg_amcheck`, then exits.
20	- A restored cluster must **not** archive into the source stanza.
21	
22	## Consequences
23	
24	- A passing test exercises the real recovery path.
25	- Restored role passwords must be reset through `post_bootstrap`, to be confirmed during implementation.
26	- In-cluster object storage is lost with the cluster, so this proves namespace-level recovery and not off-site disaster recovery.
27	
28	## R-IDs covered

1	# ADR-012: Security baseline
2	
3	**Status:** Accepted
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Security is scored, but the brief's FAQ places hardening after replication, backup and monitoring.
8	
9	## Options considered
10	
11	- **Minimal:** generated secrets and SCRAM only.
12	- **Layered baseline:** secrets, TLS, SCRAM, NetworkPolicy, RBAC, hardened pods and separate roles.
13	- **Full hardening:** adds client certificates, rotation and image scanning.
14	
15	## Decision
16	
17	Adopt the **layered baseline, built last**.
18	
19	- **Bootstrap exceptions:** `make certs` and generated Secrets run first, because pgBackRest depends on them (ADR-009).
20	- **Auth:** SCRAM, with `hostssl` rules in `pg_hba`.
21	- **TLS:** one deployment CA for Postgres and pgBackRest. Replication uses `verify-full`.
22	- **Network:** default-deny NetworkPolicies with explicit allows. k3s includes a policy controller, and enforcement must be proven by test.
23	- **Kubernetes:** namespaced least-privilege RBAC and Pod Security `restricted` on the database namespace.
24	- **Database:** separate roles for admin, replication, rewind, monitoring, backup, application and read-only access.
25	
26	cert-manager is excluded because it is an operator (D1).
27	
28	## Consequences
29	
30	- Hardening may be cut in priority order if earlier phases overrun, and any cut is documented.
31	- Default-deny egress may interfere with API access, which spike S2 tests.
32	- Object-storage traffic is not TLS-protected (ADR-014).
33	
34	## R-IDs covered
35	
36	R8.1, R8.2, R8.3, R8.4, R8.5, R8.6, R8.7, R8.8, R11.7
37

24	## Split-brain timing argument
25	
26	With `loop_wait=3`, `retry_timeout=5` and `ttl=20`:
27	
28	```text
29	loop_wait + 2 × retry_timeout = 3 + (2 × 5) = 13 s  <  ttl = 20 s
30	```
31	
32	An isolated primary demotes within **13 s** of its last successful lock renewal, before its leader key can expire at **20 s**. No other member can therefore acquire the lock while the old primary may still accept writes.
33	
34	What this rests on, checked against Patroni `v4.1.5` source:
35	
36	- **Expiry cannot start early.** Each replica times the TTL from when it last *observed* the leader record change, using its own clock (`dcs/kubernetes.py`). Observation happens at or after the renewal, so the earliest possible expiry is renewal + 20 s, and no clock synchronisation is needed.
37	- **13 s bounds when demotion is issued, not when Postgres has stopped.** On a failed renewal Patroni calls `demote('immediate-nolock')` (`ha.py`), which stops Postgres in `immediate` mode asynchronously. That stop must finish inside the remaining **7 s margin**. This is an **[Assumption]** until `T:split-brain` measures it.
38	- **The argument needs a running Patroni.** A frozen Patroni never issues the demotion, so the inequality does not protect that case. Synchronous replication is the backstop: once the standbys follow the new leader, the old primary's commits block and are never acknowledged.
39	
40	### What `T:split-brain` must show
41	
42	The fault is `docker network disconnect` on the primary's agent, with a writer running against the old primary throughout. Timestamps are in UTC. The test passes only if all of these hold, in each of its runs:
43	
44	1. **Demotion before expiry:** the old primary stops acknowledging commits no later than 20 s after its last successful renewal. The report states the measured time against the 13 s bound and the 20 s TTL.
45	2. **No overlap:** the last commit acknowledged by the old primary is earlier than the new primary's first acknowledged commit.
46	3. **One lock holder:** the leader key names exactly one member at every sample, and the new leader acquires it only after the old key expired.
47	4. **No lost acknowledged writes:** every commit acknowledged to the client is present on the new primary after failover (RPO 0).
48	5. **Frozen-Patroni case:** with Patroni stopped by `SIGSTOP` on the primary and Postgres still running, commits on the old primary block and none is acknowledged after the standbys leave it.
49	
50	## Consequences
51

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Diagnostic for the S1 136 s hang: times connections to Garage's admin port during first startup.
# Not part of `make spikes`, and writes no evidence file. See docs/evidence/L0-spike-S1-history.md.
#
# Usage: [MODE=unbounded|bounded] [TRIALS=3] [ATTEMPTS=60] [INTERVAL=0.5] [OUT=dir] scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh
#   unbounded  ATTEMPTS curls, one every INTERVAL seconds, with no connect timeout (about 3 min per trial)
#   bounded    one curl with the bootstrap Job's timeout and retry options (under 1 min per trial)
#
# Each trial uses its own namespace, which is always deleted. Tokens are random, used once and never
# printed. Saved output is masked. Uses no kubectl exec and no project credentials.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

MODE=${MODE:-unbounded}; TRIALS=${TRIALS:-3}; ATTEMPTS=${ATTEMPTS:-60}; INTERVAL=${INTERVAL:-0.5}
OUT=${OUT:-$RUN_DIR/s1-garage-startup-race}
case "$MODE" in unbounded|bounded) ;; *) die "MODE must be unbounded or bounded" ;; esac
[[ "$TRIALS" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || die "TRIALS must be a positive integer"
[[ "$ATTEMPTS" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || die "ATTEMPTS must be a positive integer"
[[ "$INTERVAL" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]] || die "INTERVAL must be a number of seconds"

PREFIX="s1-race-$$"; CURRENT_NS=""; TOKENS=""
cleanup() {
  [ -z "$CURRENT_NS" ] || kubectl delete ns "$CURRENT_NS" --wait=true --timeout=120s >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  [ -z "$TOKENS" ] || rm -rf "$TOKENS"
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap 'exit 130' INT TERM

mask() { redact | sed -E 's/GK[0-9a-f]{24}/[MASKED:garage-key-id]/g; s/[0-9a-f]{32,}/[MASKED:hex]/g'; }

umask 077; mkdir -p "$OUT" "$RUN_DIR"; TOKENS=$(mktemp -d "$RUN_DIR/s1-race-tokens.XXXXXX")
for t in GARAGE_RPC_SECRET GARAGE_ADMIN_TOKEN GARAGE_METRICS_TOKEN; do openssl rand -hex 32 | tr -d '\n' > "$TOKENS/$t"; done

manifest() { sed "s|__GARAGE__|$GARAGE_IMAGE|; s|__CURL__|$CURL_IMAGE|; s|__NS__|$1|g; s|__MODE__|$MODE|; s|__ATTEMPTS__|$ATTEMPTS|; s|__INTERVAL__|$INTERVAL|" <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: {name: garage-config}
data:
  garage.toml: |
    metadata_dir = "/data/meta"
    data_dir = "/data/blocks"
    db_engine = "lmdb"
    replication_factor = 1
    metadata_fsync = true
    data_fsync = true
    rpc_bind_addr = "[::]:3901"
    rpc_public_addr = "127.0.0.1:3901"
    [s3_api]
    s3_region = "garage"
    api_bind_addr = "[::]:3900"
    [admin]
    api_bind_addr = "[::]:3903"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: garage-data}
spec:

  resources: {requests: {storage: 1Gi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: garage}
spec:
  selector: {app: garage}
  ports:
  - {name: s3, port: 3900}
  - {name: admin, port: 3903}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: garage}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: garage}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: garage}}
    spec:
      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}
      tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, runAsGroup: 10001, fsGroup: 10001, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
      - name: garage
        image: __GARAGE__
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        envFrom: [{secretRef: {name: garage}}]
        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}

        resources: {requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}, limits: {memory: 256Mi}}
        volumeMounts:
        - {name: data, mountPath: /data}

      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: garage-data}
      - name: config
        configMap: {name: garage-config}
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: probe}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}
      tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 100, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
      - name: probe

        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
        env:
        - {name: MODE, value: "__MODE__"}
        - {name: ATTEMPTS, value: "__ATTEMPTS__"}
        - {name: INTERVAL, value: "__INTERVAL__"}

            done
            wait
          fi
          echo PROBE_DONE

}

rc=0
for T in $(seq 1 "$TRIALS"); do
  NS="$PREFIX-$T"; f="$OUT/$MODE-trial-$T.txt"
  kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 && die "namespace $NS already exists"
  kubectl create ns "$NS" >/dev/null; CURRENT_NS=$NS

    echo "trial=$T mode=$MODE"
    kubectl -n "$NS" get pod -l job-name=probe -o jsonpath='probe_start={.items[0].status.startTime} probe_node={.items[0].spec.nodeName}{"\n"}'
    kubectl -n "$NS" get pod -l app=garage -o jsonpath='garage_start={.items[0].status.containerStatuses[0].state.running.startedAt}{"\n"}garage_ready={.items[0].status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].lastTransitionTime}{"\n"}'
    kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/probe | sort

      END{printf "trial %s: ok=%d refused=%d hung=%d hung_seconds=%.1f-%.1f other=%d\n", t, n[0], n[7], n[28], mn, mx, length(n)>0 ? (NR>0 ? 0 : 0) : 0}' "$f"

  fi

done
log "Masked output: ${OUT#"$ROOT_DIR"/}"

metadata: {name: garage-data}

spec:

- Namespace pg-ha and headless Service pg-headless (names the L0 certs assume).

# ADR-003: official Postgres plus exact PGDG Patroni and pgBackRest. Inputs come from versions.env.
ARG POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE
FROM ${POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE}

ARG PATRONI_DEB_VERSION
ARG PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION

USER root
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        "patroni=${PATRONI_DEB_VERSION}" "pgbackrest=${PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION}"; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    install -d -o postgres -g postgres -m 0750 \
        /etc/patroni /etc/pgbackrest /etc/pgbackrest/conf.d \
        /var/lib/pgbackrest /var/log/pgbackrest /var/spool/pgbackrest

# Numeric UID so Kubernetes runAsNonRoot can verify it. Bypasses the root entrypoint.
USER 999:999
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/bin/patroni"]
CMD ["/etc/patroni/patroni.yml"]

# ADR-001: 1 tainted server + 3 agents. ADR-007: node-monitor-grace-period=20s.

apiVersion: k3d.io/v1alpha5
kind: Simple
metadata:

servers: 1

kubeAPI:

options:

  k3s:
    extraArgs:
      - arg: --disable=traefik,servicelb,metrics-server
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      - arg: --kube-controller-manager-arg=node-monitor-grace-period=20s

      - arg: --node-taint=node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane=true:NoSchedule

    nodeLabels:

      - label: pg-ha/role=infra

  kubeconfig:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One private CA plus Postgres and pgBackRest certs (ADR-009, ADR-012). Never overwrites.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
umask 077
D="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"; mkdir -p "$D"; chmod 700 "$SECRETS_DIR" "$D"

# Namespaces the certs must be valid in: the main one and the restore target (R5.1).
NAMESPACES="pg-ha pg-restore"
san="DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"
for ns in $NAMESPACES; do
  san="$san,DNS:*.pg-headless.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:*.pg-headless.$ns.svc"
  san="$san,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc"
done

if [ -s "$D/ca.key" ] && [ -s "$D/ca.crt" ]; then log "OK    CA exists, kept"
elif [ -e "$D/ca.key" ] || [ -e "$D/ca.crt" ]; then die "partial CA in $D, refusing to overwrite"
else
  openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out "$D/ca.key"
  openssl req -x509 -new -sha256 -key "$D/ca.key" -days 3650 -subj "/CN=[REDACTED-GCP-PROJECT] private CA" \
    -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE,pathlen:0" \
    -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" -out "$D/ca.crt"
  log "NEW   CA created"
fi

issue() { # name CN extendedKeyUsage SAN(optional)
  local n=$1 cn=$2 eku=$3 s=${4:-} ext
  if [ -s "$D/$n.key" ] && [ -s "$D/$n.crt" ]; then log "OK    $n exists, kept"; return; fi
  [ ! -e "$D/$n.key" ] && [ ! -e "$D/$n.crt" ] || die "partial $n in $D, refusing to overwrite"
  ext=$(mktemp)
  { echo "basicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE"; echo "keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature"
    echo "extendedKeyUsage=$eku"; [ -z "$s" ] || echo "subjectAltName=$s"; } > "$ext"
  openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out "$D/$n.key.tmp"
  openssl req -new -sha256 -key "$D/$n.key.tmp" -subj "/CN=$cn" |
    openssl x509 -req -sha256 -CA "$D/ca.crt" -CAkey "$D/ca.key" -CAcreateserial -days 825 \
      -extfile "$ext" -out "$D/$n.crt" 2>/dev/null
  mv "$D/$n.key.tmp" "$D/$n.key"; rm -f "$ext"
  log "NEW   $n issued (CN=$cn)"
}

issue postgres-server pg-ha-postgres serverAuth "$san"
issue pgbackrest-server pg-ha-pgbackrest serverAuth "$san"
# pgBackRest's TLS server authorises callers by client-certificate CN.
issue pgbackrest-client pgbackrest-client clientAuth
chmod 600 "$D"/*
for n in postgres-server pgbackrest-server pgbackrest-client; do
  openssl verify -CAfile "$D/ca.crt" "$D/$n.crt" >/dev/null || die "$n does not verify against the CA"
done
log "Certs verified against the CA (in ./secrets/tls)"

KUBECTL_SHA256=c49a28f1f4efc4d475ed05f47f2ce8e563bf7bef69ed77fe1b924ea6d83b6327
K3D_VERSION=v5.9.0
K3D_SHA256=06d8f25bc3a971c4eb29e0ff08429b180402db0f4dec838c9eac427e296800a0

# Kubernetes
K3S_IMAGE=rancher/k3s:v1.35.10-k3s1@sha256:…

# PostgreSQL image inputs (PGDG packages for Debian trixie)

POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE=postgres:17.12-trixie@sha256:…
PATRONI_DEB_VERSION=4.1.5-2.pgdg13+1
PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION=2.60.1-1.pgdg13+1

# Object storage and its bootstrap Job
GARAGE_IMAGE=dxflrs/garage:v2.5.0@sha256:…
CURL_IMAGE=curlimages/curl:8.23.0@sha256:…

# Monitoring

ALERTMANAGER_IMAGE=prom/alertmanager:v0.34.2@sha256:…
POSTGRES_EXPORTER_IMAGE=quay.io/prometheuscommunity/postgres-exporter:v0.20.1@sha256:…
KUBE_STATE_METRICS_IMAGE=registry.k8s.io/kube-state-metrics/kube-state-metrics:v2.20.0@sha256:…

ARG POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE
FROM ${POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE}

ARG PATRONI_DEB_VERSION
ARG PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION

USER root
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        "patroni=${PATRONI_DEB_VERSION}" "pgbackrest=${PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION}"; \

kind: Simple
metadata:

servers: 1
agents: 3
kubeAPI:
  hostIP: 127.0.0.1
  hostPort: "6550"
options:

    timeout: 180s
    disableLoadbalancer: true   # one server, so a load balancer adds nothing

    extraArgs:

      - arg: --kube-controller-manager-arg=node-monitor-grace-period=20s
        nodeFilters: [server:*]
      - arg: --node-taint=node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane=true:NoSchedule

else k3d cluster create --config "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/k3d/cluster.yaml" --image "$K3S_IMAGE"; fi

kubectl get nodes -L pg-ha/role

  --build-arg "POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE=$POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE" \
  --build-arg "PATRONI_DEB_VERSION=$PATRONI_DEB_VERSION" \
  --build-arg "PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION=$PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION" \

docker run --rm --entrypoint sh "$PG_IMAGE" -c 'id -u; postgres --version; patroni --version; pgbackrest version'

#!/usr/bin/env bash

. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

kubectl get nodes -o wide -L pg-ha/role
log ""
docker stats --no-stream --format 'table {{.Name}}\t{{.CPUPerc}}\t{{.MemUsage}}' \
  $(docker ps -q --filter "label=k3d.cluster=$CLUSTER_NAME")
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One private CA plus Postgres and pgBackRest certs (ADR-009, ADR-012). Never overwrites.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

D="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"; mkdir -p "$D"; chmod 700 "$SECRETS_DIR" "$D"

  san="$san,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc"

elif [ -e "$D/ca.key" ] || [ -e "$D/ca.crt" ]; then die "partial CA in $D, refusing to overwrite"

  openssl ecparam -name prime256v1 -genkey -noout -out "$D/ca.key"
  openssl req -x509 -new -sha256 -key "$D/ca.key" -days 3650 -subj "/CN=[REDACTED-GCP-PROJECT] private CA" \

    openssl x509 -req -sha256 -CA "$D/ca.crt" -CAkey "$D/ca.key" -CAcreateserial -days 825 \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deletes only this project's named cluster. ./secrets is preserved.

rm -f "$KUBECONFIG"
log "./secrets preserved."

=================== docs/decisions/ADR-001-cluster-topology.md
## Decision

Use **1 tainted server + 3 agents**. Postgres pods use required node affinity on `pg-ha/role=db`, required pod anti-affinity on hostname, and a topology spread constraint with `maxSkew: 1` and `DoNotSchedule`. Infrastructure workloads tolerate the taint and run on the server.

## Consequences

- Any Postgres node can be stopped while object storage and monitoring keep running.
- The API server is a single point of failure, documented in ADR-002 and known limitations.
- All nodes share one VM, kernel and disk, so this simulates node failure rather than proving zone independence.

## R-IDs covered
=================== docs/decisions/ADR-002-ha-manager-leader-election.md
## Decision

Use **Patroni 4.1.5 with `use_endpoints: true`** and **`failsafe_mode` off**.

Kubernetes v1.35.10, the base of the pinned k3s release, still defines the v1 Endpoints paths in its OpenAPI spec and marks the API as deprecated since v1.33. This was verified from source, and a runtime check is part of spike S4.

## API-server outage

With `failsafe_mode` off, a primary that cannot renew its lock **demotes itself**. Replicas cannot take the lock either. Writes stop until the API returns, reads continue, and no split-brain or data loss occurs.

This is the right trade-off here because the API server is a known single point of failure and safety outranks write availability. Failsafe mode would keep writes running only while all members can confirm the primary, which adds a further mode to test and defend.

## Consequences

- An API-server outage is a full write outage, documented as a known limitation.
- A future Kubernetes release could remove Endpoints, so upgrades must recheck this decision.
- A multi-server control plane would be the production fix.

## R-IDs covered
=================== docs/decisions/ADR-003-postgres-image.md
## Decision

Build `FROM` the digest-pinned `postgres:17.12-trixie`, and install the exact PGDG `patroni` and `pgbackrest` versions from `versions.env`. Run as UID 999, bypassing the root entrypoint. Build with `docker build` and load with `k3d image import`.

## Consequences

- The Dockerfile stays short enough to explain line by line.
- Transitive Debian packages are not individually pinned, which is a documented reproducibility limit.
- PGDATA must be a subdirectory of the volume so Patroni can create it with mode 0700. Spike S3 proves this.
- The estimated compressed size of 200–230 MiB is measured at build time.

## R-IDs covered
=================== docs/decisions/ADR-004-replication-mode.md
## Decision

Use **non-strict `synchronous_mode: true` with one synchronous standby**.

## Stated RPO

- **RPO is 0 for any single failure.**
- With non-strict `synchronous_mode`, a **double replica failure falls back to asynchronous operation**. Writes continue without replica protection, choosing availability over durability.
- If the primary and its synchronous standby fail **at the same time**, the remaining replica may be promoted without the latest commits.

## Consequences

- One lost replica does not stop writes.
- A backend cancelled while waiting for sync confirmation can expose a transaction that was not replicated.
- A client can opt out with `SET synchronous_commit = local`, so the RPO applies to the default commit setting.
- `T:rpo` tests the claim against acknowledged commits.

## R-IDs covered
=================== docs/decisions/ADR-005-slots-disk-protection.md
## Decision

Use `use_slots: true`, with `max_wal_size=512MB`, `max_slot_wal_keep_size=1GB`, 5 GiB PVCs and `archive-push-queue-max=2GiB`. Alert on low safe WAL size and on lost slots.

## Consequences

- WAL held for slots has a hard limit, independent of PVC enforcement.
- A replica past the cap must recover through `restore_command`. `T:slot-bound` proves this.
- During a long object-storage outage, the archive queue limit drops WAL rather than filling the disk. That creates a PITR gap, which must alert.

## R-IDs covered
=================== docs/decisions/ADR-006-fencing-timing.md
## Decision

- Use `ttl=20`, `loop_wait=3`, `retry_timeout=5` and `primary_start_timeout=0`.
- Fence through lock-based demotion plus synchronous replication, with **no watchdog**.
- **"Accepts writes" means acknowledged commits.** A commit that blocks and never returns success is not an accepted write.
- Measure RTO per failure mode and **report the real numbers**. The 26–28 s worst case is only an estimate.
- **Do not tune timeouts into unsafe territory to hit the target.** If a mode exceeds 30 s with safe settings, record the miss and explain it.

## Split-brain timing argument

With `loop_wait=3`, `retry_timeout=5` and `ttl=20`:

```text
loop_wait + 2 × retry_timeout = 3 + (2 × 5) = 13 s  <  ttl = 20 s
```

An isolated primary demotes within **13 s** of its last successful lock renewal, before its leader key can expire at **20 s**. No other member can therefore acquire the lock while the old primary may still accept writes.

What this rests on, checked against Patroni `v4.1.5` source:

- **Expiry cannot start early.** Each replica times the TTL from when it last *observed* the leader record change, using its own clock (`dcs/kubernetes.py`). Observation happens at or after the renewal, so the earliest possible expiry is renewal + 20 s, and no clock synchronisation is needed.
- **13 s bounds when demotion is issued, not when Postgres has stopped.** On a failed renewal Patroni calls `demote('immediate-nolock')` (`ha.py`), which stops Postgres in `immediate` mode asynchronously. That stop must finish inside the remaining **7 s margin**. This is an **[Assumption]** until `T:split-brain` measures it.
- **The argument needs a running Patroni.** A frozen Patroni never issues the demotion, so the inequality does not protect that case. Synchronous replication is the backstop: once the standbys follow the new leader, the old primary's commits block and are never acknowledged.

### What `T:split-brain` must show

The fault is `docker network disconnect` on the primary's agent, with a writer running against the old primary throughout. Timestamps are in UTC. The test passes only if all of these hold, in each of its runs:

1. **Demotion before expiry:** the old primary stops acknowledging commits no later than 20 s after its last successful renewal. The report states the measured time against the 13 s bound and the 20 s TTL.
2. **No overlap:** the last commit acknowledged by the old primary is earlier than the new primary's first acknowledged commit.
3. **One lock holder:** the leader key names exactly one member at every sample, and the new leader acquires it only after the old key expired.
4. **No lost acknowledged writes:** every commit acknowledged to the client is present on the new primary after failover (RPO 0).
5. **Frozen-Patroni case:** with Patroni stopped by `SIGSTOP` on the primary and Postgres still running, commits on the old primary block and none is acknowledged after the standbys leave it.

## Consequences

- A frozen Patroni cannot demote itself, but sync replication should stop its commits being acknowledged. `T:split-brain` must prove this.
- Tight timing can cause unnecessary failovers if the API is slow.
- A production deployment on real nodes should add a hardware or software watchdog.

## R-IDs covered
=================== docs/decisions/ADR-007-client-endpoints.md
## Decision

Use a selector-less **`pg-rw`** whose Endpoints Patroni writes, and **`pg-ro`** selecting ready pods with `role=replica`. Set `node-monitor-grace-period=20s`. Do **not** add a connection pooler.

## Consequences

- The primary endpoint follows the leader lock directly.
- Routing depends on EndpointSlice mirroring, whose latency is measured in spike S4.
- Clients need short connect timeouts and TCP keepalives to reconnect quickly.
- Applications with many short connections would need a pooler in production.

## R-IDs covered
=================== docs/decisions/ADR-008-old-primary-rejoin.md
## Decision

Set `use_pg_rewind: true` and `remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true`. Initialise with data checksums, keep `wal_log_hints=on`, and use a dedicated rewind role.

## Consequences

- The fallback deletes that member's diverged data directory, which is safe only because the current primary remains the source of truth.
- `restore_command` lets rewind fetch older WAL from the archive.
- Checksums also detect page corruption, at a small write cost.

## R-IDs covered

content.content:
## Target architecture

A k3d cluster runs one tainted server and three agents on a single VM. Three Postgres 17 pods in a StatefulSet run one per agent, each with Patroni managing Postgres and using the Kubernetes API as its leader lock. Patroni writes the leader's address directly into the `pg-rw` Endpoints, while `pg-ro` selects healthy replicas by label. Replication is synchronous to one standby through Patroni, with slots bounded by `max_slot_wal_keep_size`. pgBackRest archives encrypted WAL continuously to an in-cluster Garage object store, and CronJobs run base backups and a scratch restore test. Prometheus, Alertmanager and small exporters run from our own manifests on the server node, so they survive agent failures. One `make up` builds and deploys everything from a single pinned versions file.

```text
                        Clients (one connection string each)
                             |                      |
                     pg-rw Service            pg-ro Service
                 (Patroni-managed Endpoints) (selector: role=replica)
                             |                      |
    +------------------------v----------------------v------------------+
    | k3d cluster on one VM                                            |
    |                                                                  |
    |  agent-0            agent-1             agent-2                  |
    | +------------+     +------------+      +------------+            |
    | | pg-0       |====>| pg-1       |      | pg-2       |            |
    | | PRIMARY    | sync| SYNC       |      | REPLICA    |            |
    | | Patroni    |=====|============|=====>| Patroni    |            |
    | | pgBackRest |async| pgBackRest |      | pgBackRest |            |
    | | exporter   |     | exporter   |      | exporter   |            |
    | +-----+------+     +------+-----+      +-----+------+            |
    |       |  leader lock      |                  |                   |
    |       +-------------------+------------------+                   |
    |                           v                                      |
    |  server (tainted, runs infrastructure only)                      |
    | +--------------------------------------------------------------+ |
    | | Kubernetes API | Garage <- WAL + backups | Prometheus        | |
    | | Backup and restore-test CronJobs         | Alertmanager      | |
    | +--------------------------------------------------------------+ |
    +------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

## Decision

Use **raw manifests with Kustomize overlays** and a **Makefile**. `versions.env` is the single version source. `make tools` installs checksum-verified `kubectl` and `k3d` into a git-ignored `./bin`, leaving system tools unchanged.

Target groups: `preflight`, `tools`, `certs`, `image`, `up`, `down`, `status`, `test-*`, `failover-*`, `backup`, `restore`, `switchover` and `upgrade-minor`.

## Consequences

- A reviewer can read exactly what is deployed.
- Kustomize offers limited parameterisation, so restore differences live in an overlay.
- `make down` must delete only this project's named cluster.

## R-IDs covered
## O7. Client endpoints and pooling

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Patroni-managed `pg-rw` + selector-based `pg-ro`** | `pg-rw` has no selector and Patroni writes its Endpoints. `pg-ro` selects `role=replica` and ready pods | Primary routing changes atomically with leadership, no extra hop | Relies on EndpointSlice mirroring **[Assumption: latency measured in spike S4]** | Meets R2.1–R2.4, R3.7 | 1.5 h |
| B. Label selectors for both | Patroni patches `role` labels and Services follow | Standard Kubernetes pattern | A dead node's pod can remain for up to 50 s | Risks R2.1, R3.2, R3.7 | 1 h |
| C. HAProxy in front | Proxy health-checks Patroni REST | Fast routing, common on VMs | Another HA component to run and explain | Meets R2.x. Risks D7 | 4 h |

- **Read endpoint on node loss:** set `node-monitor-grace-period=20s` through k3s so a dead replica leaves `pg-ro` sooner (R2.4).
- **Clients:** the test probe must set a short `connect_timeout` and TCP keepalives. Otherwise, a connection to a dead pod hangs and inflates the measured RTO.

**Pooling options**

| Option | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. No pooler** | Fewer failure modes, direct RTO measurement | No connection multiplexing | Meets R2.5 (omission justified) | 0 h |
| B. PgBouncer [NICE] | Protects Postgres from connection storms | Extra hop, more auth config, must be HA itself | Optional | 3 h |

**Recommendation: A and no pooler.** Strongest reason: the primary endpoint cannot point at a stale pod after failover, and the brief does not require pooling.

## O8. Old primary rejoin

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. `pg_rewind`, with re-clone fallback** | `use_pg_rewind: true`, and `remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true` | Fast normal path, and still recovers automatically when rewind fails | Fallback deletes that member's data dir | Meets R3.6 | 1.5 h |
| B. Always re-clone | Remove data and copy from primary | Simple logic | Slower, more I/O on a shared disk | Meets R3.6 | 1 h |
| C. `pg_rewind` only | No fallback | No automatic deletion | Can leave a member stuck | Risks R3.6 | 1 h |

**Requirements:**

- `pg_rewind` needs **`wal_log_hints=on` or data checksums**. **[Verified]**
- Enable **both**: initialise with `--data-checksums`, which also detects corruption, and keep `wal_log_hints=on`, which Patroni sets. **[Verified]**
- Create a dedicated rewind role with only the required function privileges.
- `restore_command` lets rewind fetch older WAL from the archive when needed.

**Recommendation: A.** Strongest reason: it gives the fast path while guaranteeing the old primary always returns with no human step.


| Tool | Version | Status |
|---|---|---|
| docker | 29.10.0 (client and server) | OK, user is in the `docker` group |
| kubectl | v1.37.2 (Kustomize v5.8.1) | **Skew against k3s default** |
| k3d | v5.9.0 (default k3s v1.35.5-k3s1) | OK |
| kind | Not installed | Not needed if we use k3d |
| helm | v3.22.1 | Installed, not needed under decision D2 |
| make | 4.3 | OK |
| git | 2.43.0 | OK |
| jq | 1.7 | OK |

Not requested but likely useful, and all missing: `yq`, `psql`, `mc`, `shellcheck`, `kubeconform`. Whether we need them is a Phase 1 decision.

## Host readiness

| Check | Result | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| inotify instances / watches | 512 / 524288 | OK for a multi-node cluster |
| `vm.max_map_count` | 1048576 | OK |
| Open file limit | 1048576 | OK |
| Kernel modules | `overlay`, `ip_tables`, `xt_conntrack` loaded; `nf_conntrack` built in; `br_netfilter`, `iptable_nat` available | OK |
| iptables | 1.8.10 (nf_tables) | OK |
| Transparent huge pages | `madvise` | OK for Postgres |

toolUseResult.stdout:
## Target architecture

A k3d cluster runs one tainted server and three agents on a single VM. Three Postgres 17 pods in a StatefulSet run one per agent, each with Patroni managing Postgres and using the Kubernetes API as its leader lock. Patroni writes the leader's address directly into the `pg-rw` Endpoints, while `pg-ro` selects healthy replicas by label. Replication is synchronous to one standby through Patroni, with slots bounded by `max_slot_wal_keep_size`. pgBackRest archives encrypted WAL continuously to an in-cluster Garage object store, and CronJobs run base backups and a scratch restore test. Prometheus, Alertmanager and small exporters run from our own manifests on the server node, so they survive agent failures. One `make up` builds and deploys everything from a single pinned versions file.

```text
                        Clients (one connection string each)
                             |                      |
                     pg-rw Service            pg-ro Service
                 (Patroni-managed Endpoints) (selector: role=replica)
                             |                      |
    +------------------------v----------------------v------------------+
    | k3d cluster on one VM                                            |
    |                                                                  |
    |  agent-0            agent-1             agent-2                  |
    | +------------+     +------------+      +------------+            |
    | | pg-0       |====>| pg-1       |      | pg-2       |            |
    | | PRIMARY    | sync| SYNC       |      | REPLICA    |            |
    | | Patroni    |=====|============|=====>| Patroni    |            |
    | | pgBackRest |async| pgBackRest |      | pgBackRest |            |
    | | exporter   |     | exporter   |      | exporter   |            |
    | +-----+------+     +------+-----+      +-----+------+            |
    |       |  leader lock      |                  |                   |
    |       +-------------------+------------------+                   |
    |                           v                                      |
    |  server (tainted, runs infrastructure only)                      |
    | +--------------------------------------------------------------+ |
    | | Kubernetes API | Garage <- WAL + backups | Prometheus        | |
    | | Backup and restore-test CronJobs         | Alertmanager      | |
    | +--------------------------------------------------------------+ |
    +------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

---

## Decision

Use **raw manifests with Kustomize overlays** and a **Makefile**. `versions.env` is the single version source. `make tools` installs checksum-verified `kubectl` and `k3d` into a git-ignored `./bin`, leaving system tools unchanged.

Target groups: `preflight`, `tools`, `certs`, `image`, `up`, `down`, `status`, `test-*`, `failover-*`, `backup`, `restore`, `switchover` and `upgrade-minor`.

## Consequences

- A reviewer can read exactly what is deployed.
- Kustomize offers limited parameterisation, so restore differences live in an overlay.
- `make down` must delete only this project's named cluster.

## R-IDs covered
## O7. Client endpoints and pooling

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Patroni-managed `pg-rw` + selector-based `pg-ro`** | `pg-rw` has no selector and Patroni writes its Endpoints. `pg-ro` selects `role=replica` and ready pods | Primary routing changes atomically with leadership, no extra hop | Relies on EndpointSlice mirroring **[Assumption: latency measured in spike S4]** | Meets R2.1–R2.4, R3.7 | 1.5 h |
| B. Label selectors for both | Patroni patches `role` labels and Services follow | Standard Kubernetes pattern | A dead node's pod can remain for up to 50 s | Risks R2.1, R3.2, R3.7 | 1 h |
| C. HAProxy in front | Proxy health-checks Patroni REST | Fast routing, common on VMs | Another HA component to run and explain | Meets R2.x. Risks D7 | 4 h |

- **Read endpoint on node loss:** set `node-monitor-grace-period=20s` through k3s so a dead replica leaves `pg-ro` sooner (R2.4).
- **Clients:** the test probe must set a short `connect_timeout` and TCP keepalives. Otherwise, a connection to a dead pod hangs and inflates the measured RTO.

**Pooling options**

| Option | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. No pooler** | Fewer failure modes, direct RTO measurement | No connection multiplexing | Meets R2.5 (omission justified) | 0 h |
| B. PgBouncer [NICE] | Protects Postgres from connection storms | Extra hop, more auth config, must be HA itself | Optional | 3 h |

**Recommendation: A and no pooler.** Strongest reason: the primary endpoint cannot point at a stale pod after failover, and the brief does not require pooling.

## O8. Old primary rejoin

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. `pg_rewind`, with re-clone fallback** | `use_pg_rewind: true`, and `remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true` | Fast normal path, and still recovers automatically when rewind fails | Fallback deletes that member's data dir | Meets R3.6 | 1.5 h |
| B. Always re-clone | Remove data and copy from primary | Simple logic | Slower, more I/O on a shared disk | Meets R3.6 | 1 h |
| C. `pg_rewind` only | No fallback | No automatic deletion | Can leave a member stuck | Risks R3.6 | 1 h |

**Requirements:**

- `pg_rewind` needs **`wal_log_hints=on` or data checksums**. **[Verified]**
- Enable **both**: initialise with `--data-checksums`, which also detects corruption, and keep `wal_log_hints=on`, which Patroni sets. **[Verified]**
- Create a dedicated rewind role with only the required function privileges.
- `restore_command` lets rewind fetch older WAL from the archive when needed.

**Recommendation: A.** Strongest reason: it gives the fast path while guaranteeing the old primary always returns with no human step.

    verbs: [get, list, watch, create, update, patch, delete]

metadata: {name: pg-patroni}

# Patroni L1 base config. Per-pod values (name, addresses, passwords) come from environment variables.
# L3 adds archive_mode, archive_command, restore_command and create_replica_methods in a later file
# (20-archive.yml), which Patroni merges over this one.
scope: pg-rw            # Patroni names the leader Endpoints after the scope, so this is the pg-rw Service
restapi:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:8008
kubernetes:             # ADR-002
  use_endpoints: true
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
  role_label: role
  ports: [{name: postgresql, port: 5432}]
bootstrap:
  dcs:
    ttl: 20             # ADR-006: loop_wait + 2 x retry_timeout = 13 s < ttl
    loop_wait: 3
    retry_timeout: 5
    primary_start_timeout: 0
    maximum_lag_on_failover: 1048576
    synchronous_mode: true          # ADR-004: non-strict, one synchronous standby
    synchronous_mode_strict: false
    synchronous_node_count: 1
    postgresql:
      use_pg_rewind: true           # ADR-008
      use_slots: true               # ADR-005
      parameters:
        wal_level: replica
        hot_standby: "on"
        wal_log_hints: "on"         # ADR-008, in addition to data checksums
        max_wal_size: 512MB         # ADR-005
        max_slot_wal_keep_size: 1GB # ADR-005: hard cap on WAL held for slots
        max_wal_senders: 10
        max_replication_slots: 10
        max_connections: 100
        shared_buffers: 128MB
        password_encryption: scram-sha-256
  initdb:
    - data-checksums
    - encoding: UTF8
  post_bootstrap: /etc/patroni/scripts/post-bootstrap.sh
postgresql:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:5432
  data_dir: /data/pgdata            # a subdirectory of the volume, created 0700 (S3)
  bin_dir: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
  pgpass: /tmp/pgpass
  use_unix_socket: true
  remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true   # ADR-008: re-clone if pg_rewind fails

    unix_socket_directories: /var/run/postgresql

    ssl: "on"
    ssl_cert_file: /etc/pg-tls/tls.crt
    ssl_key_file: /etc/pg-tls/tls.key
    ssl_ca_file: /etc/pg-tls/ca.crt
  pg_hba:
    - local all all peer
    - host replication replicator 10.42.0.0/16 scram-sha-256
    - host all all 10.42.0.0/16 scram-sha-256
    - host all all 127.0.0.1/32 scram-sha-256
EOF
cat > deploy/pg/scripts/post-bootstrap.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Patroni post_bootstrap: runs once, on the first primary after initdb. $1 is a superuser connection URL.
# Patroni itself creates the superuser, replicator and rewind roles. This creates the others.
# Passwords are read inside psql with \getenv, so they never appear on a command line or in output,
# and failed statements are kept out of the server log.
set -eu
psql "$1" -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
\set VERBOSITY terse
SET log_min_error_statement = panic;
SET log_statement = none;
\getenv monitor_pw PG_MONITOR_PASSWORD
\getenv backup_pw PG_BACKUP_PASSWORD
\getenv app_pw PG_APP_PASSWORD
\getenv app_ro_pw PG_APP_RO_PASSWORD
CREATE ROLE monitor LOGIN PASSWORD :'monitor_pw' IN ROLE pg_monitor;
-- pgBackRest privileges are finalised in L3.
CREATE ROLE backup LOGIN PASSWORD :'backup_pw' IN ROLE pg_read_all_settings, pg_checkpoint;
CREATE ROLE app LOGIN PASSWORD :'app_pw';
CREATE ROLE app_ro LOGIN PASSWORD :'app_ro_pw' IN ROLE pg_read_all_data;
CREATE DATABASE app OWNER app;
SQL
echo "post-bootstrap: roles monitor, backup, app, app_ro and database app created"
EOF

cat >> scripts/lib.sh <<'EOF'

# L1: Postgres cluster
PG_NS=pg-ha
PG_STS=pg
# Patroni's /cluster view, read through the API server's pod proxy, so no kubectl exec is needed (D4).
patroni_cluster() {
  local i out
  for i in 0 1 2; do
    out=$(kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/namespaces/$PG_NS/pods/$PG_STS-$i:8008/proxy/cluster" 2>/dev/null) && { printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0; }
  done
  return 1
}
# Succeeds when Patroni reports 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas and 1 sync standby.
patroni_healthy() {
  patroni_cluster | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role == "leader" and .state == "running")] | length == 1' >/dev/null &&
  patroni_cluster | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role != "leader" and .state == "streaming")] | length == 2' >/dev/null &&
  patroni_cluster | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role == "sync_standby")] | length == 1' >/dev/null
}
EOF
cat > scripts/deploy.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploys the Patroni cluster (L1) and waits until it is healthy. Idempotent, and never prints a secret.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || die "cluster $CLUSTER_NAME not found, run: make cluster"
C="$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"; T="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"
for f in "$C"/pg-{postgres,replicator,rewind,monitor,backup,app,app_ro}-password "$T"/{ca.crt,postgres-server.crt,postgres-server.key}; do
  [ -s "$f" ] || die "missing $f, run: make certs secrets"
done

kubectl apply -f "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg/namespace.yaml" >/dev/null
# Server-side apply keeps secret values out of the last-applied annotation.
secret() { kubectl -n "$PG_NS" create secret generic "$@" --dry-run=client -o yaml |
  kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-deploy --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null; }
secret pg-credentials $(for r in postgres replicator rewind monitor backup app app_ro; do printf -- '--from-file=%s ' "$C/pg-$r-password"; done)
secret pg-tls --from-file=tls.crt="$T/postgres-server.crt" --from-file=tls.key="$T/postgres-server.key" --from-file=ca.crt="$T/ca.crt"
kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg" | sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|" | kubectl apply -f -

kubectl -n "$PG_NS" rollout status "statefulset/$PG_STS" --timeout=300s
end=$((SECONDS + ${PG_WAIT:-180}))
until patroni_healthy; do
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "\(.name) \(.role) \(.state)"' || true; die "Patroni not healthy after ${PG_WAIT:-180} s"; }
  sleep 2
done
log "Patroni healthy: 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas, 1 sync standby"
EOF
cat > scripts/status.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shows nodes, resource use and, once deployed, Patroni members. Read-only, and uses no kubectl exec (D4).
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || { log "Cluster $CLUSTER_NAME is not running."; exit 0; }
kubectl get nodes -o wide -L pg-ha/role
log ""
docker stats --no-stream --format 'table {{.Name}}\t{{.CPUPerc}}\t{{.MemUsage}}' \
  $(docker ps -q --filter "label=k3d.cluster=$CLUSTER_NAME")
kubectl get ns "$PG_NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
log ""
if J=$(patroni_cluster); then
  log "Patroni cluster $(jq -r '.scope // "pg-rw"' <<<"$J") (lag in bytes behind the leader, from Patroni's REST API)"
  { echo "MEMBER ROLE STATE TIMELINE LAG_BYTES NODE"
    for n in $(jq -r '.members[].name' <<<"$J"); do
      node=$(kubectl -n "$PG_NS" get pod "$n" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}' 2>/dev/null || echo -)
      jq -r --arg n "$n" --arg node "$node" '.members[] | select(.name == $n) |
        "\(.name) \(.role) \(.state) \(.timeline // "-") \(if .role == "leader" then "-" else (.lag // "?") end) \($node)"' <<<"$J"
    done; } | column -t
  log "Sync standby: $(jq -r '[.members[] | select(.role == "sync_standby") | .name] | join(", ") | if . == "" then "none" else . end' <<<"$J")"
  log "pg-rw ->     $(kubectl -n "$PG_NS" get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=pg-rw -o jsonpath='{.items[*].endpoints[*].addresses[*]}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
  log "pg-ro ->     $(kubectl -n "$PG_NS" get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=pg-ro -o jsonpath='{range .items[*].endpoints[?(@.conditions.ready==true)]}{.addresses[0]} {end}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
else
  log "Patroni REST API not reachable yet."; kubectl -n "$PG_NS" get pods -o wide
fi
EOF
cat > scripts/seed.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Loads a synthetic pgbench dataset through pg-rw from an in-cluster Job (no kubectl exec, D4).
# SEED_SCALE=10 gives about 150 MB. Re-running drops and reloads the pgbench tables.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
SCALE=${SEED_SCALE:-10}
[[ "$SCALE" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || die "SEED_SCALE must be a positive integer"
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" delete job pg-seed --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|; s|__SCALE__|$SCALE|" <<'YAML' | kubectl -n "$PG_NS" apply -f - >/dev/null
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: pg-seed}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
      - name: seed
        image: __PG_IMAGE__
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
        env:
        - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
        - {name: PGHOST, value: pg-rw.pg-ha.svc.cluster.local}
        - {name: PGUSER, value: app}
        - {name: PGDATABASE, value: app}
        - {name: PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT, value: "5"}
        - name: PGPASSWORD
          valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app-password}}
        command: [sh, -ec]
        args:
        - |
          echo "seed: pgbench -i -s __SCALE__ through $PGHOST"
          pgbench -i -s __SCALE__ -q --no-vacuum
          psql -XAtc "vacuum analyze"
          psql -XAtc "select 'server=' || inet_server_addr() || ' in_recovery=' || pg_is_in_recovery() || ' ssl=' || (select ssl from pg_stat_ssl where pid = pg_backend_pid())"
          psql -XAtc "select 'database_size=' || pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size('app')) || ' accounts=' || (select count(*) from pgbench_accounts)"
        volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
      volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]
YAML
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" wait --for=condition=complete job/pg-seed --timeout="${SEED_TIMEOUT:-600}s" >/dev/null || {
  kubectl -n "$PG_NS" logs job/pg-seed --tail=20 || true; die "seed Job did not complete"; }
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" logs job/pg-seed | grep -vE '^[0-9]+ of [0-9]+ tuples'
EOF
chmod +x scripts/deploy.sh scripts/seed.sh scripts/status.sh
python3 -I - <<'E'
p='Makefile'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""        spike-s1 spike-s2 spike-s3 spike-s4 spikes""","""        deploy seed test-replication spike-s1 spike-s2 spike-s3 spike-s4 spikes""")
s=s.replace("""up: preflight tools certs secrets cluster image ## Bootstrap everything built so far""","""up: preflight tools certs secrets cluster image deploy ## Bootstrap everything built so far""")
s=s.replace("""status: ## Show cluster nodes and resource use""","""deploy: ## Deploy the Patroni cluster and wait until healthy
	@scripts/deploy.sh

seed: ## Load a synthetic ~150 MB pgbench dataset through pg-rw (SEED_SCALE=10)
	@scripts/seed.sh

test-replication: ## L1 gate: topology, sync standby, endpoints, lag, slots, replica rejoin
	@tests/test-replication.sh

status: ## Show nodes, resource use, Patroni members, lag and the sync standby""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
bash -n scripts/deploy.sh scripts/seed.sh scripts/status.sh scripts/lib.sh && make help | grep -E 'deploy|seed|test-rep|status|^up'

cat > tests/test-replication.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L1 gate (T:topology, T:replication, T:endpoints): writes docs/evidence/L1-replication.md with PASS/FAIL per check.
#
# kubectl exec (D4): this committed test runs psql inside its own short-lived client pod, pg-test-client,
# to reach pg-rw, pg-ro and each member's DNS name from inside the cluster. It never execs into a
# Postgres pod. Patroni state is read through the API server's pod proxy. The only fault injected is
# deleting one replica pod. Passwords come from the pg-credentials Secret and are never printed.
. "$(dirname "$0")/../scripts/spikes/lib.sh"
NS=$PG_NS; CLIENT=pg-test-client
EV_FILE="$EV_DIR/L1-replication.md"
BODY=$(mktemp); CHECKS=$(mktemp); FAILS=0; T0=$SECONDS; STARTED=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
cleanup() { kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$CLIENT" --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

finish() {
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  { printf '# L1: replication, endpoints and rejoin\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **Covers:** R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R1.7 (bytes and seconds), R2.1, R2.2, R7.4 (placement), ADR-004 sync standby, ADR-005 slot cap\n'
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make test-replication`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))"
    printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
    printf -- '- **kubectl exec:** psql runs only in the test'"'"'s own client pod `%s`, never in a Postgres pod (D4)\n' "$CLIENT"
    printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_FILE"
  log "RESULT L1: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L1-replication.md"
  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}

# q HOST USER SQL: one psql call from the client pod. The password is chosen inside the pod from its env.
q() {
  kubectl -n "$NS" exec "$CLIENT" -- sh -c '
    case "$2" in app) PGPASSWORD=$APP_PW ;; monitor) PGPASSWORD=$MON_PW ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac; export PGPASSWORD
    exec psql "host=$1 user=$2 dbname=app connect_timeout=5" -XAtq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -F " " -c "$3"' sh "$1" "$2" "$3"
}
RW=pg-rw.$NS.svc.cluster.local; RO=pg-ro.$NS.svc.cluster.local
member() { echo "$1.pg-headless.$NS.svc.cluster.local"; }
cluster_json() { patroni_cluster; }
leader() { cluster_json | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .name'; }
pod_ip() { kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}'; }

kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "namespace $NS not found, run: make up"
patroni_healthy || die "Patroni is not healthy, see: make status"

section "Setup: test client pod (our image, Pod Security restricted)"
kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$CLIENT" --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|" <<'YAML' | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - >/dev/null
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: pg-test-client, labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg-test-client}}
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0
  securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
  containers:
  - name: client
    image: __PG_IMAGE__
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    command: [sleep, "1800"]
    securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
    env:
    - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
    - name: APP_PW
      valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app-password}}
    - name: MON_PW
      valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-monitor-password}}
    volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
  volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]
YAML
kubectl -n "$NS" wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$CLIENT" --timeout=60s >/dev/null || die "client pod not ready"

section "Topology (T:topology)"
run "patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | \"\(.name) role=\(.role) state=\(.state) timeline=\(.timeline) lag=\(.lag // \"-\")\"'"
run "kubectl -n $NS get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=pg -o custom-columns=POD:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName,IP:.status.podIP,ROLE:.metadata.labels.role,READY:.status.containerStatuses[0].ready"
J=$(cluster_json); L=$(leader); LIP=$(pod_ip "$L")
REPLICAS=$(jq -r '.members[] | select(.role != "leader") | .name' <<<"$J" | tr '\n' ' ')
check "Patroni: exactly 1 leader" test "$(jq '[.members[] | select(.role == "leader" and .state == "running")] | length' <<<"$J")" = 1
check "Patroni: exactly 2 streaming replicas" test "$(jq '[.members[] | select(.role != "leader" and .state == "streaming")] | length' <<<"$J")" = 2
check "Patroni: exactly 1 synchronous standby" test "$(jq '[.members[] | select(.role == "sync_standby")] | length' <<<"$J")" = 1
nodes=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=pg -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName}{"\n"}{end}')
check "Placement: 3 members on 3 distinct agent nodes (R7.4)" bash -c "[ \$(sort -u <<<'$nodes' | grep -c agent) = 3 ]"
for m in $L $REPLICAS; do
  echo "$m: $(q "$(member "$m")" monitor "select 'version_num=' || current_setting('server_version_num') || ' in_recovery=' || pg_is_in_recovery() || ' checksums=' || current_setting('data_checksums') || ' ssl=' || current_setting('ssl')")"
done > /tmp/l1-members.$$ 2>&1
run "cat /tmp/l1-members.$$"
check "Every member runs Postgres >= 15 (R1.1)" bash -c "[ \$(grep -cE 'version_num=(1[5-9]|[2-9][0-9])[0-9]{4}' /tmp/l1-members.$$) = 3 ]"
check "Exactly 1 member not in recovery, 2 in recovery (R1.2)" bash -c "[ \$(grep -c 'in_recovery=false' /tmp/l1-members.$$) = 1 ] && [ \$(grep -c 'in_recovery=true' /tmp/l1-members.$$) = 2 ]"
check "Data checksums and server TLS on every member" bash -c "[ \$(grep -c 'checksums=on ssl=on' /tmp/l1-members.$$) = 3 ]"
rm -f /tmp/l1-members.$$

section "Streaming and the synchronous standby (T:replication)"
REPL_SQL="select application_name, state, sync_state from pg_stat_replication order by application_name"
run "q $RW monitor \"$REPL_SQL\""
R=$(q "$RW" monitor "$REPL_SQL")
