#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L2 optional: Kubernetes API outage (ADR-002, failsafe_mode off). Stops the k3d server container for
# OUTAGE seconds (default 60), then starts it again. Expected: every member demotes, so writes stop;
# reads continue; no two members are primary at once; a leader is elected once the API returns.
#
# Observation does not use make status or the API during the outage. A Job on an agent node, started
# beforehand, asks each member by pod IP (cluster DNS runs on the server, so it is down too) every second
# whether it is in recovery, and tries one write on each. Its log is read after the API returns.
# Fault injection (D4): docker stop / docker start of the k3d server container. No exec is used.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
OUTAGE=${OUTAGE:-60}; [[ "$OUTAGE" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "OUTAGE must be seconds"
SERVER="k3d-$CLUSTER_NAME-server-0"; EV_FILE="$EV_DIR/L2/api-outage.md"; mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L2"
W=$(mktemp -d); STOPPED=0
cleanup() { [ $STOPPED = 0 ] || docker start "$SERVER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -rf "$W" "$BODY" "$CHECKS"; }
trap cleanup EXIT
api_up() { kubectl get --raw /readyz >/dev/null 2>&1; }

client_up
until primary_confirms; do sleep 1; done
L=$(leader); IPS=""; for m in pg-0 pg-1 pg-2; do IPS="$IPS $m=$(pod_ip "$m")"; done
RUN_ID="api-outage-$(date +%s)"; DURATION=$((OUTAGE + 150))
kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-api-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|; s|__IPS__|${IPS# }|; s|__RUN__|$RUN_ID|; s|__DURATION__|$DURATION|" <<'YAML' | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - >/dev/null
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: pg-api-probe}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: db}
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
      - name: probe
        image: __PG_IMAGE__
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
        env:
        - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
        - name: PGPASSWORD
          valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app-password}}
        command: [bash, -c]
        args:
        - |
          end=$(( $(date +%s) + __DURATION__ )); i=0
          while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$end" ]; do i=$((i+1))
            for kv in __IPS__; do ( m=${kv%%=*}; ip=${kv#*=}; c="host=$ip user=app dbname=app connect_timeout=2"
              r=$(timeout 3 psql "$c" -XAtqc "select pg_is_in_recovery()" 2>/dev/null) || r=x
              w=no; timeout 3 psql "$c" -XAtq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "insert into probe (run, seq, client_ts) values ('__RUN__', $i * 10 + ${m#pg-}, now())" >/dev/null 2>&1 && w=yes
              echo "R $i $(date +%s.%N) $m ${r:-x} $w" ) & done
            sleep 1
          done; wait; echo DONE
        volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
      volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]
YAML
until [ "$(kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-api-probe 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^R')" -ge 15 ]; do sleep 1; done

section "API server outage"
T_STOP=$(now); docker stop "$SERVER" >/dev/null; STOPPED=1
note "Leader before: \`$L\`. Server container \`$SERVER\` stopped at $(iso "$T_STOP") UTC for ${OUTAGE} s. Members by IP: \`${IPS# }\`."
sleep "$OUTAGE"
T_START=$(now); docker start "$SERVER" >/dev/null; STOPPED=0
end=$((SECONDS + 240)); until api_up; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || die "API not back after 240 s"; sleep 1; done; T_API=$(now)
client_up   # the test client runs on the server node, so it did not survive the restart
T_HEALTHY=""; end=$((SECONDS + 240)); until primary_confirms 2>/dev/null; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || break; sleep 1; done
primary_confirms 2>/dev/null && T_HEALTHY=$(now); L2=$(leader)
end=$((SECONDS + DURATION + 60)); until kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-api-probe 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^DONE'; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || break; sleep 2; done
kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-api-probe > "$W/probe.txt"
kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-api-probe --wait=false >/dev/null

# Rounds are grouped by round number; times are each round's first sample.
awk '$1=="R"' "$W/probe.txt" | sort -k2,2n -k4,4 > "$W/r.txt"
LAST_PRIMARY_DURING=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b && $5=="f" {print $3}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -n | tail -1)
LAST_WRITE_DURING=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b && $6=="yes" {print $3}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -n | tail -1)
FIRST_WRITE_AFTER=$(awk -v b="$T_START" '$3>b && $6=="yes" {print $3}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -n | head -1)
OUT_ROUNDS=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b {print $2}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -u | wc -l)
READ_ROUNDS=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b && $5=="t" {print $2}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -u | wc -l)
NOPRIM_ROUNDS=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b {r[$2]=1} $3>a && $3<b && $5=="f" {p[$2]=1} END {n=0; for (k in r) if (!(k in p)) n++; print n}' "$W/r.txt")
MAXP=$(awk '$5=="f" {c[$2]++} END {m=0; for (k in c) if (c[k]>m) m=c[k]; print m}' "$W/r.txt")
WRITERS=$(awk '$6=="yes" {c[$2]++} END {m=0; for (k in c) if (c[k]>m) m=c[k]; print m}' "$W/r.txt")
note "During the outage: last sample with a primary +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_PRIMARY_DURING") s, last successful write +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_WRITE_DURING") s. $READ_ROUNDS of $OUT_ROUNDS rounds had a replica answering reads, and $NOPRIM_ROUNDS rounds had no primary at all. API back at +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_API") s, healthy with leader \`$L2\` at +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_HEALTHY") s, first write after restart +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$FIRST_WRITE_AFTER") s."
run "awk -v a=$T_STOP '\$3>a-3' $W/r.txt | awk '{printf \"%s round=%s %s in_recovery=%s write=%s\\n\", strftime(\"%H:%M:%S\", \$3, 1), \$2, \$4, \$5, \$6}' | awk 'NR%3==1 || /write=yes/' | head -40" || true
check "Every member demoted during the outage (writes stopped)" test -n "$LAST_WRITE_DURING" -a "$NOPRIM_ROUNDS" -gt 0
check "Demotion within 20 s of the outage starting (ttl)" awk -v d="$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_WRITE_DURING")" 'BEGIN{exit !(d != "n/a" && d <= 20)}'
check "Reads continued on replicas in every outage round" test "$READ_ROUNDS" = "$OUT_ROUNDS"
check "Never more than 1 primary in any round" test "$MAXP" -le 1
check "Never more than 1 member accepted a write in any round" test "$WRITERS" -le 1
check "A leader was elected and replication healthy after the API returned" test -n "$T_HEALTHY"

verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
{ printf '# L2 failure mode: api-outage\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$verdict"
  printf -- '- **Fault:** `docker stop` on the k3d server container for %s s, then `docker start`. With `failsafe_mode` off (ADR-002), every member should demote, so writes stop and reads continue. Observed by a Job on an agent node that queried each member by pod IP every second. Its log was read after the API returned, so nothing depends on `make status` or the API during the outage.\n' "$OUTAGE"
  printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make test-api-outage`\n- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "${K3S_IMAGE%%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
  printf '\n## Summary\n\n| Outage (s) | Last write during outage (s) | Rounds with no primary | Reads served | Max primaries in a round | API back (s) | Healthy again (s) | First write after (s) | Result |\n|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|\n'
  printf '| %s | +%s | %s of %s | %s of %s rounds | %s | +%s | +%s | +%s | %s |\n\n' "$OUTAGE" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_WRITE_DURING")" "$NOPRIM_ROUNDS" "$OUT_ROUNDS" "$READ_ROUNDS" "$OUT_ROUNDS" "$MAXP" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_API")" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_HEALTHY")" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$FIRST_WRITE_AFTER")" "$verdict"
  printf 'Times are seconds after the server was stopped. Write unavailability lasts the whole outage plus recovery, by design.\n\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'
  cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_FILE"
"$ROOT_DIR/tests/l2-summary.sh"
log "RESULT L2 api-outage: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L2/api-outage.md"
[ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# L2 optional: Kubernetes API outage (ADR-002, failsafe_mode off). Stops the k3d server container for
3	# OUTAGE seconds (default 60), then starts it again. Expected: every member demotes, so writes stop;
4	# reads continue; no two members are primary at once; a leader is elected once the API returns.
5	#
6	# Observation does not use make status or the API during the outage. A Job on an agent node, started
7	# beforehand, asks each member by pod IP (cluster DNS runs on the server, so it is down too) every second
8	# whether it is in recovery, and tries one write on each. Its log is read after the API returns.
9	# Fault injection (D4): docker stop / docker start of the k3d server container. No exec is used.
10	. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
11	OUTAGE=${OUTAGE:-60}; [[ "$OUTAGE" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "OUTAGE must be seconds"
12	SERVER="k3d-$CLUSTER_NAME-server-0"; EV_FILE="$EV_DIR/L2/api-outage.md"; mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L2"
13	W=$(mktemp -d); STOPPED=0
14	cleanup() { [ $STOPPED = 0 ] || docker start "$SERVER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; rm -rf "$W" "$BODY" "$CHECKS"; }
15	trap cleanup EXIT
16	api_up() { kubectl get --raw /readyz >/dev/null 2>&1; }
17	
18	client_up
19	until primary_confirms; do sleep 1; done
20	L=$(leader); IPS=""; for m in pg-0 pg-1 pg-2; do IPS="$IPS $m=$(pod_ip "$m")"; done
21	RUN_ID="api-outage-$(date +%s)"; DURATION=$((OUTAGE + 150))
22	kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-api-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
23	sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|; s|__IPS__|${IPS# }|; s|__RUN__|$RUN_ID|; s|__DURATION__|$DURATION|" <<'YAML' | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - >/dev/null
24	apiVersion: batch/v1
25	kind: Job
26	metadata: {name: pg-api-probe}
27	spec:
28	  backoffLimit: 0
29	  template:
30	    spec:
31	      restartPolicy: Never
32	      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: db}
33	      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
34	      containers:
35	      - name: probe
36	        image: __PG_IMAGE__
37	        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
38	        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
39	        env:
40	        - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
41	        - name: PGPASSWORD
42	          valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app-password}}
43	        command: [bash, -c]
44	        args:
45	        - |
46	          end=$(( $(date +%s) + __DURATION__ )); i=0
47	          while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$end" ]; do i=$((i+1))
48	            for kv in __IPS__; do ( m=${kv%%=*}; ip=${kv#*=}; c="host=$ip user=app dbname=app connect_timeout=2"
49	              r=$(timeout 3 psql "$c" -XAtqc "select pg_is_in_recovery()" 2>/dev/null) || r=x
50	              w=no; timeout 3 psql "$c" -XAtq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c "insert into probe (run, seq, client_ts) values ('__RUN__', $i * 10 + ${m#pg-}, now())" >/dev/null 2>&1 && w=yes
51	              echo "R $i $(date +%s.%N) $m ${r:-x} $w" ) & done
52	            sleep 1
53	          done; wait; echo DONE
54	        volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
55	      volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]
56	YAML
57	until [ "$(kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-api-probe 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^R')" -ge 15 ]; do sleep 1; done
58	
59	section "API server outage"
60	T_STOP=$(now); docker stop "$SERVER" >/dev/null; STOPPED=1
61	note "Leader before: \`$L\`. Server container \`$SERVER\` stopped at $(iso "$T_STOP") UTC for ${OUTAGE} s. Members by IP: \`${IPS# }\`."
62	sleep "$OUTAGE"
63	T_START=$(now); docker start "$SERVER" >/dev/null; STOPPED=0
64	end=$((SECONDS + 240)); until api_up; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || die "API not back after 240 s"; sleep 1; done; T_API=$(now)
65	client_up   # the test client runs on the server node, so it did not survive the restart
66	T_HEALTHY=""; end=$((SECONDS + 240)); until primary_confirms 2>/dev/null; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || break; sleep 1; done
67	primary_confirms 2>/dev/null && T_HEALTHY=$(now); L2=$(leader)
68	end=$((SECONDS + DURATION + 60)); until kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-api-probe 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^DONE'; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || break; sleep 2; done
69	kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-api-probe > "$W/probe.txt"
70	kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-api-probe --wait=false >/dev/null
71	
72	# Rounds are grouped by round number; times are each round's first sample.
73	awk '$1=="R"' "$W/probe.txt" | sort -k2,2n -k4,4 > "$W/r.txt"
74	LAST_PRIMARY_DURING=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b && $5=="f" {print $3}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -n | tail -1)
75	LAST_WRITE_DURING=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b && $6=="yes" {print $3}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -n | tail -1)
76	FIRST_WRITE_AFTER=$(awk -v b="$T_START" '$3>b && $6=="yes" {print $3}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -n | head -1)
77	OUT_ROUNDS=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b {print $2}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -u | wc -l)
78	READ_ROUNDS=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b && $5=="t" {print $2}' "$W/r.txt" | sort -u | wc -l)
79	NOPRIM_ROUNDS=$(awk -v a="$T_STOP" -v b="$T_START" '$3>a && $3<b {r[$2]=1} $3>a && $3<b && $5=="f" {p[$2]=1} END {n=0; for (k in r) if (!(k in p)) n++; print n}' "$W/r.txt")
80	MAXP=$(awk '$5=="f" {c[$2]++} END {m=0; for (k in c) if (c[k]>m) m=c[k]; print m}' "$W/r.txt")
81	WRITERS=$(awk '$6=="yes" {c[$2]++} END {m=0; for (k in c) if (c[k]>m) m=c[k]; print m}' "$W/r.txt")
82	note "During the outage: last sample with a primary +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_PRIMARY_DURING") s, last successful write +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_WRITE_DURING") s. $READ_ROUNDS of $OUT_ROUNDS rounds had a replica answering reads, and $NOPRIM_ROUNDS rounds had no primary at all. API back at +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_API") s, healthy with leader \`$L2\` at +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_HEALTHY") s, first write after restart +$(secs "$T_STOP" "$FIRST_WRITE_AFTER") s."
83	run "awk -v a=$T_STOP '\$3>a-3' $W/r.txt | awk '{printf \"%s round=%s %s in_recovery=%s write=%s\\n\", strftime(\"%H:%M:%S\", \$3, 1), \$2, \$4, \$5, \$6}' | awk 'NR%3==1 || /write=yes/' | head -40" || true
84	check "Every member demoted during the outage (writes stopped)" test -n "$LAST_WRITE_DURING" -a "$NOPRIM_ROUNDS" -gt 0
85	check "Demotion within 20 s of the outage starting (ttl)" awk -v d="$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_WRITE_DURING")" 'BEGIN{exit !(d != "n/a" && d <= 20)}'
86	check "Reads continued on replicas in every outage round" test "$READ_ROUNDS" = "$OUT_ROUNDS"
87	check "Never more than 1 primary in any round" test "$MAXP" -le 1
88	check "Never more than 1 member accepted a write in any round" test "$WRITERS" -le 1
89	check "A leader was elected and replication healthy after the API returned" test -n "$T_HEALTHY"
90	
91	verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
92	{ printf '# L2 failure mode: api-outage\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$verdict"
93	  printf -- '- **Fault:** `docker stop` on the k3d server container for %s s, then `docker start`. With `failsafe_mode` off (ADR-002), every member should demote, so writes stop and reads continue. Observed by a Job on an agent node that queried each member by pod IP every second. Its log was read after the API returned, so nothing depends on `make status` or the API during the outage.\n' "$OUTAGE"
94	  printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make test-api-outage`\n- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "${K3S_IMAGE%%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
95	  printf '\n## Summary\n\n| Outage (s) | Last write during outage (s) | Rounds with no primary | Reads served | Max primaries in a round | API back (s) | Healthy again (s) | First write after (s) | Result |\n|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|\n'
96	  printf '| %s | +%s | %s of %s | %s of %s rounds | %s | +%s | +%s | +%s | %s |\n\n' "$OUTAGE" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$LAST_WRITE_DURING")" "$NOPRIM_ROUNDS" "$OUT_ROUNDS" "$READ_ROUNDS" "$OUT_ROUNDS" "$MAXP" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_API")" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$T_HEALTHY")" "$(secs "$T_STOP" "$FIRST_WRITE_AFTER")" "$verdict"
97	  printf 'Times are seconds after the server was stopped. Write unavailability lasts the whole outage plus recovery, by design.\n\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'
98	  cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_FILE"

The spike harness (`scripts/spikes/lib.sh`) replaces any value from `./secrets/credentials` with `[REDACTED:<credential-name>]` before writing evidence files. These replacements are made at generation time, so no unredacted original exists in the repository to log individually.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. Phase L3: Garage, pgBackRest, WAL archiving, retention, verification. Read CLAUDE.md, the L3
section and "Phase notes from L0" in docs/01-design-options.md, ADR-005/009/014, the S1 spike
scripts and history, and the "What changes L3" notes at the end of docs/evidence/L2-failover.md.
Work on main. Deadline Thu 26 Nov 23:59 Asia/Dhaka: minimal, aimed at the gate.

Carry the L2 findings: deploy the archiving config BEFORE any measurement (it rolls every pod and
moves the leader); anything that POSTs to Patroni avoids the API-server proxy.

Build in small verified steps (timebox ~2h):
1. Garage from our own manifests (productionise the S1 spike): single node, PVC, metadata/data
   fsync on, bootstrap Job via the Admin API with keys from ./secrets. Part of make up.
2. pgBackRest per ADR-009: all repo1-* settings only in repo.conf, repository encryption from
   ./secrets, pg1..pg3 via stable headless-service DNS, TLS server using the L0 certs.
3. WAL archiving: archive_mode on, async archive-push, restore_command via archive-get, added as
   a Patroni config file so L1's structure holds. Confirm pg_stat_archiver shows no failures and
   `pgbackrest check` passes.
4. Stanza creation as a Job (idempotent).
5. Backup CronJob: full backup, then expire (repo1-retention-full=7), then verify. The job fails
   unless verify reports status ok (L0 finding: verify can exit 0 with status error).
   BACKUP_SCHEDULE is a parameter (default daily 20:00 UTC).
6. make backup: on-demand run from the same CronJob template.
7. Evidence of a truly scheduled run (R4.1): set BACKUP_SCHEDULE to every 10 minutes, let at least
   one scheduled Job complete, then restore the default.
8. Retention enforcement: with a temporary low retention (e.g. 2 fulls), run 3 backups and prove
   the oldest is expired along with its WAL; restore the real setting.
9. Backup after failover (R4.6): run one failover-node, then confirm archiving stays healthy on
   the new timeline and a backup + verify succeeds.
10. Garage restart watch item: restart Garage while the probe writes; prove WAL archiving
    recovers on its own within a bounded time (no permanent stall) and record the time.

Results to docs/evidence/L3-backup.md (generated) with PASS/FAIL per check, plus a short
history file for anything hand-written.

Optional, only if time remains at the end: one rerun of make test-api-outage with the fixed
report guard; if it fails again, record "observed recovery, not measured" in the L2 history.

Rules: stop and report if something fails twice. Never print secrets or key material.
exec only inside committed test/fault-injection scripts (D4); disclose anything else.

Finish with: the gate checklist, actual time vs 2h, and anything that changes L4 (restore/PITR).
Don't commit.

# Project context

**Goal:** A PostgreSQL 15+ HA cluster on Kubernetes, built without operators or turnkey charts, with everything as code and reproducible by a reviewer.

**Timezones:** The VM runs on UTC and the lead works in UTC+6.

**Priorities:** replication and failover, then backup and PITR, then monitoring, then security. The optional second-agent comparison comes next, and the optional GCS backup overlay (R4.7) is the lowest priority.

## Key constraints

- No operators of any kind, third-party Helm charts, prebuilt HA images or managed databases.
- Postgres image is built by us from the official `postgres` image plus Patroni.
- Garage (object storage, see `docs/decisions/ADR-014-object-storage.md`), Prometheus and Alertmanager use our own minimal manifests.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).
