#!/bin/bash
# Runs inside the spike pod. Exercises pgBackRest against Garage end to end. Prints no credentials.
set -euo pipefail
export PGHOST=/tmp PGUSER=postgres
S=s1
step() { printf '\n--- %s\n' "$1"; }
mkdir -p /work/log /work/lock /work/spool
sql() { psql -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -Atc "$1"; }

step "pgBackRest config in use (credentials come from environment variables)"
pgbackrest version
grep -h '^repo1-' /etc/pgbackrest/conf.d/repo.conf

step "initdb and start Postgres with WAL archiving through pgBackRest"
mkdir -m 0700 /work/pgdata
initdb -D /work/pgdata --data-checksums --auth-local=trust --auth-host=reject >/dev/null
cat >> /work/pgdata/postgresql.conf <<CONF
listen_addresses = ''
unix_socket_directories = '/tmp'
wal_level = replica
archive_mode = on
archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=$S archive-push %p'
CONF
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -l /work/pg.log -w start >/dev/null

step "stanza-create"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=warn stanza-create; echo STANZA_OK

step "check (proves WAL archiving reaches the repository)"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=warn check; echo CHECK_OK

step "write data, then take a full backup"
sql "create table marker as select g id, md5(g::text) v from generate_series(1,200000) g" >/dev/null
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --type=full --start-fast --log-level-console=warn backup; echo BACKUP_OK

step "write more data after the backup, which only archived WAL can restore"
sql "insert into marker select g, md5(g::text) from generate_series(200001,250000) g" >/dev/null
EXPECT=$(sql "select count(*) || ':' || md5(string_agg(v, '' order by id)) from marker")
echo "source: $EXPECT"
LSN=$(sql "select pg_walfile_name(pg_switch_wal())")
echo "switched WAL segment: $LSN"
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  A=$(sql "select coalesce(last_archived_wal,'') from pg_stat_archiver")
  [[ "$A" > "$LSN" || "$A" == "$LSN" ]] && break; sleep 1
done
echo "last archived: $A"
[[ "$A" > "$LSN" || "$A" == "$LSN" ]]; echo ARCHIVE_OK
sql "select 'archived=' || archived_count || ' failed=' || failed_count from pg_stat_archiver"

step "pgbackrest info"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S info

step "pgbackrest verify (the exit code alone is not trusted, the reported status must be ok)"
V=$(pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info --verbose verify 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -E 'status:|archiveId|backup:|checked|missing|checksum invalid|size invalid|other' | sed -E 's/^[0-9-]+ [0-9:.]+ +P[0-9]+ +[A-Z]+: //; s/^ +//'
printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -q 'status: ok'; echo VERIFY_OK

step "encryption: raw object is ciphertext, right passphrase reads it, wrong one cannot"
F=backup/$S/backup.info
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=error repo-get --raw "$F" > /work/raw.bin
RAW=$(head -c 8 /work/raw.bin); echo "raw header: $RAW"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=error repo-get "$F" > /work/plain.bin
PLAIN=$(head -c 9 /work/plain.bin); echo "decrypted header: $PLAIN"
if PGBACKREST_REPO1_CIPHER_PASS=wrong-passphrase pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=off --log-level-stderr=off repo-get "$F" >/dev/null 2>&1
then WRONG=read; else WRONG=refused; fi
echo "wrong passphrase: $WRONG"
[ "$RAW" = "Salted__" ] && [ "$PLAIN" = "[backrest" ] && [ "$WRONG" = refused ]; echo CIPHER_OK

step "stop the source and destroy its data directory, then restore"
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -m fast -w stop >/dev/null
rm -rf /work/pgdata; mkdir -m 0700 /work/pgdata
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=warn --type=default --archive-mode=off restore; echo RESTORE_OK
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -l /work/restore.log -w -t 120 start >/dev/null
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do [ "$(sql 'select pg_is_in_recovery()')" = f ] && break; sleep 1; done
GOT=$(sql "select count(*) || ':' || md5(string_agg(v, '' order by id)) from marker")
echo "restored: $GOT"
[ "$GOT" = "$EXPECT" ]; echo DATA_MATCH_OK
sql "select 'in_recovery=' || pg_is_in_recovery() || ' timeline=' || (select timeline_id from pg_control_checkpoint())"
pg_amcheck --all --install-missing --heapallindexed -h /tmp -U postgres; echo AMCHECK_OK
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -m fast -w stop >/dev/null
echo SPIKE_INNER_DONE
# L0 spike S1: history and investigations

This file is maintained by hand. `make spike-s1` writes only the generated results in [`L0-spike-S1.md`](L0-spike-S1.md) and never touches this file.

## Run history

The clean L0 run was made at 11:11 UTC after `make down && make up`. Earlier attempts on 2026-11-23 (UTC), kept here so the result is not overstated:

1. **Failed at 11:06.** The bootstrap Job outlasted the harness's 90 s wait, because one connection to the Garage admin port hung for 136 s. pgBackRest therefore ran before its key existed and got HTTP 403. The trigger is a startup race, and the curl connect timeout is the fix. See "Resolution" below.
2. **The same run exposed two vacuous checks.** `pgbackrest verify` **exited 0 while reporting `status: error`**, and the wrong-passphrase check passed against an empty repository. Verify now requires `status: ok`. The cipher check now requires ciphertext on disk, a successful read with the right passphrase and a refused read with a wrong one.
3. **Failed at 11:09.** Stanza, backup, archive, verify, encryption and restore passed, but `pg_amcheck` stopped because the `amcheck` extension was not installed. It now runs with `--install-missing`.

## Resolution: the 136 s Garage connection hang

**Verdict:** The startup-race explanation is correct about the trigger, and the earlier "cause unknown" statement is superseded. Two details of the original explanation were wrong or incomplete:

- The hang is not simply "admin port not ready". A connection attempted during Garage startup can stall for about 135 s and never recover, even after Garage is serving.
- The readiness probe does not gate the bootstrap Job. The Job and Garage are applied together, and the Job started 4 to 5 s before the Garage container in every trial. **The connect timeout with retry is the fix.**

**Not established:** why these connections stall instead of being refused. No packet capture was taken. The 132 to 136 s duration is consistent with kernel SYN retry exhaustion (`net.ipv4.tcp_syn_retries = 6` on the host), but that mechanism is inferred.

### Evidence (2026-11-23, UTC)

Original failure at 11:06, from the bootstrap Job log:

```console
curl: (7) Failed to connect to garage.spike-s1.svc.cluster.local:3903 after 15 ms: Could not connect to server
curl: (28) Failed to connect to garage.spike-s1.svc.cluster.local:3903 after 136050 ms: Could not connect to server
```

**Reproduction, 14:20 to 14:28.** Three fresh namespaces used the same Garage image, config, PVC, readiness probe and node placement. A probe Job started one curl every 0.5 s with no connect timeout, 60 per trial.

| Trial | Probe Job start | Garage container start | Pod Ready | Refused | Hung (duration) | Succeeded (max time) | Last hung attempt started |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 14:20:06 | 14:20:10 | 14:20:11 | 1 | 10 (132.6 to 136.2 s) | 49 (9 ms) | 14:20:12 |
| 2 | 14:22:47 | 14:22:51 | 14:22:52 | 3 | 8 (132.5 to 136.1 s) | 49 (6 ms) | 14:22:52 |
| 3 | 14:25:26 | 14:25:31 | 14:25:32 | 1 | 10 (132.4 to 136.0 s) | 49 (7 ms) | 14:25:32 |

The hang reproduced in 3 of 3 trials, across 28 of 180 connections. Attempt start times have 1 s resolution. Attempts started in the same second as Ready, and in trial 1 one second after it, still hung, so waiting for Ready alone would not fully close the window.

**Fix check.** Five more fresh startups ran curl with the bootstrap Job's options (`--connect-timeout 3 --max-time 15 --retry 20 --retry-delay 1 --retry-all-errors`). All five reached Garage's admin port after 1 or 2 connect timeouts and 1 or 2 refusals. The HTTP 503 they received is expected from `/health` before a layout exists. Their 23 to 26 s run time includes retries of that 503, so it is not a time-to-connect measurement.

The retry budget covers the observed window: 21 connect attempts at 3 s plus 20 delays of 1 s is at most 83 s, inside the harness's 120 s wait. The clean S1 run at 11:11 UTC showed the same recovery in its bootstrap log: one refusal, four 3 s timeouts, then success.

### Rerun the trials

`scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh` is the committed form of this probe. It needs a running cluster (`make up`), creates one throwaway namespace per trial, always deletes it, uses random one-time tokens and masks its saved output in `.run/s1-garage-startup-race/`.

```console
$ MODE=unbounded TRIALS=3 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh   # about 3 min per trial
$ MODE=bounded TRIALS=5 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh     # under 1 min per trial
```

The committed script probes an unauthenticated admin route, so a reachable Garage returns HTTP 403 at once and bounded runs measure real time to connect. Its validation run on 2026-11-23 (UTC) gave:

```console
$ MODE=bounded TRIALS=3 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh
trial 1: BOUNDED exit=0 http=403 retries=3 elapsed_s=9
trial 2: BOUNDED exit=0 http=403 retries=3 elapsed_s=9
trial 3: BOUNDED exit=0 http=403 retries=3 elapsed_s=10
$ MODE=unbounded TRIALS=1 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh
trial 1: ok=49 refused=3 hung=8 hung_seconds=132.8-136.4 other=0
```

### Diagnostic `docker exec` disclosure

At 2026-11-23T14:19:20Z (UTC), during this investigation, one read-only `docker exec` ran on the k3d server node `k3d-pg-ha-server-0`:

```console
$ docker exec k3d-pg-ha-server-0 sh -c 'iptables-save 2>/dev/null | grep -c KUBE; nft list ruleset 2>/dev/null | grep -c -i kube; cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_syn_sent'
126
122
120
```

- **What it inspected:** the number of Kubernetes firewall rules visible through iptables and nftables, and the connection-tracking timeout for unanswered SYNs.
- **What it changed:** nothing. All three commands only read state.
- **Dependence:** none. No result or conclusion in this file uses its output, and the committed probe does not use `exec`.
- **Policy:** the lead accepted this diagnostic-only use. Delivery paths stay exec-free under D4.

### L3 watch item

The S1 bootstrap hang is closed. The untested question of a Garage restart affecting running clients is tracked in the L3 notes of [`docs/01-design-options.md`](../01-design-options.md#phase-notes-from-l0).

## S3 access key rotation and S1 rerun

The Garage S3 access key **ID** was printed in session logs while debugging (see [`redaction-log.md`](../process/redaction-log.md)). The secret key was not exposed. On 2026-11-23 at about 15:07 UTC, the ID and secret key were both regenerated with `scripts/secrets.sh`, and no other credential changed. The old pair was only ever valid on Garage instances in spike namespaces that no longer exist, and it has been destroyed.

`make spike-s1` then passed all 12 checks on the new key (run 2026-11-23T15:07:51Z, 52 s, backup `20261123-150811F`). That run is the current [`L0-spike-S1.md`](L0-spike-S1.md). #!/bin/bash
# Runs inside the spike pod. Exercises pgBackRest against Garage end to end. Prints no credentials.
set -euo pipefail
export PGHOST=/tmp PGUSER=postgres
S=s1
step() { printf '\n--- %s\n' "$1"; }
mkdir -p /work/log /work/lock /work/spool
sql() { psql -d postgres -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -Atc "$1"; }

step "pgBackRest config in use (credentials come from environment variables)"
pgbackrest version
grep -h '^repo1-' /etc/pgbackrest/conf.d/repo.conf

step "initdb and start Postgres with WAL archiving through pgBackRest"
mkdir -m 0700 /work/pgdata
initdb -D /work/pgdata --data-checksums --auth-local=trust --auth-host=reject >/dev/null
cat >> /work/pgdata/postgresql.conf <<CONF
listen_addresses = ''
unix_socket_directories = '/tmp'
wal_level = replica
archive_mode = on
archive_command = 'pgbackrest --stanza=$S archive-push %p'
CONF
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -l /work/pg.log -w start >/dev/null

step "stanza-create"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=warn stanza-create; echo STANZA_OK

step "check (proves WAL archiving reaches the repository)"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=warn check; echo CHECK_OK

step "write data, then take a full backup"
sql "create table marker as select g id, md5(g::text) v from generate_series(1,200000) g" >/dev/null
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --type=full --start-fast --log-level-console=warn backup; echo BACKUP_OK

step "write more data after the backup, which only archived WAL can restore"
sql "insert into marker select g, md5(g::text) from generate_series(200001,250000) g" >/dev/null
EXPECT=$(sql "select count(*) || ':' || md5(string_agg(v, '' order by id)) from marker")
echo "source: $EXPECT"
LSN=$(sql "select pg_walfile_name(pg_switch_wal())")
echo "switched WAL segment: $LSN"
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  A=$(sql "select coalesce(last_archived_wal,'') from pg_stat_archiver")
  [[ "$A" > "$LSN" || "$A" == "$LSN" ]] && break; sleep 1
done
echo "last archived: $A"
[[ "$A" > "$LSN" || "$A" == "$LSN" ]]; echo ARCHIVE_OK
sql "select 'archived=' || archived_count || ' failed=' || failed_count from pg_stat_archiver"

step "pgbackrest info"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S info

step "pgbackrest verify (the exit code alone is not trusted, the reported status must be ok)"
V=$(pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info --verbose verify 2>&1 || true)
printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -E 'status:|archiveId|backup:|checked|missing|checksum invalid|size invalid|other' | sed -E 's/^[0-9-]+ [0-9:.]+ +P[0-9]+ +[A-Z]+: //; s/^ +//'
printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -q 'status: ok'; echo VERIFY_OK

step "encryption: raw object is ciphertext, right passphrase reads it, wrong one cannot"
F=backup/$S/backup.info
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=error repo-get --raw "$F" > /work/raw.bin
RAW=$(head -c 8 /work/raw.bin); echo "raw header: $RAW"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=error repo-get "$F" > /work/plain.bin
PLAIN=$(head -c 9 /work/plain.bin); echo "decrypted header: $PLAIN"
if PGBACKREST_REPO1_CIPHER_PASS=wrong-passphrase pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=off --log-level-stderr=off repo-get "$F" >/dev/null 2>&1
then WRONG=read; else WRONG=refused; fi
echo "wrong passphrase: $WRONG"
[ "$RAW" = "Salted__" ] && [ "$PLAIN" = "[backrest" ] && [ "$WRONG" = refused ]; echo CIPHER_OK

step "stop the source and destroy its data directory, then restore"
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -m fast -w stop >/dev/null
rm -rf /work/pgdata; mkdir -m 0700 /work/pgdata
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=warn --type=default --archive-mode=off restore; echo RESTORE_OK
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -l /work/restore.log -w -t 120 start >/dev/null
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do [ "$(sql 'select pg_is_in_recovery()')" = f ] && break; sleep 1; done
GOT=$(sql "select count(*) || ':' || md5(string_agg(v, '' order by id)) from marker")
echo "restored: $GOT"
[ "$GOT" = "$EXPECT" ]; echo DATA_MATCH_OK
sql "select 'in_recovery=' || pg_is_in_recovery() || ' timeline=' || (select timeline_id from pg_control_checkpoint())"
pg_amcheck --all --install-missing --heapallindexed -h /tmp -U postgres; echo AMCHECK_OK
pg_ctl -D /work/pgdata -m fast -w stop >/dev/null
echo SPIKE_INNER_DONE
# L0 spike S1: history and investigations

This file is maintained by hand. `make spike-s1` writes only the generated results in [`L0-spike-S1.md`](L0-spike-S1.md) and never touches this file.

## Run history

The clean L0 run was made at 11:11 UTC after `make down && make up`. Earlier attempts on 2026-11-23 (UTC), kept here so the result is not overstated:

1. **Failed at 11:06.** The bootstrap Job outlasted the harness's 90 s wait, because one connection to the Garage admin port hung for 136 s. pgBackRest therefore ran before its key existed and got HTTP 403. The trigger is a startup race, and the curl connect timeout is the fix. See "Resolution" below.
2. **The same run exposed two vacuous checks.** `pgbackrest verify` **exited 0 while reporting `status: error`**, and the wrong-passphrase check passed against an empty repository. Verify now requires `status: ok`. The cipher check now requires ciphertext on disk, a successful read with the right passphrase and a refused read with a wrong one.
3. **Failed at 11:09.** Stanza, backup, archive, verify, encryption and restore passed, but `pg_amcheck` stopped because the `amcheck` extension was not installed. It now runs with `--install-missing`.

## Resolution: the 136 s Garage connection hang

**Verdict:** The startup-race explanation is correct about the trigger, and the earlier "cause unknown" statement is superseded. Two details of the original explanation were wrong or incomplete:

- The hang is not simply "admin port not ready". A connection attempted during Garage startup can stall for about 135 s and never recover, even after Garage is serving.
- The readiness probe does not gate the bootstrap Job. The Job and Garage are applied together, and the Job started 4 to 5 s before the Garage container in every trial. **The connect timeout with retry is the fix.**

**Not established:** why these connections stall instead of being refused. No packet capture was taken. The 132 to 136 s duration is consistent with kernel SYN retry exhaustion (`net.ipv4.tcp_syn_retries = 6` on the host), but that mechanism is inferred.

### Evidence (2026-11-23, UTC)

Original failure at 11:06, from the bootstrap Job log:

```console
curl: (7) Failed to connect to garage.spike-s1.svc.cluster.local:3903 after 15 ms: Could not connect to server
curl: (28) Failed to connect to garage.spike-s1.svc.cluster.local:3903 after 136050 ms: Could not connect to server
```

**Reproduction, 14:20 to 14:28.** Three fresh namespaces used the same Garage image, config, PVC, readiness probe and node placement. A probe Job started one curl every 0.5 s with no connect timeout, 60 per trial.

| Trial | Probe Job start | Garage container start | Pod Ready | Refused | Hung (duration) | Succeeded (max time) | Last hung attempt started |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 14:20:06 | 14:20:10 | 14:20:11 | 1 | 10 (132.6 to 136.2 s) | 49 (9 ms) | 14:20:12 |
| 2 | 14:22:47 | 14:22:51 | 14:22:52 | 3 | 8 (132.5 to 136.1 s) | 49 (6 ms) | 14:22:52 |
| 3 | 14:25:26 | 14:25:31 | 14:25:32 | 1 | 10 (132.4 to 136.0 s) | 49 (7 ms) | 14:25:32 |

The hang reproduced in 3 of 3 trials, across 28 of 180 connections. Attempt start times have 1 s resolution. Attempts started in the same second as Ready, and in trial 1 one second after it, still hung, so waiting for Ready alone would not fully close the window.

**Fix check.** Five more fresh startups ran curl with the bootstrap Job's options (`--connect-timeout 3 --max-time 15 --retry 20 --retry-delay 1 --retry-all-errors`). All five reached Garage's admin port after 1 or 2 connect timeouts and 1 or 2 refusals. The HTTP 503 they received is expected from `/health` before a layout exists. Their 23 to 26 s run time includes retries of that 503, so it is not a time-to-connect measurement.

The retry budget covers the observed window: 21 connect attempts at 3 s plus 20 delays of 1 s is at most 83 s, inside the harness's 120 s wait. The clean S1 run at 11:11 UTC showed the same recovery in its bootstrap log: one refusal, four 3 s timeouts, then success.

### Rerun the trials

`scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh` is the committed form of this probe. It needs a running cluster (`make up`), creates one throwaway namespace per trial, always deletes it, uses random one-time tokens and masks its saved output in `.run/s1-garage-startup-race/`.

```console
$ MODE=unbounded TRIALS=3 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh   # about 3 min per trial
$ MODE=bounded TRIALS=5 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh     # under 1 min per trial
```

The committed script probes an unauthenticated admin route, so a reachable Garage returns HTTP 403 at once and bounded runs measure real time to connect. Its validation run on 2026-11-23 (UTC) gave:

```console
$ MODE=bounded TRIALS=3 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh
trial 1: BOUNDED exit=0 http=403 retries=3 elapsed_s=9
trial 2: BOUNDED exit=0 http=403 retries=3 elapsed_s=9
trial 3: BOUNDED exit=0 http=403 retries=3 elapsed_s=10
$ MODE=unbounded TRIALS=1 scripts/spikes/s1-garage-startup-race.sh
trial 1: ok=49 refused=3 hung=8 hung_seconds=132.8-136.4 other=0
```

### Diagnostic `docker exec` disclosure

At 2026-11-23T14:19:20Z (UTC), during this investigation, one read-only `docker exec` ran on the k3d server node `k3d-pg-ha-server-0`:

```console
$ docker exec k3d-pg-ha-server-0 sh -c 'iptables-save 2>/dev/null | grep -c KUBE; nft list ruleset 2>/dev/null | grep -c -i kube; cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_syn_sent'
126
122
120
```

- **What it inspected:** the number of Kubernetes firewall rules visible through iptables and nftables, and the connection-tracking timeout for unanswered SYNs.
- **What it changed:** nothing. All three commands only read state.
- **Dependence:** none. No result or conclusion in this file uses its output, and the committed probe does not use `exec`.
- **Policy:** the lead accepted this diagnostic-only use. Delivery paths stay exec-free under D4.

### L3 watch item

The S1 bootstrap hang is closed. The untested question of a Garage restart affecting running clients is tracked in the L3 notes of [`docs/01-design-options.md`](../01-design-options.md#phase-notes-from-l0).

## S3 access key rotation and S1 rerun

The Garage S3 access key **ID** was printed in session logs while debugging (see [`redaction-log.md`](../process/redaction-log.md)). The secret key was not exposed. On 2026-11-23 at about 15:07 UTC, the ID and secret key were both regenerated with `scripts/secrets.sh`, and no other credential changed. The old pair was only ever valid on Garage instances in spike namespaces that no longer exist, and it has been destroyed.

`make spike-s1` then passed all 12 checks on the new key (run 2026-11-23T15:07:51Z, 52 s, backup `20261123-150811F`). That run is the current [`L0-spike-S1.md`](L0-spike-S1.md). Its bootstrap log shows the same startup race, bounded: one refusal, two 3 s timeouts, then success. This history file was byte-identical before and after the rerun.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared settings. Sourced by every project script.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT_DIR/versions.env"
set +a

CLUSTER_NAME=pg-ha
API_PORT=6550
BIN_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/bin"
SECRETS_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/secrets"
RUN_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/.run"
export KUBECONFIG="$RUN_DIR/kubeconfig"
export PATH="$BIN_DIR:$PATH"

# Image tag derived from the pinned inputs, so a version change produces a new tag.
pg_version="${POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE#postgres:}"; pg_version="${pg_version%%-*}"
PG_IMAGE="pg-ha-postgres:${pg_version}-patroni${PATRONI_DEB_VERSION%%-*}-pgbackrest${PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION%%-*}"

log()  { printf '%s\n' "$*"; }
die()  { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
cluster_exists() { k3d cluster list -o json | jq -e --arg n "$CLUSTER_NAME" 'any(.[]; .name == $n)' >/dev/null; }

# L1: Postgres cluster
PG_NS=pg-ha
PG_STS=pg
# Patroni's /cluster view, read through the API server's pod proxy, so no kubectl exec is needed (D4).
patroni_cluster() {
  local i out
  for i in 0 1 2; do
    out=$(kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/namespaces/$PG_NS/pods/$PG_STS-$i:8008/proxy/cluster" 2>/dev/null) && { printf '%s\n' "$out"; return 0; }
  done
  return 1
}
# Succeeds when Patroni reports 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas and 1 sync standby.
patroni_healthy() {
  patroni_cluster | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role == "leader" and .state == "running")] | length == 1' >/dev/null &&
  patroni_cluster | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role != "leader" and .state == "streaming")] | length == 2' >/dev/null &&
  patroni_cluster | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role == "sync_standby")] | length == 1' >/dev/null
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploys the Patroni cluster (L1) and waits until it is healthy. Idempotent, and never prints a secret.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || die "cluster $CLUSTER_NAME not found, run: make cluster"
C="$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"; T="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"
for f in "$C"/pg-{postgres,replicator,rewind,monitor,backup,app,app_ro}-password "$T"/{ca.crt,postgres-server.crt,postgres-server.key}; do
  [ -s "$f" ] || die "missing $f, run: make certs secrets"
done

kubectl apply -f "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg/namespace.yaml" >/dev/null
# Server-side apply keeps secret values out of the last-applied annotation.
secret() { kubectl -n "$PG_NS" create secret generic "$@" --dry-run=client -o yaml |
  kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-deploy --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null; }
secret pg-credentials $(for r in postgres replicator rewind monitor backup app app_ro; do printf -- '--from-file=%s ' "$C/pg-$r-password"; done)
secret pg-tls --from-file=tls.crt="$T/postgres-server.crt" --from-file=tls.key="$T/postgres-server.key" --from-file=ca.crt="$T/ca.crt"
kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg" | sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|" | kubectl apply -f -

kubectl -n "$PG_NS" rollout status "statefulset/$PG_STS" --timeout=300s
end=$((SECONDS + ${PG_WAIT:-180}))
until patroni_healthy; do
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "\(.name) \(.role) \(.state)"' || true; die "Patroni not healthy after ${PG_WAIT:-180} s"; }
  sleep 2
done
log "Patroni healthy: 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas, 1 sync standby"
# L1: Patroni-managed Postgres (ADR-001..008). Rendered by scripts/deploy.sh, which fills in the image.
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: pg-ha
resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - rbac.yaml
  - services.yaml
  - statefulset.yaml
  - pdb.yaml
configMapGenerator:
  # Patroni reads every file in /etc/patroni/conf.d, merged in name order.
  # L3 adds archiving as a further file (for example 20-archive.yml) without editing 10-base.yml.
  - name: pg-patroni
    files: [patroni/10-base.yml]
  - name: pg-scripts
    files: [scripts/post-bootstrap.sh]
# Patroni L1 base config. Per-pod values (name, addresses, passwords) come from environment variables.
# L3 adds archive_mode, archive_command, restore_command and create_replica_methods in a later file
# (20-archive.yml), which Patroni merges over this one.
scope: pg-rw            # Patroni names the leader Endpoints after the scope, so this is the pg-rw Service
restapi:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:8008
kubernetes:             # ADR-002
  use_endpoints: true
  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg, cluster-name: pg-rw}
  role_label: role
  ports: [{name: postgresql, port: 5432}]
bootstrap:
  dcs:
    ttl: 20             # ADR-006: loop_wait + 2 x retry_timeout = 13 s < ttl
    loop_wait: 3
    retry_timeout: 5
    primary_start_timeout: 0
    maximum_lag_on_failover: 1048576
    synchronous_mode: true          # ADR-004: non-strict, one synchronous standby
    synchronous_mode_strict: false
    synchronous_node_count: 1
    postgresql:
      use_pg_rewind: true           # ADR-008
      use_slots: true               # ADR-005
      parameters:
        wal_level: replica
        hot_standby: "on"
        wal_log_hints: "on"         # ADR-008, in addition to data checksums
        max_wal_size: 512MB         # ADR-005
        max_slot_wal_keep_size: 1GB # ADR-005: hard cap on WAL held for slots
        max_wal_senders: 10
        max_replication_slots: 10
        max_connections: 100
        shared_buffers: 128MB
        password_encryption: scram-sha-256
  initdb:
    - data-checksums
    - encoding: UTF8
  post_bootstrap: /etc/patroni/scripts/post-bootstrap.sh
postgresql:
  listen: 0.0.0.0:5432
  data_dir: /data/pgdata            # a subdirectory of the volume, created 0700 (S3)
  bin_dir: /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin
  pgpass: /tmp/pgpass
  use_unix_socket: true
  remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true   # ADR-008: re-clone if pg_rewind fails
  parameters:
    unix_socket_directories: /var/run/postgresql
    # Server TLS on with the L0 certificate. hostssl enforcement waits for L6.
    ssl: "on"
    ssl_cert_file: /etc/pg-tls/tls.crt
    ssl_key_file: /etc/pg-tls/tls.key
    ssl_ca_file: /etc/pg-tls/ca.crt
  pg_hba:
    - local all all peer
    - host replication replicator 127.0.0.1/32 scram-sha-256   # Patroni's local timeline check on replicas
    - host replication replicator 10.42.0.0/16 scram-sha-256
    - host all all 10.42.0.0/16 scram-sha-256
    - host all all 127.0.0.1/32 scram-sha-256
9:san="DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"
11:  san="$san,DNS:*.pg-headless.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:*.pg-headless.$ns.svc"
12:  san="$san,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc"
25:issue() { # name CN extendedKeyUsage SAN(optional)
31:    echo "extendedKeyUsage=$eku"; [ -z "$s" ] || echo "subjectAltName=$s"; } > "$ext"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for tests. Sources the spike evidence helpers (redact, run, check, note, section).
#
# kubectl exec (D4): tests run psql only inside their own client pod, pg-test-client, never in a
# Postgres pod. Fault scripts may use docker exec on a k3d node, and each use is documented where it runs.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../scripts/spikes/lib.sh"
NS=$PG_NS; CLIENT=pg-test-client
BODY=$(mktemp); CHECKS=$(mktemp); FAILS=0; T0=$SECONDS; STARTED=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
RW=pg-rw.$NS.svc.cluster.local; RO=pg-ro.$NS.svc.cluster.local
member() { echo "$1.pg-headless.$NS.svc.cluster.local"; }
now() { date +%s.%N; }
iso() { date -u -d "@$1" +%H:%M:%S.%3N; }
secs() { awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN{ if (a == "" || b == "") print "n/a"; else printf "%.2f", b - a }'; }

# q HOST USER SQL: one psql call from the client pod. The password is chosen inside the pod from its env.
q() {
  kubectl -n "$NS" exec "$CLIENT" -- sh -c '
    case "$2" in app) PGPASSWORD=$APP_PW ;; monitor) PGPASSWORD=$MON_PW ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac; export PGPASSWORD
    exec psql "host=$1 user=$2 dbname=app connect_timeout=3" -XAtq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -F " " -c "$3"' sh "$1" "$2" "$3"
}
export -f q; export NS CLIENT

client_up() {
  kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$CLIENT" >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl -n "$NS" wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$CLIENT" --timeout=5s >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0

  sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|" <<'YAML' | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - >/dev/null

metadata: {name: pg-test-client, labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg-test-client}}
spec:

  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0

  tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
  securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
  containers:
  - name: client
    image: __PG_IMAGE__
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    command: [sleep, "7200"]
    securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
    env:
    - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
    - name: APP_PW
      valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app-password}}
    - name: MON_PW
      valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-monitor-password}}
    volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
  volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]
YAML
  kubectl -n "$NS" wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$CLIENT" --timeout=90s >/dev/null || die "client pod not ready"
}

# Lock holder and renew time, read from the pg-rw Endpoints object that Patroni uses as its leader lock.
lock() { kubectl -n "$NS" get endpoints pg-rw -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.leader} {.metadata.annotations.renewTime} {.metadata.annotations.acquireTime}' 2>/dev/null; }
leader() { lock | awk '{print $1}'; }
pod_ip() { kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}' 2>/dev/null; }
pod_node() { kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$1" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}' 2>/dev/null; }
sync_standby() { q "$RW" monitor "select application_name from pg_stat_replication where sync_state = 'sync'" 2>/dev/null; }

# Healthy as seen from the primary itself: 2 streaming standbys, exactly 1 sync, and Patroni agrees.
primary_confirms() { # [member that must be streaming]
  local r; r=$(q "$RW" monitor "select application_name, state, sync_state from pg_stat_replication" 2>/dev/null) || return 1

{ printf '# L2: failover, switchover and split-brain\n\nGenerated from the per-mode files in [`L2/`](L2/) each time a mode runs. Timestamps are UTC.\n\n'

RPO is the number of acknowledged rows missing on the new primary. The target is RTO at most 30 s with safe settings (ttl 20, loop_wait 3, retry_timeout 5).\n'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Spike harness: runs commands, records them with their output, and writes a PASS/FAIL evidence file.
# Any value from ./secrets/credentials is replaced by a visible placeholder before it reaches the file.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../lib.sh"
SPIKE_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/scripts/spikes"
EV_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/docs/evidence"

redact() {
  python3 -I -c '
import glob, os, sys
data = sys.stdin.read()
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "*")):
    value = open(path).read().strip()
    if value:
        data = data.replace(value, "[REDACTED:" + os.path.basename(path) + "]")
sys.stdout.write(data)' "$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"
}

ev_start() { # id title question criteria
  SPIKE=$1; TITLE=$2; QUESTION=$3; CRITERIA=$4; NS="spike-$(echo "$1" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
  BODY=$(mktemp); CHECKS=$(mktemp); FAILS=0; T0=$SECONDS; STARTED=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
  kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl delete ns "$NS" --wait=true >/dev/null
  trap ev_cleanup EXIT
}
ev_cleanup() {
  [ "${KEEP:-0}" = 1 ] || kubectl delete ns "$NS" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -f "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
}
section() { printf '\n## %s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; log "== $1"; }
run() { # command string; output is recorded. Returns the command's exit code.
  local out rc=0
  out=$(eval "$1" 2>&1) || rc=$?
  { printf '\n```console\n$ %s\n' "$1"; printf '%s\n' "$out"; [ $rc -eq 0 ] || printf '[exit code %s]\n' "$rc"; printf '```\n'; } | redact >> "$BODY"
  printf '%s\n' "$out" | redact | tail -"${TAIL:-12}"
  return $rc
}
note() { printf '\n%s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; }
check() { # description, command...
  local d=$1; shift
  if "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '| %s | PASS |\n' "$d" >> "$CHECKS"; log "PASS  $d"
  else printf '| %s | **FAIL** |\n' "$d" >> "$CHECKS"; log "FAIL  $d"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); fi
}
ev_finish() {
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  local f="$EV_DIR/L0-spike-$SPIKE.md"; mkdir -p "$EV_DIR"
  { printf '# L0 spike %s: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$SPIKE" "$TITLE" "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **Question:** %s\n- **Pass criteria:** %s\n' "$QUESTION" "$CRITERIA"
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make spike-%s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$(echo "$SPIKE" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')"
    printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
    [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L0-spike-$SPIKE-history.md" ] || printf -- '- **History:** [`L0-spike-%s-history.md`](L0-spike-%s-history.md) (maintained by hand, never written by this harness)\n' "$SPIKE" "$SPIKE"
    printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$f"
  log "RESULT $SPIKE: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L0-spike-$SPIKE.md"
  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}
wait_job() { # job timeout-seconds; succeeds only if the Job completes
  local end=$((SECONDS+$2)) s f
  while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
    s=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    f=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)
    [ "${s:-0}" -ge 1 ] && return 0; [ "${f:-0}" -ge 1 ] && return 1; sleep 1
  done; return 1
}
apply_yaml() { sed "s|__IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|g; s|__NS__|$NS|g" | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - ; }

. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
umask 077
D="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"; mkdir -p "$D"; chmod 700 "$SECRETS_DIR" "$D"

# Namespaces the certs must be valid in: the main one and the restore target (R5.1).
NAMESPACES="pg-ha pg-restore"
san="DNS:localhost,IP:127.0.0.1"
for ns in $NAMESPACES; do
  san="$san,DNS:*.pg-headless.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:*.pg-headless.$ns.svc"
  san="$san,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc"
done

if [ -s "$D/ca.key" ] && [ -s "$D/ca.crt" ]; then log "OK    CA exists, kept"
elif [ -e "$D/ca.key" ] || [ -e "$D/ca.crt" ]; then die "partial CA in $D, refusing to overwrite"
else

  openssl req -x509 -new -sha256 -key "$D/ca.key" -days 3650 -subj "/CN=[REDACTED-GCP-PROJECT] private CA" \
    -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE,pathlen:0" \
    -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" -out "$D/ca.crt"
  log "NEW   CA created"
fi

issue() { # name CN extendedKeyUsage SAN(optional)
  local n=$1 cn=$2 eku=$3 s=${4:-} ext
  if [ -s "$D/$n.key" ] && [ -s "$D/$n.crt" ]; then log "OK    $n exists, kept"; return; fi
  [ ! -e "$D/$n.key" ] && [ ! -e "$D/$n.crt" ] || die "partial $n in $D, refusing to overwrite"
  ext=$(mktemp)
  { echo "basicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE"; echo "keyUsage=critical,digitalSignature"
# Write probe (R3.7): every 500 ms, a new connection through pg-rw inserts one sequenced row.
# A row counts as acknowledged only when psql returns it. The client gives up after 3 s, so a commit
# blocked waiting for a standby is never counted. Each attempt runs in the background, keeping the
# 500 ms cadence while earlier attempts hang. Lines: ACK seq start_ts ack_ts server_ip | ERR seq start_ts end_ts
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: pg-probe}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg-probe}}
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}     # the probe must survive agent failures
      tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
      - name: probe
        image: __PG_IMAGE__
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
        env:
        - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
        - {name: RUN_ID, value: "__RUN_ID__"}
        - {name: DURATION, value: "__DURATION__"}
        - {name: CONN, value: "host=pg-rw.pg-ha.svc.cluster.local user=app dbname=app connect_timeout=2 keepalives=1 keepalives_idle=1 keepalives_interval=1 keepalives_count=2"}
        - name: PGPASSWORD
          valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-app-password}}
        command: [bash, -c]
        args:
        - |
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            psql "$CONN" -XAtq -c "create table if not exists probe (run text, seq bigint, client_ts timestamptz,
              server_ts timestamptz default clock_timestamp(), server_addr inet default inet_server_addr(),
              primary key (run, seq))" && break; sleep 1
          done
          echo "START $(date +%s.%N)"
          end=$(( $(date +%s) + DURATION )); i=0
          while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$end" ]; do
            i=$((i + 1))
            ( s=$(date +%s.%N)
              if out=$(timeout -s KILL 3 psql "$CONN" -XAtq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \
                   "insert into probe (run, seq, client_ts) values ('$RUN_ID', $i, to_timestamp($s)) returning host(server_addr)" 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$out" ]
              then echo "ACK $i $s $(date +%s.%N) $out"; else echo "ERR $i $s $(date +%s.%N)"; fi ) &
            sleep 0.5
          done
          wait
          echo "DONE $(date +%s.%N)"
        volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
      volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]

redact() {
  python3 -I -c '

data = sys.stdin.read()
for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(sys.argv[1], "*")):

}

ev_cleanup() {

section() { printf '\n## %s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; log "== $1"; }

  local out rc=0

note() { printf '\n%s\n' "$1" >> "$BODY"; }

  local end=$((SECONDS+$2)) s f

D="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"; mkdir -p "$D"; chmod 700 "$SECRETS_DIR" "$D"

for ns in $NAMESPACES; do

  san="$san,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-rw.$ns.svc,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc.cluster.local,DNS:pg-ro.$ns.svc"
done

elif [ -e "$D/ca.key" ] || [ -e "$D/ca.crt" ]; then die "partial CA in $D, refusing to overwrite"

    -addext "basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE,pathlen:0" \
    -addext "keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign" -out "$D/ca.crt"
  log "NEW   CA created"
fi

# Write probe (R3.7): every 500 ms, a new connection through pg-rw inserts one sequenced row.
# A row counts as acknowledged only when psql returns it. The client gives up after 3 s, so a commit
# blocked waiting for a standby is never counted. Each attempt runs in the background, keeping the
# 500 ms cadence while earlier attempts hang. Lines: ACK seq start_ts ack_ts server_ip | ERR seq start_ts end_ts
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: pg-probe}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 0
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg-probe}}
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}     # the probe must survive agent failures
      tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
      - name: probe
        image: __PG_IMAGE__
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}

        - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
        - {name: RUN_ID, value: "__RUN_ID__"}
        - {name: DURATION, value: "__DURATION__"}
        - {name: CONN, value: "host=pg-rw.pg-ha.svc.cluster.local user=app dbname=app connect_timeout=2 keepalives=1 keepalives_idle=1 keepalives_interval=1 keepalives_count=2"}

        command: [bash, -c]
        args:
        - |
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            psql "$CONN" -XAtq -c "create table if not exists probe (run text, seq bigint, client_ts timestamptz,
              server_ts timestamptz default clock_timestamp(), server_addr inet default inet_server_addr(),
              primary key (run, seq))" && break; sleep 1
          done
          echo "START $(date +%s.%N)"
          end=$(( $(date +%s) + DURATION )); i=0
          while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$end" ]; do
            i=$((i + 1))
            ( s=$(date +%s.%N)
              if out=$(timeout -s KILL 3 psql "$CONN" -XAtq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -c \
                   "insert into probe (run, seq, client_ts) values ('$RUN_ID', $i, to_timestamp($s)) returning host(server_addr)" 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$out" ]
              then echo "ACK $i $s $(date +%s.%N) $out"; else echo "ERR $i $s $(date +%s.%N)"; fi ) &
            sleep 0.5
          done
          wait
          echo "DONE $(date +%s.%N)"

      volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]

# L3: Garage object storage for the pgBackRest repository (ADR-014), productionised from spike S1.
# Single node, replication_factor 1, metadata and data fsync on. Rendered by scripts/garage.sh, which fills
# in the image. Secrets garage (RPC secret, admin and metrics tokens) and pgbackrest-repo come from ./secrets.
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: {name: garage-config}
data:
  garage.toml: |
    metadata_dir = "/data/meta"
    data_dir = "/data/blocks"
    db_engine = "lmdb"
    replication_factor = 1
    metadata_fsync = true
    data_fsync = true
    rpc_bind_addr = "[::]:3901"
    rpc_public_addr = "127.0.0.1:3901"
    [s3_api]
    s3_region = "garage"
    api_bind_addr = "[::]:3900"
    [admin]
    api_bind_addr = "[::]:3903"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata: {name: garage-data}
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: local-path
  resources: {requests: {storage: 5Gi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: garage}
spec:
  selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: garage}
  ports:
  - {name: s3, port: 3900}
  - {name: admin, port: 3903}
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: garage}
spec:
  replicas: 1
  strategy: {type: Recreate}          # one writer on the RWO volume
  selector: {matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: garage}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: garage}}
    spec:
      enableServiceLinks: false
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      # ADR-001: infrastructure runs on the tainted server, away from the database nodes.
      nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}
      tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 10001, runAsGroup: 10001, fsGroup: 10001, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
      containers:
      - name: garage
        image: __GARAGE_IMAGE__
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        envFrom: [{secretRef: {name: garage}}]
        ports:
        - {name: s3, containerPort: 3900}
        - {name: admin, containerPort: 3903}
        securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
        readinessProbe: {tcpSocket: {port: 3900}, periodSeconds: 2}
        resources: {requests: {cpu: 50m, memory: 64Mi}, limits: {memory: 512Mi}}
        volumeMounts:
        - {name: data, mountPath: /data}
        - {name: config, mountPath: /etc/garage.toml, subPath: garage.toml}
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim: {claimName: garage-data}
      - name: config
        configMap: {name: garage-config}
---
# Idempotent bootstrap through the Admin API v2: layout, imported key, bucket and grant. Every step checks
# first, so a rerun against an existing Garage changes nothing. Connect timeouts with retries bound the
# startup race found in S1 (docs/evidence/L0-spike-S1-history.md).
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: garage-bootstrap}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 2
  template:
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      automountServiceAccountToken: false

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploys Garage (ADR-014) into pg-ha and bootstraps it through the Admin API from a Job. Idempotent,
# and never prints a secret. Creates the Secrets garage and pgbackrest-repo from ./secrets.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || die "cluster $CLUSTER_NAME not found, run: make cluster"
C="$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"
for f in garage-rpc-secret garage-admin-token garage-metrics-token garage-s3-access-key-id garage-s3-secret-key pgbackrest-cipher-passphrase; do
  [ -s "$C/$f" ] || die "missing $C/$f, run: make secrets"
done
kubectl apply -f "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg/namespace.yaml" >/dev/null
secret() { kubectl -n "$PG_NS" create secret generic "$@" --dry-run=client -o yaml |
  kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-deploy --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null; }
secret garage --from-file=GARAGE_RPC_SECRET="$C/garage-rpc-secret" \
  --from-file=GARAGE_ADMIN_TOKEN="$C/garage-admin-token" --from-file=GARAGE_METRICS_TOKEN="$C/garage-metrics-token"
# pgBackRest reads these as environment variables, so no credential is ever written to repo.conf (ADR-009).
secret pgbackrest-repo --from-file=PGBACKREST_REPO1_S3_KEY="$C/garage-s3-access-key-id" \
  --from-file=PGBACKREST_REPO1_S3_KEY_SECRET="$C/garage-s3-secret-key" \
  --from-file=PGBACKREST_REPO1_CIPHER_PASS="$C/pgbackrest-cipher-passphrase"

# Jobs are immutable, so the bootstrap Job is replaced on every deploy. It is idempotent.
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" delete job garage-bootstrap --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
sed "s|__GARAGE_IMAGE__|$GARAGE_IMAGE|; s|__CURL_IMAGE__|$CURL_IMAGE|" "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/garage/garage.yaml" |
  kubectl -n "$PG_NS" apply -f -
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" rollout status deploy/garage --timeout=180s
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" wait --for=condition=Complete job/garage-bootstrap --timeout=180s >/dev/null ||
  { kubectl -n "$PG_NS" logs job/garage-bootstrap --tail=20 || true; die "garage-bootstrap did not complete"; }
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" logs job/garage-bootstrap

#!/bin/bash
# Backup CronJob body (ADR-009): full backup, then expire, then verify. Exits non-zero unless verify
# reports status ok, because verify can exit 0 while reporting status error (L0 finding, spike S1).
set -euo pipefail
S=main
say() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*"; }
say "full backup"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --type=full --log-level-console=info backup | grep -E 'backup command (begin|end)|new backup label|full backup size|backup start archive|INFO: (check|execute)' || true
# pipefail would hide a backup failure behind grep's status, so check the result explicitly.
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --output=json info | grep -q '"type":"full"'
say "expire (repo1-retention-full from repo.conf, or PGBACKREST_REPO1_RETENTION_FULL for a test)"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info expire | grep -E 'expire|remove' || true
say "verify"
rc=0; V=$(pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info --verbose verify 2>&1) || rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -E 'status:|archiveId:|backup:|checksum invalid|size invalid|missing|other' | sed -E 's/^[0-9-]+ [0-9:.]+ +P[0-9]+ +[A-Z]+: //; s/^ +//'
if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || ! grep -q 'status: ok' <<<"$V" || grep -q 'status: error' <<<"$V"; then
  say "VERIFY_FAILED (exit $rc)"; exit 1
fi
say VERIFY_OK
pgbackrest --stanza=$S info
say BACKUP_JOB_OK
EOF
cat > backup-cronjob.yaml <<'EOF'
# L3 (ADR-009): scheduled full backup, expire and verify, from the repository host role. The schedule is
# filled in by scripts/deploy.sh from BACKUP_SCHEDULE (default daily 20:00 UTC). make backup creates a Job
# from this same template.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata: {name: pg-backup}
spec:
  schedule: "__BACKUP_SCHEDULE__"
  timeZone: Etc/UTC
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid           # pgBackRest holds a stanza lock; never run two
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 0
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600
      template:
        metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg-backup}}
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          enableServiceLinks: false
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: db}
          securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, fsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: __PG_IMAGE__
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              command: [bash, /scripts/backup-job.sh]
              env:
                - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
              envFrom:
                - secretRef: {name: pgbackrest-repo}
              securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
              resources:
                requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}
                limits: {memory: 512Mi}
              volumeMounts:
                - {name: config, mountPath: /etc/pgbackrest, readOnly: true}
                - {name: tls, mountPath: /etc/pgbackrest-tls, readOnly: true}
                - {name: scripts, mountPath: /scripts, readOnly: true}
                - {name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}
          volumes:
            - name: config
              configMap:
                name: pg-pgbackrest
                items:
                  - {key: job.conf, path: pgbackrest.conf}
                  - {key: repo.conf, path: conf.d/repo.conf}
            - name: tls
              secret: {secretName: pgbackrest-tls, defaultMode: 0440}
            - name: scripts
              configMap: {name: pg-scripts, defaultMode: 0555}
            - {name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}
EOF
sed -i 's|    files: \[scripts/post-bootstrap.sh\]|    files: [scripts/post-bootstrap.sh, scripts/backup-job.sh]|' kustomization.yaml
grep -n "files:" kustomization.yaml

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploys Garage (L3), the Patroni cluster (L1) with WAL archiving (L3), and creates the pgBackRest stanza.
# Waits until healthy. Idempotent, and never prints a secret.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
cluster_exists || die "cluster $CLUSTER_NAME not found, run: make cluster"
C="$SECRETS_DIR/credentials"; T="$SECRETS_DIR/tls"
for f in "$C"/pg-{postgres,replicator,rewind,monitor,backup,app,app_ro}-password \
         "$T"/{ca.crt,postgres-server.crt,postgres-server.key,pgbackrest-server.crt,pgbackrest-server.key,pgbackrest-client.crt,pgbackrest-client.key}; do
  [ -s "$f" ] || die "missing $f, run: make certs secrets"
done
BACKUP_SCHEDULE=${BACKUP_SCHEDULE:-0 20 * * *}   # ADR-009: daily at 20:00 UTC unless overridden
[[ "$BACKUP_SCHEDULE" =~ ^[0-9*/,-]+( [0-9*/,-]+){4}$ ]] || die "BACKUP_SCHEDULE must be a 5-field cron expression"

# L3: Garage first, so WAL archiving has somewhere to go as soon as Postgres starts (ADR-014).
"$ROOT_DIR/scripts/garage.sh"

kubectl apply -f "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg/namespace.yaml" >/dev/null
# Server-side apply keeps secret values out of the last-applied annotation.
secret() { kubectl -n "$PG_NS" create secret generic "$@" --dry-run=client -o yaml |
  kubectl apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-deploy --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null; }
secret pg-credentials $(for r in postgres replicator rewind monitor backup app app_ro; do printf -- '--from-file=%s ' "$C/pg-$r-password"; done)
secret pg-tls --from-file=tls.crt="$T/postgres-server.crt" --from-file=tls.key="$T/postgres-server.key" --from-file=ca.crt="$T/ca.crt"
secret pgbackrest-tls --from-file=server.crt="$T/pgbackrest-server.crt" --from-file=server.key="$T/pgbackrest-server.key" \
  --from-file=client.crt="$T/pgbackrest-client.crt" --from-file=client.key="$T/pgbackrest-client.key" --from-file=ca.crt="$T/ca.crt"
kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/pg" | sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|; s|__BACKUP_SCHEDULE__|$BACKUP_SCHEDULE|" | kubectl apply -f -

kubectl -n "$PG_NS" rollout status "statefulset/$PG_STS" --timeout=600s
end=$((SECONDS + ${PG_WAIT:-180}))
until patroni_healthy; do
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "\(.name) \(.role) \(.state)"' || true; die "Patroni not healthy after ${PG_WAIT:-180} s"; }
  sleep 2
done
log "Patroni healthy: 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas, 1 sync standby"

# L3: create the stanza (idempotent), then prove that archiving reaches the repository.
out=$(JOB_WAIT=300 "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/pgbr-job.sh" pg-stanza-create \
  'pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info stanza-create && pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info check && echo STANZA_OK') ||
  { printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -20; die "stanza-create or check failed"; }
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -E 'stanza-create command end|check command end|already exists|STANZA_OK' || true
log "Backup schedule: $BACKUP_SCHEDULE (UTC)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the L3 backup tests. Each test writes docs/evidence/L3/<part>.md and then regenerates
# docs/evidence/L3-backup.md. Repository commands run in Jobs made from the pg-backup CronJob template
# (scripts/pgbr-job.sh), never by exec. SQL runs in the test client pod, as in L1 and L2.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/lib.sh"
mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L3"
pgbr() { JOB_WAIT=${JOB_WAIT:-900} "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/pgbr-job.sh" "$@"; }
# pgBackRest info as JSON, from a short Job. Prints only the JSON line.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L3 R4.1: evidence of a truly scheduled backup. Redeploys with BACKUP_SCHEDULE set to every 10 minutes,
# waits for a Job that the CronJob controller created itself (not one made from it by hand), requires it
# to complete with verify status ok, then redeploys with the default schedule and confirms it.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l3-lib.sh"
SHORT=${SHORT_SCHEDULE:-*/10 * * * *}; DEFAULT="0 20 * * *"
section "Short schedule for the evidence run"
BACKUP_SCHEDULE="$SHORT" "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/deploy.sh" >/dev/null
run "kubectl -n $NS get cronjob pg-backup -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,SCHEDULE:.spec.schedule,TZ:.spec.timeZone,LAST:.status.lastScheduleTime" || true
T_SET=$(date +%s); note "Schedule set to \`$SHORT\` (UTC) at $(date -u -d "@$T_SET" +%H:%M:%S) UTC."

# A scheduled Job has the CronJob as its owner and lacks the cronjob.kubernetes.io/instantiate=manual annotation.
scheduled_job() {
  kubectl -n "$NS" get jobs -o json | jq -r --argjson t "$T_SET" '.items[]
    | select(any(.metadata.ownerReferences[]?; .kind == "CronJob" and .name == "pg-backup"))
    | select((.metadata.annotations["cronjob.kubernetes.io/instantiate"] // "") != "manual")
    | select((.metadata.creationTimestamp | fromdateiso8601) >= $t) | .metadata.name' | head -1; }
J=""; end=$((SECONDS + 900))
until J=$(scheduled_job) && [ -n "$J" ]; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || break; sleep 5; done
ok=0
if [ -n "$J" ]; then
  until s=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$J" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}/{.status.failed}'); [ "${s%/*}" = 1 ] || [ "${s#*/}" = 1 ] || [ $SECONDS -ge $end ]; do sleep 3; done
  [ "${s%/*}" = 1 ] && ok=1
  section "The scheduled Job"
  run "kubectl -n $NS get job $J -o json | jq -r '{name: .metadata.name, created: .metadata.creationTimestamp, owner: [.metadata.ownerReferences[] | .kind + \"/\" + .name][0], manual: (.metadata.annotations[\"cronjob.kubernetes.io/instantiate\"] // \"no\"), scheduled_at: (.metadata.annotations[\"batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp\"] // \"-\"), completed: .status.completionTime, succeeded: .status.succeeded}'" || true
  TAIL=40 run "kubectl -n $NS logs job/$J | grep -vE 'command begin'" || true
fi
check "The CronJob controller created a Job on the short schedule (not a manual Job)" test -n "$J"
check "The scheduled Job completed" test $ok = 1
check "Its verify reported status ok" bash -c "kubectl -n $NS logs job/$J | grep -q VERIFY_OK"

section "Default schedule restored"
"$ROOT_DIR/scripts/deploy.sh" >/dev/null
run "kubectl -n $NS get cronjob pg-backup -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,SCHEDULE:.spec.schedule,TZ:.spec.timeZone,LAST:.status.lastScheduleTime" || true
check "Schedule restored to the default ($DEFAULT UTC)" test "$(kubectl -n "$NS" get cronjob pg-backup -o jsonpath='{.spec.schedule}')" = "$DEFAULT"
l3_finish scheduled "Scheduled backup (R4.1)" "BACKUP_SCHEDULE set to \`$SHORT\` through \`make deploy\`, one Job created by the CronJob controller itself runs full backup, expire and verify, then the default \`$DEFAULT\` (UTC) is restored." test-backup-schedule

SHORT=${SHORT_SCHEDULE:-*/10 * * * *}; DEFAULT="0 20 * * *"
section "Short schedule for the evidence run"
BACKUP_SCHEDULE="$SHORT" "$ROOT_DIR/scripts/deploy.sh" >/dev/null
run "kubectl -n $NS get cronjob pg-backup -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,SCHEDULE:.spec.schedule,TZ:.spec.timeZone,LAST:.status.lastScheduleTime" || true
T_SET=$(date +%s); note "Schedule set to \`$SHORT\` (UTC) at $(date -u -d "@$T_SET" +%H:%M:%S) UTC."

# A scheduled Job has the CronJob as its owner and lacks the cronjob.kubernetes.io/instantiate=manual annotation.
scheduled_job() {
  kubectl -n "$NS" get jobs -o json | jq -r --argjson t "$T_SET" '.items[]
    | select(any(.metadata.ownerReferences[]?; .kind == "CronJob" and .name == "pg-backup"))
    | select((.metadata.annotations["cronjob.kubernetes.io/instantiate"] // "") != "manual")
    | select((.metadata.creationTimestamp | fromdateiso8601) >= $t) | .metadata.name' | head -1; }
J=""; end=$((SECONDS + 900))
until J=$(scheduled_job) && [ -n "$J" ]; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || break; sleep 5; done
ok=0
if [ -n "$J" ]; then
  until s=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job "$J" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}/{.status.failed}'); [ "${s%/*}" = 1 ] || [ "${s#*/}" = 1 ] || [ $SECONDS -ge $end ]; do sleep 3; done
  [ "${s%/*}" = 1 ] && ok=1
  section "The scheduled Job"
  run "kubectl -n $NS get job $J -o json | jq -r '{name: .metadata.name, created: .metadata.creationTimestamp, owner: [.metadata.ownerReferences[] | .kind + \"/\" + .name][0], manual: (.metadata.annotations[\"cronjob.kubernetes.io/instantiate\"] // \"no\"), scheduled_at: (.metadata.annotations[\"batch.kubernetes.io/cronjob-scheduled-timestamp\"] // \"-\"), completed: .status.completionTime, succeeded: .status.succeeded}'" || true
  TAIL=40 run "kubectl -n $NS logs job/$J | grep -vE 'command begin'" || true
fi
check "The CronJob controller created a Job on the short schedule (not a manual Job)" test -n "$J"
check "The scheduled Job completed" test $ok = 1
check "Its verify reported status ok" bash -c "kubectl -n $NS logs job/$J | grep -q VERIFY_OK"

section "Default schedule restored"
"$ROOT_DIR/scripts/deploy.sh" >/dev/null
run "kubectl -n $NS get cronjob pg-backup -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,SCHEDULE:.spec.schedule,TZ:.spec.timeZone,LAST:.status.lastScheduleTime" || true
check "Schedule restored to the default ($DEFAULT UTC)" test "$(kubectl -n "$NS" get cronjob pg-backup -o jsonpath='{.spec.schedule}')" = "$DEFAULT"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L2 failure harness (R3.1-R3.7, R6.3, ADR-006). Usage: tests/failover.sh pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover
#   RUNS=n (default 3, switchover 1), TO=pg-N (switchover target, default the current sync standby)
#
# RTO = fault injection to the first commit acknowledged by a new primary, seen by the probe Job
# (tests/probe-job.yaml), which writes through pg-rw every 500 ms. RPO = acknowledged sequence numbers
# missing on the new primary. Leadership is sampled twice every 500 ms: the lock holder from the pg-rw
# Endpoints object, and pg_is_in_recovery() asked of each member directly.
  printf -- '- **Method:** RTO is fault injection to the first commit acknowledged by a new primary, from a probe writing through pg-rw every 500 ms. Write gap is the last acknowledged write before that to the first after it. RPO counts acknowledged rows missing on the new primary.\n'
  printf '\n## Summary\n\n%s\n\nRTO: %s. Target 30 s.\n\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n' "$(cat "$SUMMARY")" "$STATS"
  cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_FILE"

"$ROOT_DIR/tests/l2-summary.sh"
log "RESULT L2 $MODE: $verdict ($STATS) -> docs/evidence/L2/$MODE.md"
[ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]

open(p,'w').write(s)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L3: Garage, pgBackRest configuration, WAL archiving, stanza and an on-demand backup with verify.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l3-lib.sh"
client_up

section "Garage (ADR-014)"
run "kubectl -n $NS get deploy,pvc,svc -l app.kubernetes.io/name=garage -o wide; kubectl -n $NS get pvc garage-data; kubectl -n $NS get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=garage -o custom-columns=POD:.metadata.name,NODE:.spec.nodeName,READY:.status.containerStatuses[0].ready,IMAGE:.spec.containers[0].image" || true
check "Garage is Ready on the infra node with its PVC bound" bash -c "kubectl -n $NS rollout status deploy/garage --timeout=60s && test \"\$(kubectl -n $NS get pvc garage-data -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}')\" = Bound"
check "Garage runs single node with metadata and data fsync on" bash -c "kubectl -n $NS get cm garage-config -o jsonpath='{.data.garage\.toml}' | grep -qx 'metadata_fsync = true' && kubectl -n $NS get cm garage-config -o jsonpath='{.data.garage\.toml}' | grep -qx 'data_fsync = true' && kubectl -n $NS get cm garage-config -o jsonpath='{.data.garage\.toml}' | grep -qx 'replication_factor = 1'"
BOOT=$("$ROOT_DIR/scripts/garage.sh" 2>&1 | tail -6) || true
run "printf '%s\n' \"\$BOOT\"" || true
check "Bootstrap Job is idempotent: a rerun keeps layout, key and bucket" bash -c "grep -q 'layout: version 1 exists, kept' <<<\"\$0\" && grep -q 'key: exists, kept' <<<\"\$0\" && grep -q 'bucket: exists, kept' <<<\"\$0\" && grep -q BOOTSTRAP_OK <<<\"\$0\"" "$BOOT"

section "pgBackRest configuration (ADR-009)"
run "cat deploy/pg/pgbackrest/repo.conf | grep -v '^#'" || true
run "grep -rnE '^[[:space:]]*repo1-|--repo1-' deploy scripts tests --exclude=repo.conf --exclude-dir=spikes || echo 'no repo1-* setting outside repo.conf'" || true
check "No repo1-* setting outside repo.conf (config lines or CLI options)" bash -c "! grep -rqE '^[[:space:]]*repo1-|--repo1-' deploy scripts tests --exclude=repo.conf --exclude-dir=spikes"
check "No credential value in any rendered manifest or ConfigMap" bash -c "kubectl kustomize deploy/pg > /tmp/l3-render.yaml && kubectl kustomize deploy/pg >/dev/null && python3 -I -c '
import glob, sys; d = open(\"/tmp/l3-render.yaml\").read() + open(\"deploy/garage/garage.yaml\").read()
sys.exit(any(open(p).read().strip() and open(p).read().strip() in d for p in glob.glob(\"secrets/credentials/*\")))'; rc=\$?; rm -f /tmp/l3-render.yaml; exit \$rc"
check "Repository encryption is aes-256-cbc, with the passphrase only in a Secret" bash -c "grep -qx 'repo1-cipher-type=aes-256-cbc' deploy/pg/pgbackrest/repo.conf && kubectl -n $NS get secret pgbackrest-repo -o jsonpath='{.data.PGBACKREST_REPO1_CIPHER_PASS}' | grep -q ."
check "Jobs list pg1..pg3 by headless-service DNS over TLS" bash -c "test \$(grep -cE '^pg[123]-host=pg-[012]\.pg-headless\.pg-ha\.svc\.cluster\.local$' deploy/pg/pgbackrest/job.conf) = 3 && test \$(grep -c '^pg[123]-host-type=tls$' deploy/pg/pgbackrest/job.conf) = 3"
check "Archiving is asynchronous with a 2 GiB queue cap (ADR-005)" bash -c "grep -qx 'archive-async=y' deploy/pg/pgbackrest/db.conf && grep -qx 'archive-push-queue-max=2GiB' deploy/pg/pgbackrest/db.conf"

section "WAL archiving (Patroni conf.d/20-archive.yml)"
run "q $RW monitor \"select name, setting from pg_settings where name in ('archive_mode','archive_command','archive_timeout','restore_command','ssl') order by 1\"" || true
S=$(q "$RW" monitor "select string_agg(name || '=' || setting, ' ') from pg_settings where name in ('archive_mode','archive_command','restore_command','ssl')")
check "archive_mode on with archive-push, restore_command via archive-get, and 10-base.yml settings kept (ssl on)" bash -c "grep -q 'archive_mode=on' <<<\"\$0\" && grep -q 'archive-push' <<<\"\$0\" && grep -q 'archive-get' <<<\"\$0\" && grep -q 'ssl=on' <<<\"\$0\"" "$S"
A0=$(archiver); T_A=$(date +%s)
run "q $RW monitor 'select archived_count, failed_count, last_archived_wal, last_archived_time, last_failed_wal, last_failed_time from pg_stat_archiver'" || true
STANZA_T=$(kubectl -n "$NS" get job pg-stanza-create -o jsonpath='{.status.startTime}' 2>/dev/null | xargs -r -I{} date -d {} +%s)
note "Failures counted before the stanza existed are expected: Postgres starts archiving before the stanza Job runs and retries each segment until it succeeds. The checks below therefore require that no failure happened after the stanza was created, and none during this test."
AT=$(archived_after "$T_A" 120) || AT=""
A1=$(archiver)
run "q $RW monitor 'select archived_count, failed_count, last_archived_wal, last_archived_time, last_failed_wal, last_failed_time from pg_stat_archiver'" || true
check "A new WAL segment was archived within 120 s (archive_timeout 60 s)" test -n "$AT"
check "pg_stat_archiver: no new failures during the test" test "$(awk '{print $2}' <<<"$A0")" = "$(awk '{print $2}' <<<"$A1")"
check "pg_stat_archiver: last failure (if any) is older than the stanza creation" awk -v f="$(awk '{print $5}' <<<"$A1")" -v s="${STANZA_T:-0}" 'BEGIN{exit !(f < s)}'

section "Stanza (idempotent) and pgbackrest check, from Jobs over TLS"
TAIL=8 run "JOB_WAIT=300 scripts/pgbr-job.sh pg-stanza-create 'pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info stanza-create && pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info check && echo STANZA_OK' | grep -vE 'command begin'" && st=1 || st=0
check "stanza-create reruns cleanly on the existing stanza, and pgbackrest check passes" test $st = 1

section "On-demand backup: make backup (full, expire, verify)"
B=pg-backup-manual-$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S)
TAIL=30 run "scripts/pgbr-job.sh $B | grep -vE 'command begin'" && bk=1 || bk=0
check "make backup completed: full backup, expire, verify status ok" bash -c "test $bk = 1 && kubectl -n $NS logs job/$B | grep -q VERIFY_OK"
check "The backup job script fails unless verify reports status ok (not only exit 0)" grep -q "grep -q 'status: ok'" deploy/pg/scripts/backup-job.sh
kubectl -n "$NS" delete job "$B" pg-stanza-create --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
l3_finish archive "Garage, pgBackRest, archiving and on-demand backup" "Garage from our manifests with an idempotent Admin API bootstrap, pgBackRest with every repo1-* setting in repo.conf and an encrypted repository, async WAL archiving added as Patroni conf.d/20-archive.yml, stanza and check as a Job over the TLS server, and \`make backup\` (full, expire, verify)." test-archive

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L3 R4.3: retention enforcement. Three backups run from the CronJob template with a temporary retention of
# 2 fulls, given only to those test Jobs as PGBACKREST_REPO1_RETENTION_FULL (repo.conf is never edited).
# Proves the older backups are expired with their WAL, then that a normal run uses repo.conf's 7 again.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l3-lib.sh"
client_up
labels() { jq -r '.[0].backup[].label' <<<"$1"; }
amin() { jq -r '[.[0].archive[] | .min] | min' <<<"$1"; }
start_of() { jq -r --arg l "$2" '.[0].backup[] | select(.label == $l) | .archive.start' <<<"$1"; }

section "Before"
I0=$(pgbr_info); run "jq -r '.[0].backup[] | .label + \"  wal \" + .archive.start + \"..\" + .archive.stop' <<<'$I0'; echo \"archive min: $(amin "$I0")\"" || true
OLDEST_BEFORE=$(labels "$I0" | head -1)

section "Three backups with a temporary retention of 2 fulls"
NEW=()
for n in 1 2 3; do
  J=pg-backup-ret-$n
  pgbr "$J" "" PGBACKREST_REPO1_RETENTION_FULL=2 > "$BODY.job" 2>&1 && ok=1 || ok=0
  L=$(sed -nE 's/.*new backup label = ([0-9F-]+).*/\1/p' "$BODY.job"); NEW+=("$L")
  run "grep -E 'new backup label|expire|remove|VERIFY_OK|VERIFY_FAILED' $BODY.job | grep -vE 'command (begin|end)' | sed -E 's/^[0-9-]+ [0-9:.]+ +P[0-9]+ +//'" || true
  check "Backup $n ($L) completed with verify status ok" bash -c "test $ok = 1 && grep -q VERIFY_OK $BODY.job"
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job "$J" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  # Some WAL between backups, so expiring a backup has archive to remove with it.
  [ $n = 3 ] || archived_after "$(date +%s)" 120 >/dev/null || true
done
rm -f "$BODY.job"

section "After"
I1=$(pgbr_info); run "jq -r '.[0].backup[] | .label + \"  wal \" + .archive.start + \"..\" + .archive.stop' <<<'$I1'; echo \"archive min: $(amin "$I1")\"" || true
LEFT=$(labels "$I1" | tr '\n' ' '); WANT="${NEW[1]} ${NEW[2]} "
note "Labels before: \`$(labels "$I0" | tr '\n' ' ')\`. New: \`${NEW[*]}\`. Left after expire: \`$LEFT\`. Archive min before \`$(amin "$I0")\`, after \`$(amin "$I1")\`. Start WAL of the expired backup ${NEW[0]}: \`$(start_of "$I1" "${NEW[0]}")$(start_of "$I0" "${NEW[0]}")\`, of the oldest kept ${NEW[1]}: \`$(start_of "$I1" "${NEW[1]}")\`."
check "Exactly the 2 newest fulls remain" test "$LEFT" = "$WANT"
check "The oldest backup from before the test ($OLDEST_BEFORE) and backup 1 (${NEW[0]}) were expired" bash -c "! grep -qw '$OLDEST_BEFORE' <<<'$LEFT' && ! grep -qw '${NEW[0]}' <<<'$LEFT'"
check "WAL older than the oldest kept backup was expired with it (archive min = its start WAL)" test "$(amin "$I1")" = "$(start_of "$I1" "${NEW[1]}")"
check "Archive min moved forward" bash -c "[[ '$(amin "$I1")' > '$(amin "$I0")' ]]"

section "Real setting in force again"
run "grep -h retention deploy/pg/pgbackrest/*.conf; kubectl -n $NS get cronjob pg-backup -o json | jq -c '[.spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[] | .name]'" || true
check "repo.conf still says repo1-retention-full=7 and the CronJob sets no retention override" bash -c "grep -qx 'repo1-retention-full=7' deploy/pg/pgbackrest/repo.conf && ! kubectl -n $NS get cronjob pg-backup -o json | grep -q RETENTION"
pgbr pg-backup-ret-normal > "$BODY.job" 2>&1 && ok=1 || ok=0
kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-backup-ret-normal --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
I2=$(pgbr_info); rm -f "$BODY.job"
run "jq -r '.[0].backup[] | .label' <<<'$I2'" || true
check "A normal run (retention 7) keeps all 3 fulls" test "$(labels "$I2" | wc -l)" = 3 -a $ok = 1
l3_finish retention "Retention enforcement" "Three full backups from the CronJob template with a temporary \`PGBACKREST_REPO1_RETENTION_FULL=2\` on those Jobs only, proving the oldest fulls and their WAL are expired, then a normal run with repo.conf's \`repo1-retention-full=7\` keeping every full." test-retention

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L3 R4.6: backup after failover. Runs one L2 node failover (stop the primary's k3d agent, restart it), with
# its evidence written under L3/ so the L2 results stay as they are. Then requires that archiving continues
# on the new timeline with no failures on the new primary, that pgbackrest check passes, and that a backup
# with verify succeeds from the new primary with no config change.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l3-lib.sh"
client_up
tl() { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline'; }
OLD=$(leader); TL0=$(tl)
section "Failover: one node-stop run of the L2 harness"
note "Before: leader \`$OLD\`, timeline $TL0. The full failover evidence is in [\`failover-node-run.md\`](failover-node-run.md)."
RUNS=1 EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L3/failover-node-run.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" node > "$BODY.fo" 2>&1 && fo=1 || fo=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $BODY.fo" || true; rm -f "$BODY.fo"
check "Node failover run passed (RTO, RPO 0, one primary, old primary rejoined)" test $fo = 1
client_up
NEW=$(leader); TL1=$(tl); TLX=$(printf '%08X' "$TL1"); T_AFTER=$(date +%s)
note "After: leader \`$NEW\`, timeline $TL1 (WAL prefix \`$TLX\`)."
check "Leadership moved to another member on a higher timeline" test "$NEW" != "$OLD" -a "$TL1" -gt "$TL0"

section "Archiving on the new timeline"
A0=$(archiver); AT=$(archived_after "$T_AFTER" 150) || AT=""; A1=$(archiver)
run "q $RW monitor 'select inet_server_addr(), archived_count, failed_count, last_archived_wal, last_archived_time, last_failed_wal, last_failed_time from pg_stat_archiver'" || true
check "The new primary archived a segment within 150 s" test -n "$AT"
check "The latest archived segment is on the new timeline ($TLX)" bash -c "[[ '$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$A1")' == $TLX* ]]"
check "No archive failures on the new primary during the check" test "$(awk '{print $2}' <<<"$A0")" = "$(awk '{print $2}' <<<"$A1")"
TAIL=6 run "JOB_WAIT=300 scripts/pgbr-job.sh pg-check-after-failover 'pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info check && echo CHECK_OK' | grep -vE 'command begin'" && ck=1 || ck=0
check "pgbackrest check passes against the new primary" test $ck = 1

section "Backup and verify after failover (no config change)"
B=pg-backup-after-failover
TAIL=30 run "scripts/pgbr-job.sh $B | grep -vE 'command begin'" && bk=1 || bk=0
START=$(kubectl -n "$NS" logs "job/$B" 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's/.*backup start archive = ([0-9A-F]{24}).*/\1/p')
check "Backup completed with verify status ok" bash -c "test $bk = 1 && kubectl -n $NS logs job/$B | grep -q VERIFY_OK"
check "The backup started on the new timeline ($TLX), so it was taken from the new primary" bash -c "[[ '$START' == $TLX* ]]"
