tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L2 failure harness (R3.1-R3.7, R6.3, ADR-006). Usage: tests/failover.sh pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover
#   RUNS=n (default 3, switchover 1), TO=pg-N (switchover target, default the current sync standby)
#   EV_OUT=path writes the evidence there instead of docs/evidence/L2/<mode>.md, and leaves L2-failover.md alone
#   (used by L3 to fault the cluster without replacing the L2 results).
#
# RTO = fault injection to the first commit acknowledged by a new primary, seen by the probe Job
# (tests/probe-job.yaml), which writes through pg-rw every 500 ms. RPO = acknowledged sequence numbers
# missing on the new primary. Leadership is sampled twice every 500 ms: the lock holder from the pg-rw
# Endpoints object, and pg_is_in_recovery() asked of each member directly.
#
# Fault injection (D4, committed and documented):
#   pod          kubectl delete pod <primary> (default grace period, so Patroni shuts down normally)
#   node         docker stop <agent hosting the primary>, then docker start once a new leader holds the lock
#   storage      docker exec <agent>: lazily unmount /data inside the primary container's mount namespace, so
#                the volume is gone from that container, then SIGKILL the postmaster, standing in for the
#                I/O error a lost disk causes. Restored by deleting the pod once a new leader holds the lock,
#                so the kubelet mounts the volume again. See the evidence file for the limits.
#   split-brain  docker exec <agent> iptables: drop the primary pod's traffic to the API server backend only.
#                Pod-to-pod traffic, including replication, is untouched. The rule is removed afterwards.
#   switchover   POST /switchover to the leader's Patroni REST API over kubectl port-forward and curl
#                (the REST API is unauthenticated until L6). The API server pod proxy is not used for this
#                POST because Patroni rejects its request without a Content-Length header (HTTP 411).
# psql runs only in the test client pod, never in a Postgres pod.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
MODE=${1:-}; case "$MODE" in pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover) ;; *) die "usage: $0 pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover" ;; esac
RUNS=${RUNS:-$([ "$MODE" = switchover ] && echo 1 || echo 3)}
[[ "$RUNS" =~ ^[1-9]$ ]] || die "RUNS must be 1-9"
case "$MODE" in pod) DURATION=70 ;; switchover) DURATION=50 ;; *) DURATION=110 ;; esac
W=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L2"; EV_FILE="${EV_OUT:-$EV_DIR/L2/$MODE.md}"
PENDING_RESTORE=""; SAMPLER_PIDS=""

restore_fault() {
  case "$PENDING_RESTORE" in
    node:*) docker start "${PENDING_RESTORE#node:}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
    storage:*) kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "${PENDING_RESTORE#storage:}" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
    split:*) set -- ${PENDING_RESTORE#split:}; docker exec "$1" iptables -D FORWARD -s "$2" -d "$3" -p tcp --dport "$4" -j DROP >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
  esac
  PENDING_RESTORE=""
}
stop_samplers() { [ -z "$SAMPLER_PIDS" ] || kill $SAMPLER_PIDS 2>/dev/null || true; wait $SAMPLER_PIDS 2>/dev/null || true; SAMPLER_PIDS=""; }
cleanup() {
  restore_fault; stop_samplers
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$CLIENT" --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -rf "$W" "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

wait_until() { # timeout-seconds command...
  local end=$((SECONDS + $1)); shift
  until "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || return 1; sleep 0.5; done
}
leader_is_not() { local l; l=$(leader); [ -n "$l" ] && [ "$l" != "$1" ]; }
leader_is() { [ "$(leader)" = "$1" ]; }
pod_uid() { kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$1" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}' 2>/dev/null; }
uid_changed() { local u; u=$(pod_uid "$1"); [ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" != "$2" ]; }
ts_of_log() { # "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm" or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm UTC" at line start -> epoch
  sed -E 's/^([0-9-]+ [0-9:]+)[.,]([0-9]+).*/\1.\2 UTC/' | head -1 | xargs -r -I{} date -d {} +%s.%N
}
container_pid() { # agent pod -> host-visible PID of the Postgres container, via crictl on that node
  local id; id=$(docker exec "$1" crictl ps -q --name postgres --label "io.kubernetes.pod.name=$2" --label "io.kubernetes.pod.namespace=$NS")
  docker exec "$1" crictl inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$id"
}

client_up
kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "namespace $NS not found, run: make up"
SUMMARY=$(mktemp -p "$W")
printf '| Run | Old primary | New primary | RTO (s) | Write gap (s) | Acked | RPO (acked rows missing) | Max primaries in one sample | Rejoin | Rejoin after fault (s) | Result |\n|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|\n' > "$SUMMARY"
RTOS=""

for N in $(seq 1 "$RUNS"); do
  R="$W/run$N"; mkdir -p "$R"; run_fails=$FAILS
  section "Run $N"
  wait_until 240 primary_confirms || die "cluster not healthy before run $N, see: make status"
  sleep 3
  OLD=$(leader); OLD_IP=$(pod_ip "$OLD"); OLD_NODE=$(pod_node "$OLD"); OLD_UID=$(pod_uid "$OLD")
  SYNC=$(sync_standby); TL0=$(patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline')
  TARGET=${TO:-$SYNC}
  [ "$MODE" != switchover ] || [ "$TARGET" != "$OLD" ] || die "switchover target $TARGET is already the leader"
  RUN_ID="$MODE-$N-$(date +%s)"

  # Probe, then samplers. Nothing is deployed or reconfigured during the measured window.
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
  sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|; s|__RUN_ID__|$RUN_ID|; s|__DURATION__|$DURATION|" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/probe-job.yaml" | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - >/dev/null
  wait_until 90 bash -c "[ \$(kubectl -n $NS logs job/pg-probe 2>/dev/null | grep -c '^ACK') -ge 6 ]" || die "probe did not start acknowledging writes"
  ( while :; do echo "L $(now) $(lock)"; sleep 0.5; done ) > "$R/lock.txt" 2>/dev/null & SAMPLER_PIDS="$!"
  kubectl -n "$NS" exec "$CLIENT" -- sh -c 'end=$(( $(date +%s) + 600 )); i=0
    while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$end" ]; do i=$((i+1))
      for m in pg-0 pg-1 pg-2; do ( r=$(PGPASSWORD=$MON_PW psql "host=$m.pg-headless.pg-ha.svc.cluster.local user=monitor dbname=app connect_timeout=2" -XAtqc "select pg_is_in_recovery()" 2>/dev/null) || r=x; echo "S $i $(date +%s.%N) $m ${r:-x}" ) & done
      sleep 0.5; done' > "$R/samples.txt" 2>/dev/null & SAMPLER_PIDS="$SAMPLER_PIDS $!"
  sleep 2

  # Fault.
  case "$MODE" in
    pod) T_FAULT=$(now); kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$OLD" --wait=false >/dev/null ;;
    node) T_FAULT=$(now); docker stop "$OLD_NODE" >/dev/null; PENDING_RESTORE="node:$OLD_NODE" ;;
    storage)
      PID=$(container_pid "$OLD_NODE" "$OLD")
      PM=$(docker exec "$OLD_NODE" sh -c "for d in /proc/[0-9]*; do [ \"\$(cut -d' ' -f4 \$d/stat 2>/dev/null)\" = $PID ] && [ \"\$(cat \$d/comm 2>/dev/null)\" = postgres ] && echo \${d#/proc/}; done; true" | head -1)
      [ -n "$PM" ] || die "postmaster of $OLD not found"
      T_FAULT=$(now); docker exec "$OLD_NODE" sh -c "nsenter -t $PID -m -p -- umount -l /data && kill -KILL $PM"
      PENDING_RESTORE="storage:$OLD" ;;
    split-brain)
      API=$(kubectl get endpointslice -n default -l kubernetes.io/service-name=kubernetes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].endpoints[0].addresses[0]} {.items[0].ports[0].port}')
      set -- $API; API_IP=$1; API_PORT=$2
      T_FAULT=$(now); docker exec "$OLD_NODE" iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s "$OLD_IP" -d "$API_IP" -p tcp --dport "$API_PORT" -j DROP
      PENDING_RESTORE="split:$OLD_NODE $OLD_IP $API_IP $API_PORT" ;;
    switchover)
      printf '{"leader": "%s", "candidate": "%s"}' "$OLD" "$TARGET" > "$R/body.json"
      PFPORT=$((18000 + RANDOM % 1000)); kubectl -n "$NS" port-forward "pod/$OLD" "$PFPORT:8008" >/dev/null 2>&1 & PF=$!
      wait_until 10 curl -s -o /dev/null "http://127.0.0.1:$PFPORT/liveness" || true
      T_FAULT=$(now); curl -sS -m 60 -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @"$R/body.json" "http://127.0.0.1:$PFPORT/switchover" > "$R/switchover.txt" 2>&1 || true
      kill $PF 2>/dev/null || true; wait $PF 2>/dev/null || true ;;
  esac
  note "Fault at $(iso "$T_FAULT") UTC on primary \`$OLD\` ($OLD_IP, node \`$OLD_NODE\`, timeline $TL0). Sync standby before: \`$SYNC\`."
  got=0; if [ "$MODE" = switchover ]; then wait_until 90 leader_is "$TARGET" || got=1; else wait_until 120 leader_is_not "$OLD" || got=1; fi
  T_LOCK=$(now); NEW=$(leader)
  check "run $N: lock moved from $OLD to a new leader ($NEW)" test $got = 0
  if [ "$MODE" = storage ]; then
    # Proof the volume was unavailable, taken from the old container before the pod is replaced.
    sleep 3; kubectl -n "$NS" logs "$OLD" --since-time="$(date -u -d "@${T_FAULT%.*}" +%FT%TZ)" > "$R/old-before-restore.log" 2>/dev/null || true
    run "grep -iE 'No such file|does not exist|not running|failed|crash|primary_start|releas|demot|promot' $R/old-before-restore.log | head -8" || true
  fi
  restore_fault; T_RESTORE=$(now)

  # Rejoin: a new pod where one is expected, then confirmed from the primary, not from Patroni alone.
  case "$MODE" in pod|storage) wait_until 180 uid_changed "$OLD" "$OLD_UID" || true ;; esac
  rj=0; wait_until 300 primary_confirms "$OLD" || rj=1; T_REJOIN=$(now)
  wait_until $((DURATION + 60)) bash -c "kubectl -n $NS logs job/pg-probe 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^DONE'" || true
  stop_samplers
  kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-probe > "$R/probe.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
  NEW_IP=$(pod_ip "$NEW")

  # Analysis.
  FIRST_NEW=$(awk -v ip="$OLD_IP" -v t="$T_FAULT" '$1=="ACK" && $5!=ip && $4>t {print $4}' "$R/probe.txt" | sort -n | head -1)
  LAST_OLD=$(awk -v ip="$OLD_IP" '$1=="ACK" && $5==ip {print $4}' "$R/probe.txt" | sort -n | tail -1)
  PREV=$(awk -v f="${FIRST_NEW:-0}" '$1=="ACK" && $4<f {print $4}' "$R/probe.txt" | sort -n | tail -1)
  RTO=$(secs "$T_FAULT" "$FIRST_NEW"); GAP=$(secs "$PREV" "$FIRST_NEW")
  OVERLAP=$(awk -v ip="$OLD_IP" -v f="${FIRST_NEW:-9e99}" '$1=="ACK" && $5==ip && $4>f' "$R/probe.txt" | wc -l)
  ACKED=$(awk '$1=="ACK" {print $2}' "$R/probe.txt" | sort -n | paste -sd, -)
  NACK=$(awk '$1=="ACK"' "$R/probe.txt" | wc -l); NERR=$(awk '$1=="ERR"' "$R/probe.txt" | wc -l)
  FOUND=$( [ -n "$ACKED" ] && q "$RW" app "select count(*) from probe where run = '$RUN_ID' and seq in ($ACKED)" || echo 0)
  MISSING=$((NACK - ${FOUND:-0}))
  MAXP=$(awk '$1=="S" && $5=="f" {c[$2]++} END {m=0; for (k in c) if (c[k]>m) m=c[k]; print m}' "$R/samples.txt")
  NTICKS=$(awk '$1=="S" {print $2}' "$R/samples.txt" | sort -u | wc -l)
  HOLDERS=$(awk '$1=="L" && NF>=3 {print $3}' "$R/lock.txt" | uniq | paste -sd'>' -)
  case "$MODE" in pod|storage) LOGARGS="$OLD" ;; *) LOGARGS="$OLD --since-time=$(date -u -d "@${T_FAULT%.*}" +%FT%TZ)" ;; esac
  kubectl -n "$NS" logs $LOGARGS > "$R/old.log" 2>/dev/null || true
  if grep -qiE 'Removing data directory|replica has been created using basebackup|bootstrap from leader' "$R/old.log"; then REJOIN="re-clone"
  elif grep -qiE 'running pg_rewind|pg_rewind.*(success|done)|rewind' "$R/old.log"; then REJOIN="pg_rewind"
  else REJOIN="restart only"; fi
  TL1=$(patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline')
  OLD_TL=$(patroni_cluster | jq -r --arg o "$OLD" '.members[] | select(.name == $o) | .timeline')

  note "Probe: $NACK acknowledged, $NERR failed attempts. Lock holders sampled: \`$HOLDERS\`. Leadership samples: $NTICKS rounds of 3 members."
  note "First acknowledged write on the new primary at $( [ -n "$FIRST_NEW" ] && iso "$FIRST_NEW" || echo none) UTC. Last on the old primary at $( [ -n "$LAST_OLD" ] && iso "$LAST_OLD" || echo none) UTC. Timeline $TL0 -> $TL1. Fault restored at $(iso "$T_RESTORE"), old member streaming from the new primary at $(iso "$T_REJOIN") UTC."
  run "grep -iE 'rewind|basebackup|Removing data|bootstrap from leader|Demoting|demote|promot|shut down|immediate shutdown|read-only|PANIC' $R/old.log | sed -E 's/[0-9a-f]{32,}/[hex]/g' | head -12" || true
  [ "$MODE" != switchover ] || run "cat $R/switchover.txt" || true
  check "run $N: writes resumed on the new primary (RTO $RTO s)" test -n "$FIRST_NEW"
  check "run $N: RPO 0, all $NACK acknowledged rows present on the new primary" test "$MISSING" = 0
  check "run $N: never more than 1 member out of recovery in any sample" test "$MAXP" -le 1
  check "run $N: no acknowledged write on the old primary after the new primary's first" test "$OVERLAP" = 0
  check "run $N: old primary $OLD rejoined as a streaming replica of $NEW, sync standby restored" test $rj = 0
  check "run $N: old primary in recovery on the new leader's timeline" bash -c "[ \"\$(q $(member "$OLD") monitor 'select pg_is_in_recovery()')\" = t ] && [ '$OLD_TL' = '$TL1' ]"

  if [ "$MODE" = split-brain ]; then
    # ADR-006: demotion must complete before the old lock can expire (last renewal + ttl 20 s).
    LAST_RENEW=$(awk -v o="$OLD" '$1=="L" && $3==o {print $4}' "$R/lock.txt" | sort | tail -1 | xargs -r -I{} date -d {} +%s.%N)
    ACQ=$(lock | awk '{print $3}' | xargs -r -I{} date -d {} +%s.%N)
    T_DEMOTE=$(grep -iE 'demot' "$R/old.log" | head -1 | ts_of_log)
    T_STOPPED=$(grep -E 'database system is shut down' "$R/old.log" | head -1 | ts_of_log)
    note "Last lock renewal by $OLD: $( [ -n "$LAST_RENEW" ] && iso "$LAST_RENEW") UTC. Demotion issued +$(secs "$LAST_RENEW" "$T_DEMOTE") s (bound 13 s). Postgres stopped +$(secs "$LAST_RENEW" "$T_STOPPED") s. Last acknowledged write on the old primary +$(secs "$LAST_RENEW" "$LAST_OLD") s. New leader $NEW acquired the lock +$(secs "$LAST_RENEW" "$ACQ") s (ttl 20 s)."
    check "run $N: demotion issued within 13 s of the last renewal" awk -v d="$(secs "$LAST_RENEW" "$T_DEMOTE")" 'BEGIN{exit !(d != "n/a" && d <= 13.5)}'
    check "run $N: old primary stopped within 20 s of the last renewal (13 s + 7 s stop budget)" awk -v d="$(secs "$LAST_RENEW" "$T_STOPPED")" 'BEGIN{exit !(d != "n/a" && d <= 20)}'
    check "run $N: old primary's last acknowledged write precedes the new leader's lock acquisition" awk -v a="${LAST_OLD:-0}" -v b="${ACQ:-0}" 'BEGIN{exit !(b > 0 && a < b)}'
  fi
  res=PASS; [ $FAILS -eq $run_fails ] || res=FAIL
  printf '| %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s | %s |\n' "$N" "$OLD" "$NEW" "$RTO" "$GAP" "$NACK" "$MISSING" "$MAXP" "$REJOIN" "$(secs "$T_FAULT" "$T_REJOIN")" "$res" >> "$SUMMARY"
  RTOS="$RTOS $RTO"
  log "run $N: RTO=$RTO s gap=$GAP s acked=$NACK missing=$MISSING maxprimaries=$MAXP rejoin=$REJOIN $res"
done

# Evidence file for this mode, then the combined L2 summary.
verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
STATS=$(tr ' ' '\n' <<<"$RTOS" | grep -E '^[0-9.]+$' | sort -n | awk '{a[NR]=$1} END {if (NR) printf "min %.2f s, median %.2f s, max %.2f s over %d runs", a[1], (NR%2 ? a[(NR+1)/2] : (a[NR/2]+a[NR/2+1])/2), a[NR], NR; else print "no RTO measured"}')
case "$MODE" in
  pod) DESC='`kubectl delete pod` on the primary, with the default grace period. Patroni shuts Postgres down and releases the lock, so this measures a clean handover. An abrupt death is covered by the node mode.' ;;
  node) DESC='`docker stop` on the k3d agent container hosting the primary (D6), restarted with `docker start` once a new leader holds the lock. Every process on that node dies, so the lock must expire (ttl 20 s) before a replica can take over.' ;;
  storage) DESC='The primary'"'"'s data volume is made unavailable inside its container: `/data` is lazily unmounted in the Postgres container'"'"'s mount namespace (`docker exec <agent> nsenter -t <pid> -m umount -l /data`) and the postmaster is killed with SIGKILL, so Patroni cannot restart Postgres. It is restored by deleting the pod once a new leader holds the lock, so the kubelet mounts the volume again. **Limits:** a running Postgres does not notice a detached directory because it works relative to its open data directory, so the SIGKILL stands in for the I/O error or PANIC a real disk failure would cause. The data on the volume is intact, so this is not a lost or corrupted disk, and a hung disk that blocks I/O without failing is not shown. A read-only remount was tried first and refused (`mount point is busy`), because Postgres holds its files open for writing.' ;;
  split-brain) DESC='An iptables rule on the primary'"'"'s node drops only the primary pod'"'"'s traffic to the API server backend (the S2 finding: policy and filtering see the real backend address). Replication and client traffic are untouched, so the old primary can still reach its sync standby and acknowledge commits until it demotes itself. The rule is removed afterwards.' ;;
  switchover) DESC='`POST /switchover` to the leader'"'"'s Patroni REST API over `kubectl port-forward` and `curl`, naming the target (default the current sync standby). No exec is used. The API server pod proxy was tried first and refused with HTTP 411, because Patroni requires a Content-Length header that the proxy does not forward. **The REST API is unauthenticated until L6.**' ;;
esac
{ printf '# L2 failure mode: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$MODE" "$verdict"
  printf -- '- **Fault:** %s\n' "$DESC"
  printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make %s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$([ "$MODE" = switchover ] && echo switchover || ([ "$MODE" = split-brain ] && echo test-split-brain || echo "failover-$MODE"))"
  printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
  printf -- '- **Method:** RTO is fault injection to the first commit acknowledged by a new primary, from a probe writing through pg-rw every 500 ms. Write gap is the last acknowledged write before that to the first after it. RPO counts acknowledged rows missing on the new primary.\n'
  printf '\n## Summary\n\n%s\n\nRTO: %s. Target 30 s.\n\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n' "$(cat "$SUMMARY")" "$STATS"
  cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_FILE"

[ -n "${EV_OUT:-}" ] || "$ROOT_DIR/tests/l2-summary.sh"
log "RESULT L2 $MODE: $verdict ($STATS) -> ${EV_FILE#$ROOT_DIR/}"
[ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for tests. Sources the spike evidence helpers (redact, run, check, note, section).
#
# kubectl exec (D4): tests run psql only inside their own client pod, pg-test-client, never in a
# Postgres pod. Fault scripts may use docker exec on a k3d node, and each use is documented where it runs.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../scripts/spikes/lib.sh"
NS=$PG_NS; CLIENT=pg-test-client
BODY=$(mktemp); CHECKS=$(mktemp); FAILS=0; T0=$SECONDS; STARTED=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
RW=pg-rw.$NS.svc.cluster.local; RO=pg-ro.$NS.svc.cluster.local
member() { echo "$1.pg-headless.$NS.svc.cluster.local"; }
now() { date +%s.%N; }
iso() { date -u -d "@$1" +%H:%M:%S.%3N; }
secs() { awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN{ if (a == "" || b == "") print "n/a"; else printf "%.2f", b - a }'; }

# q HOST USER SQL: one psql call from the client pod. The password is chosen inside the pod from its env.
q() {
  kubectl -n "$NS" exec "$CLIENT" -- sh -c '
    case "$2" in app) PGPASSWORD=$APP_PW ;; monitor) PGPASSWORD=$MON_PW ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac; export PGPASSWORD

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L2 failure harness (R3.1-R3.7, R6.3, ADR-006). Usage: tests/failover.sh pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover
#   RUNS=n (default 3, switchover 1), TO=pg-N (switchover target, default the current sync standby)
#   EV_OUT=path writes the evidence there instead of docs/evidence/L2/<mode>.md, and leaves L2-failover.md alone
#   (used by L3 to fault the cluster without replacing the L2 results).
#
# RTO = fault injection to the first commit acknowledged by a new primary, seen by the probe Job
# (tests/probe-job.yaml), which writes through pg-rw every 500 ms. RPO = acknowledged sequence numbers
# missing on the new primary. Leadership is sampled twice every 500 ms: the lock holder from the pg-rw
# Endpoints object, and pg_is_in_recovery() asked of each member directly.
#
# Fault injection (D4, committed and documented):
#   pod          kubectl delete pod <primary> (default grace period, so Patroni shuts down normally)
#   node         docker stop <agent hosting the primary>, then docker start once a new leader holds the lock
#   storage      docker exec <agent>: lazily unmount /data inside the primary container's mount namespace, so
#                the volume is gone from that container, then SIGKILL the postmaster, standing in for the
#                I/O error a lost disk causes. Restored by deleting the pod once a new leader holds the lock,
#                so the kubelet mounts the volume again. See the evidence file for the limits.
#   split-brain  docker exec <agent> iptables: drop the primary pod's traffic to the API server backend only.
#                Pod-to-pod traffic, including replication, is untouched. The rule is removed afterwards.
#   switchover   POST /switchover to the leader's Patroni REST API over kubectl port-forward and curl
#                (the REST API is unauthenticated until L6). The API server pod proxy is not used for this
#                POST because Patroni rejects its request without a Content-Length header (HTTP 411).
# psql runs only in the test client pod, never in a Postgres pod.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
MODE=${1:-}; case "$MODE" in pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover) ;; *) die "usage: $0 pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover" ;; esac
RUNS=${RUNS:-$([ "$MODE" = switchover ] && echo 1 || echo 3)}
[[ "$RUNS" =~ ^[1-9]$ ]] || die "RUNS must be 1-9"
case "$MODE" in pod) DURATION=70 ;; switchover) DURATION=50 ;; *) DURATION=110 ;; esac
W=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L2"; EV_FILE="${EV_OUT:-$EV_DIR/L2/$MODE.md}"
PENDING_RESTORE=""; SAMPLER_PIDS=""

restore_fault() {
  case "$PENDING_RESTORE" in
    node:*) docker start "${PENDING_RESTORE#node:}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
    storage:*) kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "${PENDING_RESTORE#storage:}" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
    split:*) set -- ${PENDING_RESTORE#split:}; docker exec "$1" iptables -D FORWARD -s "$2" -d "$3" -p tcp --dport "$4" -j DROP >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;
  esac
  PENDING_RESTORE=""
}
stop_samplers() { [ -z "$SAMPLER_PIDS" ] || kill $SAMPLER_PIDS 2>/dev/null || true; wait $SAMPLER_PIDS 2>/dev/null || true; SAMPLER_PIDS=""; }
cleanup() {
  restore_fault; stop_samplers
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$CLIENT" --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  rm -rf "$W" "$BODY" "$CHECKS"
}
trap cleanup EXIT

wait_until() { # timeout-seconds command...
  local end=$((SECONDS + $1)); shift
  until "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1; do [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || return 1; sleep 0.5; done
}
leader_is_not() { local l; l=$(leader); [ -n "$l" ] && [ "$l" != "$1" ]; }
leader_is() { [ "$(leader)" = "$1" ]; }
pod_uid() { kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$1" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}' 2>/dev/null; }
uid_changed() { local u; u=$(pod_uid "$1"); [ -n "$u" ] && [ "$u" != "$2" ]; }
ts_of_log() { # "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS,mmm" or "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm UTC" at line start -> epoch
  sed -E 's/^([0-9-]+ [0-9:]+)[.,]([0-9]+).*/\1.\2 UTC/' | head -1 | xargs -r -I{} date -d {} +%s.%N
}
container_pid() { # agent pod -> host-visible PID of the Postgres container, via crictl on that node
  local id; id=$(docker exec "$1" crictl ps -q --name postgres --label "io.kubernetes.pod.name=$2" --label "io.kubernetes.pod.namespace=$NS")
  docker exec "$1" crictl inspect -o go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' "$id"
}

client_up
kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "namespace $NS not found, run: make up"
SUMMARY=$(mktemp -p "$W")
printf '| Run | Old primary | New primary | RTO (s) | Write gap (s) | Acked | RPO (acked rows missing) | Max primaries in one sample | Rejoin | Rejoin after fault (s) | Result |\n|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|\n' > "$SUMMARY"
RTOS=""

for N in $(seq 1 "$RUNS"); do
  R="$W/run$N"; mkdir -p "$R"; run_fails=$FAILS
  section "Run $N"
  wait_until 240 primary_confirms || die "cluster not healthy before run $N, see: make status"
  sleep 3
  OLD=$(leader); OLD_IP=$(pod_ip "$OLD"); OLD_NODE=$(pod_node "$OLD"); OLD_UID=$(pod_uid "$OLD")
  SYNC=$(sync_standby); TL0=$(patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline')
  TARGET=${TO:-$SYNC}

  RUN_ID="$MODE-$N-$(date +%s)"

  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job pg-probe --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
  sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|; s|__RUN_ID__|$RUN_ID|; s|__DURATION__|$DURATION|" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/probe-job.yaml" | kubectl -n "$NS" apply -f - >/dev/null

  ( while :; do echo "L $(now) $(lock)"; sleep 0.5; done ) > "$R/lock.txt" 2>/dev/null & SAMPLER_PIDS="$!"
  kubectl -n "$NS" exec "$CLIENT" -- sh -c 'end=$(( $(date +%s) + 600 )); i=0
    while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$end" ]; do i=$((i+1))
      for m in pg-0 pg-1 pg-2; do ( r=$(PGPASSWORD=$MON_PW psql "host=$m.pg-headless.pg-ha.svc.cluster.local user=monitor dbname=app connect_timeout=2" -XAtqc "select pg_is_in_recovery()" 2>/dev/null) || r=x; echo "S $i $(date +%s.%N) $m ${r:-x}" ) & done
      sleep 0.5; done' > "$R/samples.txt" 2>/dev/null & SAMPLER_PIDS="$SAMPLER_PIDS $!"
  sleep 2

  # Fault.
  case "$MODE" in
    pod) T_FAULT=$(now); kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$OLD" --wait=false >/dev/null ;;
    node) T_FAULT=$(now); docker stop "$OLD_NODE" >/dev/null; PENDING_RESTORE="node:$OLD_NODE" ;;
    storage)
      PID=$(container_pid "$OLD_NODE" "$OLD")
      PM=$(docker exec "$OLD_NODE" sh -c "for d in /proc/[0-9]*; do [ \"\$(cut -d' ' -f4 \$d/stat 2>/dev/null)\" = $PID ] && [ \"\$(cat \$d/comm 2>/dev/null)\" = postgres ] && echo \${d#/proc/}; done; true" | head -1)

      T_FAULT=$(now); docker exec "$OLD_NODE" sh -c "nsenter -t $PID -m -p -- umount -l /data && kill -KILL $PM"
      PENDING_RESTORE="storage:$OLD" ;;
    split-brain)
      API=$(kubectl get endpointslice -n default -l kubernetes.io/service-name=kubernetes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].endpoints[0].addresses[0]} {.items[0].ports[0].port}')
      set -- $API; API_IP=$1; API_PORT=$2
      T_FAULT=$(now); docker exec "$OLD_NODE" iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s "$OLD_IP" -d "$API_IP" -p tcp --dport "$API_PORT" -j DROP
      PENDING_RESTORE="split:$OLD_NODE $OLD_IP $API_IP $API_PORT" ;;

      printf '{"leader": "%s", "candidate": "%s"}' "$OLD" "$TARGET" > "$R/body.json"

  esac

  got=0; if [ "$MODE" = switchover ]; then wait_until 90 leader_is "$TARGET" || got=1; else wait_until 120 leader_is_not "$OLD" || got=1; fi
  T_LOCK=$(now); NEW=$(leader)
  check "run $N: lock moved from $OLD to a new leader ($NEW)" test $got = 0

    sleep 3; kubectl -n "$NS" logs "$OLD" --since-time="$(date -u -d "@${T_FAULT%.*}" +%FT%TZ)" > "$R/old-before-restore.log" 2>/dev/null || true

  case "$MODE" in pod|storage) wait_until 180 uid_changed "$OLD" "$OLD_UID" || true ;; esac

  wait_until $((DURATION + 60)) bash -c "kubectl -n $NS logs job/pg-probe 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^DONE'" || true
  stop_samplers
  kubectl -n "$NS" logs job/pg-probe > "$R/probe.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
  NEW_IP=$(pod_ip "$NEW")

  LAST_OLD=$(awk -v ip="$OLD_IP" '$1=="ACK" && $5==ip {print $4}' "$R/probe.txt" | sort -n | tail -1)

  NACK=$(awk '$1=="ACK"' "$R/probe.txt" | wc -l); NERR=$(awk '$1=="ERR"' "$R/probe.txt" | wc -l)

New leader $NEW acquired the lock +$(secs "$LAST_RENEW" "$ACQ") s (ttl 20 s)."

STATS=$(tr ' ' '\n' <<<"$RTOS" | grep -E '^[0-9.]+$' | sort -n | awk '{a[NR]=$1} END {if (NR) printf "min %.2f s, median %.2f s, max %.2f s over %d runs", a[1], (NR%2 ? a[(NR+1)/2] : (a[NR/2]+a[NR/2+1])/2), a[NR], NR; else print "no RTO measured"}')
case "$MODE" in
  pod) DESC='`kubectl delete pod` on the primary, with the default grace period. Patroni shuts Postgres down and releases the lock, so this measures a clean handover. An abrupt death is covered by the node mode.' ;;
  node) DESC='`docker stop` on the k3d agent container hosting the primary (D6), restarted with `docker start` once a new leader holds the lock. Every process on that node dies, so the lock must expire (ttl 20 s) before a replica can take over.' ;;
  storage) DESC='The primary'"'"'s data volume is made unavailable inside its container: `/data` is lazily unmounted in the Postgres container'"'"'s mount namespace (`docker exec <agent> nsenter -t <pid> -m umount -l /data`) and the postmaster is killed with SIGKILL, so Patroni cannot restart Postgres. The data on the volume is intact, so this is not a lost or corrupted disk, and a hung disk that blocks I/O without failing is not shown. A read-only remount was tried first and refused (`mount point is busy`), because Postgres holds its files open for writing.' ;;

  switchover) DESC='`POST /switchover` to the leader'"'"'s Patroni REST API over `kubectl port-forward` and `curl`, naming the target (default the current sync standby). No exec is used. The API server pod proxy was tried first and refused with HTTP 411, because Patroni requires a Content-Length header that the proxy does not forward. **The REST API is unauthenticated until L6.**' ;;
esac
{ printf '# L2 failure mode: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$MODE" "$verdict"
  printf -- '- **Fault:** %s\n' "$DESC"
  printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make %s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$([ "$MODE" = switchover ] && echo switchover || ([ "$MODE" = split-brain ] && echo test-split-brain || echo "failover-$MODE"))"
  printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for tests. Sources the spike evidence helpers (redact, run, check, note, section).
#

# Postgres pod. Fault scripts may use docker exec on a k3d node, and each use is documented where it runs.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../scripts/spikes/lib.sh"
NS=$PG_NS; CLIENT=pg-test-client
BODY=$(mktemp); CHECKS=$(mktemp); FAILS=0; T0=$SECONDS; STARTED=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)
RW=pg-rw.$NS.svc.cluster.local; RO=pg-ro.$NS.svc.cluster.local
member() { echo "$1.pg-headless.$NS.svc.cluster.local"; }
now() { date +%s.%N; }
iso() { date -u -d "@$1" +%H:%M:%S.%3N; }
secs() { awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN{ if (a == "" || b == "") print "n/a"; else printf "%.2f", b - a }'; }

# q HOST USER SQL: one psql call from the client pod. The password is chosen inside the pod from its env.
q() {
  kubectl -n "$NS" exec "$CLIENT" -- sh -c '
    case "$2" in app) PGPASSWORD=$APP_PW ;; monitor) PGPASSWORD=$MON_PW ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac; export PGPASSWORD
    exec psql "host=$1 user=$2 dbname=app connect_timeout=3" -XAtq -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -F " " -c "$3"' sh "$1" "$2" "$3"

client_up() {

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: pg-test-client, labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg-test-client}}
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 0
  nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: infra}     # on the server node, so agent faults never take the observer down
  tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, operator: Exists, effect: NoSchedule}]
  securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
  containers:
  - name: client
    image: __PG_IMAGE__
    imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
    command: [sleep, "7200"]
    securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
    env:
    - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
    - name: APP_PW

    - name: MON_PW
      valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: pg-credentials, key: pg-monitor-password}}
    volumeMounts: [{name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}]
  volumes: [{name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}]
YAML
  kubectl -n "$NS" wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$CLIENT" --timeout=90s >/dev/null || die "client pod not ready"
}

lock() { kubectl -n "$NS" get endpoints pg-rw -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.leader} {.metadata.annotations.renewTime} {.metadata.annotations.acquireTime}' 2>/dev/null; }
leader() { lock | awk '{print $1}'; }
pod_ip() { kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$1" -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}' 2>/dev/null; }
pod_node() { kubectl -n "$NS" get pod "$1" -o jsonpath='{.spec.nodeName}' 2>/dev/null; }
sync_standby() { q "$RW" monitor "select application_name from pg_stat_replication where sync_state = 'sync'" 2>/dev/null; }

primary_confirms() { # [member that must be streaming]
  local r; r=$(q "$RW" monitor "select application_name, state, sync_state from pg_stat_replication" 2>/dev/null) || return 1

# ADR-008: Old primary rejoin

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

After failover, the old primary must return as a replica of the new primary with no human step.

## Options considered

- **`pg_rewind` with re-clone fallback:** fast normally, and recovers when rewind fails.
- **Always re-clone:** simple, but slower and heavier on the shared disk.
- **`pg_rewind` only:** no automatic deletion, but a member can get stuck.

## Decision

Set `use_pg_rewind: true` and `remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true`. Initialise with data checksums, keep `wal_log_hints=on`, and use a dedicated rewind role.

## Consequences

- The fallback deletes that member's diverged data directory, which is safe only because the current primary remains the source of truth.
- `restore_command` lets rewind fetch older WAL from the archive.
- Checksums also detect page corruption, at a small write cost.

## R-IDs covered

R3.6
=======
# ADR-001: Cluster topology

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

D6 defines node failure as stopping a k3d agent, so every Postgres pod must run on an agent. Backups and monitoring should survive that failure. The host has 4 vCPU and 16 GB (D7).

## Options considered

- **1 server + 3 agents:** smallest layout where every Postgres node can be failed.
- **3 servers + 3 agents:** removes the API single point of failure, but runs six node containers and adds etcd load.
- **1 server + 2 agents:** smallest footprint, but one Postgres pod would sit on the server and could not be failed under D6.

## Decision

Use **1 tainted server + 3 agents**. Postgres pods use required node affinity on `pg-ha/role=db`, required pod anti-affinity on hostname, and a topology spread constraint with `maxSkew: 1` and `DoNotSchedule`. Infrastructure workloads tolerate the taint and run on the server.

## Consequences

- Any Postgres node can be stopped while object storage and monitoring keep running.
- The API server is a single point of failure, documented in ADR-002 and known limitations.
- All nodes share one VM, kernel and disk, so this simulates node failure rather than proving zone independence.

## Options considered

- **`pg_rewind` with re-clone fallback:** fast normally, and recovers when rewind fails.
- **Always re-clone:** simple, but slower and heavier on the shared disk.
- **`pg_rewind` only:** no automatic deletion, but a member can get stuck.

## Decision

Set `use_pg_rewind: true` and `remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true`. Initialise with data checksums, keep `wal_log_hints=on`, and use a dedicated rewind role.

## Consequences

- The fallback deletes that member's diverged data directory, which is safe only because the current primary remains the source of truth.
- `restore_command` lets rewind fetch older WAL from the archive.
- Checksums also detect page corruption, at a small write cost.

## R-IDs covered

R3.6
=======
# ADR-001: Cluster topology

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

D6 defines node failure as stopping a k3d agent, so every Postgres pod must run on an agent. Backups and monitoring should survive that failure. The host has 4 vCPU and 16 GB (D7).

## Options considered

- **1 server + 3 agents:** smallest layout where every Postgres node can be failed.
- **3 servers + 3 agents:** removes the API single point of failure, but runs six node containers and adds etcd load.
- **1 server + 2 agents:** smallest footprint, but one Postgres pod would sit on the server and could not be failed under D6.

## Decision

Use **1 tainted server + 3 agents**. Postgres pods use required node affinity on `pg-ha/role=db`, required pod anti-affinity on hostname, and a topology spread constraint with `maxSkew: 1` and `DoNotSchedule`. Infrastructure workloads tolerate the taint and run on the server.

## Consequences

- Any Postgres node can be stopped while object storage and monitoring keep running.
- The API server is a single point of failure, documented in ADR-002 and known limitations.
- All nodes share one VM, kernel and disk, so this simulates node failure rather than proving zone independence.

        """Handle the case when postgres isn't running.

        Depending on the state of Patroni, DCS cluster view, and pg_controldata the following could happen:

          - if ``primary_start_timeout`` is 0 and this node owns the leader lock, the lock
            will be voluntarily released if there are healthy replicas to take it over.

          - if postgres was running as a ``primary`` and this node owns the leader lock, postgres is started as primary.

          - crash recover in a single-user mode is executed in the following cases:

            - postgres was running as ``primary`` wasn't ``shut down`` cleanly and there is no leader in DCS

            - postgres was running as ``replica`` wasn't ``shut down in recovery`` (cleanly)
              and we need to run ``pg_rewind`` to join back to the cluster.

cat >> tests/lib.sh <<'EOF'

# Cluster DNS placement (L3: a single CoreDNS replica on the primary's node stalled promotion). Prints node names.
coredns_nodes() { kubectl -n kube-system get pod -l k8s-app=kube-dns -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName}{" "}{end}' 2>/dev/null | sed 's/ $//'; }

# WAL archive health (L3, ADR-008). archive_stat HOST prints: failed_count last_archived_epoch last_archived_wal
# ready_count ready_names. pg_ls_archive_statusdir() is granted to pg_monitor, so the monitor role suffices.
archive_stat() {
  q "$1" monitor "select a.failed_count, coalesce(extract(epoch from a.last_archived_time), 0), coalesce(a.last_archived_wal, '-'),
    (select count(*) from pg_ls_archive_statusdir() where name like '%.ready'),
    coalesce((select string_agg(left(name, 24), ',' order by name) from pg_ls_archive_statusdir() where name like '%.ready'), '-')
    from pg_stat_archiver a"
}
# Fills more than one 16 MB WAL segment through pg-rw, so a segment is closed without waiting for
# archive_timeout and without a superuser pg_switch_wal().
wal_fill() {
  q "$RW" app "create table if not exists harness_walfill (id int, pad text)" >/dev/null &&
  q "$RW" app "insert into harness_walfill select g, repeat(md5(g::text), 6) from generate_series(1, 80000) g" >/dev/null &&
  q "$RW" app "drop table harness_walfill" >/dev/null
}
# archive_check HOST FAILED_BEFORE BOUND: fills WAL, then waits up to BOUND s for a segment archived after the
# fill started. Sets ARCH_T (seconds to the archive, or n/a), ARCH_FAILED (failed_count delta), ARCH_STAT.
archive_check() {
  local host=$1 f0=$2 bound=$3 t0 end s; t0=$(now); end=$((SECONDS + bound)); ARCH_T=n/a
  wal_fill || true
  while [ $SECONDS -lt $end ]; do
    s=$(archive_stat "$host" 2>/dev/null) || { sleep 1; continue; }
    awk -v t="$t0" '{exit !($2 > t)}' <<<"$s" && { ARCH_T=$(secs "$t0" "$(awk '{print $2}' <<<"$s")"); break; }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L2/L3 chained scenario (ADR-008): the sequence that stalled WAL archiving in L3. A node failover, then a
# planned switchover back to the old primary, which by then has rejoined on the new timeline. When the old
# primary rejoined with pg_rewind, it held WAL files copied without archive status, and once it was primary
# again, archiving failed for good with "already exists in the repo1 archive with a different checksum".
# With rejoin by re-clone, archiving on the old primary must stay healthy.
#
# Both steps run tests/failover.sh with RUNS=1, so each has the full RTO, RPO, single-primary and archive
# health checks, with its evidence in L2/chain-node.md and L2/chain-switchover.md. This script then watches
# archiving on the returned primary over a second interval. No exec beyond the harness (D4).
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W" "$BODY" "$CHECKS"; kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$CLIENT" --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
client_up
tl() { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline'; }
row() { sed -nE '/^\| 1 \|/p' "$1" | head -1; }
OLD=$(leader); TL0=$(tl)

section "Step 1: node failover"
note "Before: leader \`$OLD\`, timeline $TL0. Evidence: [\`chain-node.md\`](chain-node.md)."
RUNS=1 EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" node > "$W/1.log" 2>&1 && s1=1 || s1=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/1.log" || true
check "Node failover run passed (RTO within target, RPO 0, one primary, rejoined, archive healthy)" test $s1 = 1
REJOIN=$(row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" | awk -F'|' '{gsub(/ /, "", $10); print $10}')
client_up; MID=$(leader); TL1=$(tl)
note "After step 1: leader \`$MID\`, timeline $TL1. \`$OLD\` rejoined by: $REJOIN."

section "Step 2: switchover back to the old primary"
note "Evidence: [\`chain-switchover.md\`](chain-switchover.md)."
RUNS=1 TO="$OLD" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" switchover > "$W/2.log" 2>&1 && s2=1 || s2=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/2.log" || true
check "Switchover to $OLD passed (including archive health right after it)" test $s2 = 1
client_up; NOW=$(leader); TL2=$(tl); TLX=$(printf '%08X' "$TL2")
check "$OLD is the primary again, on timeline $TL2" test "$NOW" = "$OLD"

section "Archive health on the returned primary, second interval"
S0=$(archive_stat "$(member "$NOW")"); F0=$(awk '{print $1}' <<<"$S0")
archive_check "$(member "$NOW")" "$F0" "$ARCHIVE_BOUND"
READY=$(awk '{print $5}' <<<"$ARCH_STAT")
STALE=$(tr ',' '\n' <<<"$READY" | grep -vE "^-$|^$TLX" | paste -sd, -)
note "Primary \`$NOW\`. Before: $(awk '{print "failed_count", $1 ", last archived", $3}' <<<"$S0"). After a WAL fill: archived in $ARCH_T s, failed_count +$ARCH_FAILED, last archived \`$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$ARCH_STAT")\`, pending .ready: ${READY}."
run "q $(member "$NOW") monitor 'select failed_count, last_failed_wal, last_failed_time, archived_count, last_archived_wal, last_archived_time from pg_stat_archiver'" || true
check "No new archive failures on $NOW" test "$ARCH_FAILED" -le 0
check "A segment was archived within $ARCHIVE_BOUND s of a WAL fill" test "$ARCH_T" != n/a
check "No pending .ready segment from an older timeline (stale WAL from a rejoin)" test -z "$STALE"

verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
{ printf '# L2 failure mode: chain\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$verdict"
  printf -- '- **Fault:** Node failover (`docker stop` of the primary'"'"'s agent), then a planned switchover back to the old primary after it has rejoined. This is the sequence that stalled WAL archiving in L3 when rejoin used `pg_rewind` (ADR-008). Archive health is checked on the returned primary.\n'
  printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make failover-chain`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))"
  printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
  printf '\n## Summary\n\n| Step | Old primary | New primary | RTO (s) | Write gap (s) | Acked | RPO (acked rows missing) | Max primaries in one sample | Rejoin | Rejoin after fault (s) | CoreDNS node | Archive failures (new) | Archived after fill (s) | Result |\n|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|\n'
  row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" | sed 's/^| 1 |/| node |/'
  row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" | sed 's/^| 1 |/| switchover back |/'
  printf '\nSecond interval on `%s`: archived %s s after a WAL fill, failed_count +%s, pending .ready `%s`.\n' "$NOW" "$ARCH_T" "$ARCH_FAILED" "$READY"
  printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_DIR/L2/chain.md"
"$ROOT_DIR/tests/l2-summary.sh"
log "RESULT L2 chain: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L2/chain.md"
[ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerates docs/evidence/L2-failover.md from the per-mode files in docs/evidence/L2/.
. "$(dirname "$0")/../scripts/spikes/lib.sh"
MODES="pod node storage split-brain switchover chain api-outage"
{ printf '# L2: failover, switchover and split-brain

Generated from the per-mode files in [`L2/`](L2/) each time a mode runs. Timestamps are UTC.'
  [ ! -f "$EV_DIR/L2-failover-history.md" ] || printf ' Hand-written notes: [`L2-failover-history.md`](L2-failover-history.md).'
  printf '

RTO is fault injection to the first commit acknowledged by a new primary, measured by a probe Job writing through pg-rw every 500 ms over new connections with a 2 s connect timeout. RPO is the number of acknowledged rows missing on the new primary. The target is RTO at most 30 s with safe settings (ttl 20, loop_wait 3, retry_timeout 5). A run over the target is reported as **OVER TARGET**, not PASS. After every run the harness also checks WAL archive health on the current primary (no new archive failures, a segment archived within 90 s of a WAL fill) and records where CoreDNS ran.
'
  printf '
## RTO by failure mode

| Mode | Result | RTO |
|---|---|---|
'
  for f in $MODES; do
    [ -f "$EV_DIR/L2/$f.md" ] || { printf '| %s | not run | |
' "$f"; continue; }
    printf '| [%s](L2/%s.md) | %s | %s |
' "$f" "$f" "$(grep -m1 -oE 'Result: (PASS|FAIL|OVER TARGET)' "$EV_DIR/L2/$f.md" | sed 's/Result: //')" \
      "$(grep -m1 -E '^RTO: ' "$EV_DIR/L2/$f.md" | sed -E 's/^RTO: //; s/\. Target 30 s.*//' || true)"
  done
  for f in $MODES; do
    [ -f "$EV_DIR/L2/$f.md" ] || { printf '
## %s

Not run yet.
' "$f"; continue; }
    printf '
## %s: %s

' "$f" "$(grep -m1 -oE 'Result: (PASS|FAIL|OVER TARGET)' "$EV_DIR/L2/$f.md")"
    sed -n '/^- \*\*Fault:\*\*/p' "$EV_DIR/L2/$f.md"
    printf -- '- Details: [`L2/%s.md`](L2/%s.md)

' "$f" "$f"
    sed -n '/^## Summary/,/^## Checks/p' "$EV_DIR/L2/$f.md" | sed '1d;$d'
  done; } > "$EV_DIR/L2-failover.md"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L2/L3 chained scenario (ADR-008): the sequence that stalled WAL archiving in L3. A node failover, then a
# planned switchover back to the old primary, which by then has rejoined on the new timeline. When the old
# primary rejoined with pg_rewind, it held WAL files copied without archive status, and once it was primary
# again, archiving failed for good with "already exists in the repo1 archive with a different checksum".
# With rejoin by re-clone, archiving on the old primary must stay healthy.
#
# Both steps run tests/failover.sh with RUNS=1, so each has the full RTO, RPO, single-primary and archive
# health checks, with its evidence in L2/chain-node.md and L2/chain-switchover.md. This script then watches
# archiving on the returned primary over a second interval. No exec beyond the harness (D4).
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W" "$BODY" "$CHECKS"; kubectl -n "$NS" delete pod "$CLIENT" --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
client_up
tl() { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline'; }
row() { sed -nE '/^\| 1 \|/p' "$1" | head -1; }
OLD=$(leader); TL0=$(tl)

section "Step 1: node failover"
note "Before: leader \`$OLD\`, timeline $TL0. Evidence: [\`chain-node.md\`](chain-node.md)."
RUNS=1 EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" node > "$W/1.log" 2>&1 && s1=1 || s1=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/1.log" || true
check "Node failover run passed (RTO within target, RPO 0, one primary, rejoined, archive healthy)" test $s1 = 1
REJOIN=$(row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" | awk -F'|' '{gsub(/ /, "", $10); print $10}')
client_up; MID=$(leader); TL1=$(tl)
note "After step 1: leader \`$MID\`, timeline $TL1. \`$OLD\` rejoined by: $REJOIN."

section "Step 2: switchover back to the old primary"
note "Evidence: [\`chain-switchover.md\`](chain-switchover.md)."
RUNS=1 TO="$OLD" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" switchover > "$W/2.log" 2>&1 && s2=1 || s2=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/2.log" || true
check "Switchover to $OLD passed (including archive health right after it)" test $s2 = 1
client_up; NOW=$(leader); TL2=$(tl); TLX=$(printf '%08X' "$TL2")
check "$OLD is the primary again, on timeline $TL2" test "$NOW" = "$OLD"

section "Archive health on the returned primary, second interval"
S0=$(archive_stat "$(member "$NOW")"); F0=$(awk '{print $1}' <<<"$S0")
archive_check "$(member "$NOW")" "$F0" "$ARCHIVE_BOUND"
READY=$(awk '{print $5}' <<<"$ARCH_STAT")
STALE=$(tr ',' '\n' <<<"$READY" | grep -vE "^-$|^$TLX" | paste -sd, -)
note "Primary \`$NOW\`. Before: $(awk '{print "failed_count", $1 ", last archived", $3}' <<<"$S0"). After a WAL fill: archived in $ARCH_T s, failed_count +$ARCH_FAILED, last archived \`$(awk '{print $3}' <<<"$ARCH_STAT")\`, pending .ready: ${READY}."
run "q $(member "$NOW") monitor 'select failed_count, last_failed_wal, last_failed_time, archived_count, last_archived_wal, last_archived_time from pg_stat_archiver'" || true
check "No new archive failures on $NOW" test "$ARCH_FAILED" -le 0
check "A segment was archived within $ARCHIVE_BOUND s of a WAL fill" test "$ARCH_T" != n/a
check "No pending .ready segment from an older timeline (stale WAL from a rejoin)" test -z "$STALE"

verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
{ printf '# L2 failure mode: chain\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$verdict"
  printf -- '- **Fault:** Node failover (`docker stop` of the primary'"'"'s agent), then a planned switchover back to the old primary after it has rejoined. This is the sequence that stalled WAL archiving in L3 when rejoin used `pg_rewind` (ADR-008). Archive health is checked on the returned primary.\n'
  printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make failover-chain`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))"
  printf -- '- **Versions:** k3s `%s`, image `%s`\n' "${K3S_IMAGE%@*}" "$PG_IMAGE"
  printf '\n## Summary\n\n| Step | Old primary | New primary | RTO (s) | Write gap (s) | Acked | RPO (acked rows missing) | Max primaries in one sample | Rejoin | Rejoin after fault (s) | CoreDNS node | Archive failures (new) | Archived after fill (s) | Result |\n|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---|\n'
  row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" | sed 's/^| 1 |/| node |/'
  row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" | sed 's/^| 1 |/| switchover back |/'
  printf '\nSecond interval on `%s`: archived %s s after a WAL fill, failed_count +%s, pending .ready `%s`.\n' "$NOW" "$ARCH_T" "$ARCH_FAILED" "$READY"
  printf '\n## Checks\n\n| Check | Result |\n|---|---|\n'; cat "$CHECKS"; cat "$BODY"; } | redact > "$EV_DIR/L2/chain.md"
"$ROOT_DIR/tests/l2-summary.sh"
log "RESULT L2 chain: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L2/chain.md"
[ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]

Exit code 2
## O8. Old primary rejoin

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. `pg_rewind`, with re-clone fallback** | `use_pg_rewind: true`, and `remove_data_directory_on_rewind_failure: true` | Fast normal path, and still recovers automatically when rewind fails | Fallback deletes that member's data dir | Meets R3.6 | 1.5 h |
| B. Always re-clone | Remove data and copy from primary | Simple logic | Slower, more I/O on a shared disk | Meets R3.6 | 1 h |
| C. `pg_rewind` only | No fallback | No automatic deletion | Can leave a member stuck | Risks R3.6 | 1 h |

**Requirements:**

- `pg_rewind` needs **`wal_log_hints=on` or data checksums**. **[Verified]**
- Enable **both**: initialise with `--data-checksums`, which also detects corruption, and keep `wal_log_hints=on`, which Patroni sets. **[Verified]**
- Create a dedicated rewind role with only the required function privileges.
- `restore_command` lets rewind fetch older WAL from the archive when needed.

**Recommendation: A.** Strongest reason: it gives the fast path while guaranteeing the old primary always returns with no human step.

## O9. Backups
## Build plan

The lean plan is **16 focused hours** and keeps every MUST. It has no spare contingency, so the cut lines are part of the plan. Docs, playbook, video and submission (L8) are separate.

| Phase | Work | Key exit check | Hours | Cumulative |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| **L0** | `make tools`, `preflight`, `certs`, generated Secrets, k3d cluster, image, **spikes S1–S4** | Spikes pass and 4 nodes Ready | 2.5 | 2.5 |
| **L1** | StatefulSet, Patroni, RBAC, Services, sync replication, slots, rewind | `T:topology`, `T:replication`, `T:endpoints` pass | 2.5 | 5.0 |
| **L2** | One parameterised failure harness: pod, node, storage, isolation, switchover, RTO | All modes run 3 times, with real RTO recorded | 3.0 | 8.0 |
| **L3** | Garage, pgBackRest, archiving, backup CronJob, retention | Archive, backup and retention tests pass | 2.0 | 10.0 |
| **L4** | Full restore, PITR, shared restore-test Job | `T:restore-full`, `T:pitr`, `T:restore-verify` pass | 2.5 | 12.5 |
| **L5** | Prometheus, Alertmanager, exporters, required alert rules | `T:metrics` and rule unit tests pass | 1.5 | 14.0 |
| **L6** | Remaining security baseline, security doc | Security tests pass | 1.0 | 15.0 |
| **L7** | Clean-host run, evidence, traceability, measured capacity | `make down && make up && make test` passes | 1.0 | **16.0** |
| **L8** | Docs, playbook, session logs, redaction, video, submission | Submission sent | Separate | |

**What changed from the 23.5-hour plan**

| Change | Saved |
|---|---:|
| Decisions and ADRs completed before the build starts | 1.0 h |
| Bootstrap combined: one `make certs`, no MinIO build | 0.5 h |
| Patroni core built with rewind in one pass | 0.5 h |
| One failure harness instead of separate scripts | 1.0 h |
| Garage image and repository encryption instead of a store build plus TLS work | 1.0 h |
| One restore path and shared test Job | 0.5 h |
| Monitoring limited to required rules first, no Grafana | 1.0 h |
| Security reuses the bootstrap CA and Secrets, built last | 1.5 h |
| Evidence captured during each phase instead of at the end | 0.5 h |
| **Total** | **7.5 h** |

**Out of scope from the start:** Grafana and R10.4, connection pooling, image scanning, simulated zones, `failsafe_mode`, differential backups and quorum replication.

**Spikes in L0, run first because they can invalidate a decision:**

| Spike | Question | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Does pgBackRest complete stanza creation, backup, archive and restore against Garage? | Evaluate SeaweedFS, with MinIO from source as last resort |
| S2 | Does k3s enforce NetworkPolicy, including egress to the API server? | Use ingress-only policy and document it |
| S3 | Can UID 999 create a 0700 `PGDATA` on a local-path volume? | Add a minimal init step and document the exception |
| S4 | Is v1 Endpoints served at runtime, and how long does EndpointSlice mirroring take? | Reassess O7 before L2 |

### Phase notes from L0

Findings from the L0 spikes that later phases must honour. Evidence is in `docs/evidence/L0-spike-S*.md`.

- **L1:** The certificates assume namespaces `pg-ha` and `pg-restore` and a headless Service named `pg-headless`. Using other names means reissuing them.
- **L2:** The 13 s in ADR-006 bounds when Patroni *issues* the demotion. Postgres must then stop within the remaining 7 s, and `T:split-brain` must measure this.
- **L3:** `pgbackrest verify` can exit 0 while reporting `status: error`, so the backup job and alerts must check the reported status and not only the exit code.
- **L3 watch item:** S1 showed that a connection opened during Garage's first startup can stall for about 135 s, and that a connect timeout with retry bounds it. Whether a **Garage restart** does the same to running clients is untested. L3 must measure WAL archiving across a Garage restart and confirm that pgBackRest's timeouts bound any stalled connection. See `docs/evidence/L0-spike-S1-history.md`.
- **L4:** `pg_amcheck` needs `--install-missing`. That is acceptable on the scratch restore, but it must not run against production.

# Known limitations

This file lists what the system does not protect against or does not implement (R12.5, HC10). Entries are added as each phase confirms them.

## Backups

### Backup repository is not off-site

The in-cluster Garage repository shares the VM and disk with the database, so it is not off-site disaster protection. In production, the pgBackRest repository points at GCS/S3 with bucket versioning and a retention lock, off-site from the cluster, using keyless workload identity where available.

- **Why it is the default:** `make up` must work for any reviewer with no cloud account or credentials.
- **Planned option:** R4.7 adds `BACKUP_TARGET=gcs make up`. It is OPTIONAL and not built yet.
- **Decision:** ADR-014.

# ADR-008: Old primary rejoin

**Status:** Accepted, revised in L3 (2026-11-25): rejoin by re-clone instead of `pg_rewind`

## Context

After failover, the old primary must return as a replica of the new primary with no human step.

The first decision (below, superseded) used `pg_rewind` with a re-clone fallback. In L3, with WAL archiving on, it caused a permanent archiving stall:

- A member that had rejoined with `pg_rewind` later became primary again. Its `pg_wal` still held segments from older timelines (`0000001E…2B` and `00000021…33` on timeline 36).
- Those copies differed from the copies the primaries of those timelines had already archived. pgBackRest therefore refused them with `[045] WAL file ... already exists in the repo1 archive with a different checksum`.
- Postgres retries the oldest `.ready` segment forever, so every current segment queued behind it was not archived either. Point-in-time recovery lost coverage from that moment, and backups after that failover could not be restored past it.
- The likely mechanism, inferred from documented Postgres behaviour and not traced: `pg_rewind` copies WAL files from the source without archive status. Segments closed early by `archive_timeout` hold leftover bytes after the switch record, and those bytes differ between servers. After a promotion, the checkpoint marks status-less files `.ready`, and the archiver pushes them.
- Evidence is in `docs/evidence/L3-backup-history.md`. The chained scenario `make failover-chain` reproduces the sequence: a node failover, then a switchover back to the old primary.

## Options considered

- **`pg_rewind` with re-clone fallback** (the first decision): fast normally, and recovers when rewind fails. It leaves stale old-timeline WAL that blocks archiving after a later promotion.
- **Always re-clone a diverged member:** `pg_basebackup` writes a fresh data directory and marks the WAL it streams as already archived, so no stale segment survives. It is slower and does more I/O.
- **`pg_rewind` only:** no automatic deletion, but a member can get stuck, and it has the same stale-WAL problem.
- **Keep `pg_rewind` and wrap `archive_command`:** on error 045 for a segment from an older timeline whose copy is already in the repository, log it and return success. **Rejected.** It hides a whole error class in the backup path. A real checksum conflict, such as two primaries writing the same timeline, would be silenced exactly where it must be loud.
- **Keep `pg_rewind` and clean up archive status after each rewind:** mark old-timeline segments `.done` before Postgres starts. This needs a hook that Patroni does not provide, plus custom code in the rejoin path.

## Decision

Set `use_pg_rewind: false` and `remove_data_directory_on_diverged_timelines: true`. Patroni checks each rejoining member against the leader's timeline history. If the member has diverged, Patroni deletes its data directory and re-clones it with `pg_basebackup`. A member that has not diverged, for example after a clean switchover, rejoins with a restart only.

Keep data checksums, `wal_log_hints=on` and the dedicated rewind role. Patroni's divergence check connects as the rewind role, and the settings keep `pg_rewind` available if this decision is reversed.

## Consequences

- Rejoin after an unclean failover is slower, because it copies the whole data directory. At about 180 MB this takes seconds, and it is not on the RTO path: writes resume on the new primary before the old one rejoins. The rejoin time is measured in the L2 evidence.
- Archiving after any sequence of failovers and switchovers no longer depends on what a rejoined member left in `pg_wal`. The L2 harness checks archive health after every run.
- The re-clone deletes the diverged member's data directory. That is safe only because the current primary remains the source of truth, as before.
- **For multi-TB databases** a full re-clone per failover is too slow and too much I/O. There, keep `pg_rewind` and add a post-rewind step that marks old-timeline segments as archived. Never suppress error 045.
- Checksums also detect page corruption, at a small write cost.

## R-IDs covered

R3.6, R4.6

# ADR-008: Old primary rejoin

**Status:** Accepted, revised in L3 (2026-11-25): rejoin by re-clone instead of `pg_rewind`

## Context

After failover, the old primary must return as a replica of the new primary with no human step.

The first decision (below, superseded) used `pg_rewind` with a re-clone fallback. In L3, with WAL archiving on, it caused a permanent archiving stall:

- A member that had rejoined with `pg_rewind` later became primary again. Its `pg_wal` still held segments from older timelines (`0000001E…2B` and `00000021…33` on timeline 36).
- Those copies differed from the copies the primaries of those timelines had already archived. pgBackRest therefore refused them with `[045] WAL file ... already exists in the repo1 archive with a different checksum`.
- Postgres retries the oldest `.ready` segment forever, so every current segment queued behind it was not archived either. Point-in-time recovery lost coverage from that moment, and backups after that failover could not be restored past it.
- The likely mechanism, inferred from documented Postgres behaviour and not traced: `pg_rewind` copies WAL files from the source without archive status. Segments closed early by `archive_timeout` hold leftover bytes after the switch record, and those bytes differ between servers. After a promotion, the checkpoint marks status-less files `.ready`, and the archiver pushes them.
- Evidence is in `docs/evidence/L3-backup-history.md`. The chained scenario `make failover-chain` reproduces the sequence: a node failover, then a switchover back to the old primary.

## Options considered

- **`pg_rewind` with re-clone fallback** (the first decision): fast normally, and recovers when rewind fails. It leaves stale old-timeline WAL that blocks archiving after a later promotion.
- **Always re-clone a diverged member:** `pg_basebackup` writes a fresh data directory and marks the WAL it streams as already archived, so no stale segment survives. It is slower and does more I/O.
- **`pg_rewind` only:** no automatic deletion, but a member can get stuck, and it has the same stale-WAL problem.
- **Keep `pg_rewind` and wrap `archive_command`:** on error 045 for a segment from an older timeline whose copy is already in the repository, log it and return success. **Rejected.** It hides a whole error class in the backup path. A real checksum conflict, such as two primaries writing the same timeline, would be silenced exactly where it must be loud.
- **Keep `pg_rewind` and clean up archive status after each rewind:** mark old-timeline segments `.done` before Postgres starts. This needs a hook that Patroni does not provide, plus custom code in the rejoin path.

## Decision

Set `use_pg_rewind: false` and `remove_data_directory_on_diverged_timelines: true`. Patroni checks each rejoining member against the leader's timeline history. If the member has diverged, Patroni deletes its data directory and re-clones it with `pg_basebackup`. A member that has not diverged, for example after a clean switchover, rejoins with a restart only.

Keep data checksums, `wal_log_hints=on` and the dedicated rewind role. Patroni's divergence check connects as the rewind role, and the settings keep `pg_rewind` available if this decision is reversed.

## Consequences

- Rejoin after an unclean failover is slower, because it copies the whole data directory. At about 180 MB this takes seconds, and it is not on the RTO path: writes resume on the new primary before the old one rejoins. The rejoin time is measured in the L2 evidence.
- Archiving after any sequence of failovers and switchovers no longer depends on what a rejoined member left in `pg_wal`. The L2 harness checks archive health after every run.
- The re-clone deletes the diverged member's data directory. That is safe only because the current primary remains the source of truth, as before.
- **For multi-TB databases** a full re-clone per failover is too slow and too much I/O. There, keep `pg_rewind` and add a post-rewind step that marks old-timeline segments as archived. Never suppress error 045.
- Checksums also detect page corruption, at a small write cost.

## R-IDs covered

R3.6, R4.6
