Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. The cache is positional: agent() calls replay from cache up to the first call that failed, no longer matches the earlier run (edited, added, removed or reordered) or never started in it; that call and every call after it run again, even when their own (prompt, opts) are unchanged. A call a usage limit refused, or one still running when the run stopped, usually runs again without ending reuse: finished calls after it still come from cache. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

content.text: Tool loaded.

content.thinking: Patroni only switches over to the sync standby in synchronous mode, so a manual failover to an async member is off the table. I'll instead chain up to three switchovers to the current sync standby until the old primary is back as sync standby, with the harness's full checks on every hop.

p='tests/failover-chain.sh'; s=open(p).read()
def r(a,b):
    global s
    assert s.count(a)==1, a[:50]; s=s.replace(a,b)
r("""# Both steps run tests/failover.sh with RUNS=1, so each has the full RTO, RPO, single-primary and archive
# health checks, with its evidence in L2/chain-node.md and L2/chain-switchover.md. This script then watches
# archiving on the returned primary over a second interval. No exec beyond the harness (D4).""","""# Every step runs tests/failover.sh with RUNS=1, so each has the full RTO, RPO, single-primary and archive
# health checks, with its evidence in L2/chain-node.md and L2/chain-switchover-N.md. In synchronous mode
# Patroni switches over only to the sync standby, so when the old primary is not the sync standby, the
# chain first switches over to whichever member is (at most 3 hops), until the old primary leads again. A
# manual failover to an async member would bypass that rule and is not used. This script then watches
# archiving on the returned primary over a second interval. No exec beyond the harness (D4).""")
r("""section "Step 2: switchover back to the old primary"
note "Evidence: [\\`chain-switchover.md\\`](chain-switchover.md)."
RUNS=1 TO="$OLD" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" switchover > "$W/2.log" 2>&1 && s2=1 || s2=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/2.log" || true
check "Switchover to $OLD passed (including archive health right after it)" test $s2 = 1
client_up; NOW=$(leader); TL2=$(tl); TLX=$(printf '%08X' "$TL2")
""","""section "Step 2: switchover back to the old primary"
rm -f "$EV_DIR"/L2/chain-switchover*.md; HOPS=0; s2=1
while [ "$(leader)" != "$OLD" ] && [ $HOPS -lt 3 ]; do
  HOPS=$((HOPS + 1)); SYNC=$(sync_standby); TGT=$( [ "$SYNC" = "$OLD" ] && echo "$OLD" || echo "$SYNC")
  note "Hop $HOPS: leader \\`$(leader)\\`, sync standby \\`$SYNC\\`, switchover to \\`$TGT\\`. Evidence: [\\`chain-switchover-$HOPS.md\\`](chain-switchover-$HOPS.md)."
  RUNS=1 TO="$TGT" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover-$HOPS.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" switchover > "$W/2.log" 2>&1 || s2=0
  run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/2.log" || true
  client_up
  [ $s2 = 1 ] || break
done
check "Every switchover hop passed (RTO, RPO 0, one primary, archive health right after it), $HOPS hop(s)" test $s2 = 1
NOW=$(leader); TL2=$(tl); TLX=$(printf '%08X' "$TL2")
""")
r("""  row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" | sed 's/^| 1 |/| switchover back |/'
""","""  for f in "$EV_DIR"/L2/chain-switchover-*.md; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; n=${f##*-}; row "$f" | sed "s/^| 1 |/| switchover ${n%.md} |/"; done
""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
bash -n tests/failover-chain.sh && echo ok

content.thinking: Patroni only switches over to the sync standby in synchronous mode, so a manual failover to an async member is off the table. I'll instead chain up to three switchovers to the current sync standby until the old primary is back as sync standby, with the harness's full checks on every hop.

input.command:
cd [REDACTED-HOME]/[REDACTED-GCP-PROJECT] && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='tests/failover-chain.sh'; s=open(p).read()
def r(a,b):
    global s
    assert s.count(a)==1, a[:50]; s=s.replace(a,b)
r("""# Both steps run tests/failover.sh with RUNS=1, so each has the full RTO, RPO, single-primary and archive
# health checks, with its evidence in L2/chain-node.md and L2/chain-switchover.md. This script then watches
# archiving on the returned primary over a second interval. No exec beyond the harness (D4).""","""# Every step runs tests/failover.sh with RUNS=1, so each has the full RTO, RPO, single-primary and archive
# health checks, with its evidence in L2/chain-node.md and L2/chain-switchover-N.md. In synchronous mode
# Patroni switches over only to the sync standby, so when the old primary is not the sync standby, the
# chain first switches over to whichever member is (at most 3 hops), until the old primary leads again. A
# manual failover to an async member would bypass that rule and is not used. This script then watches
# archiving on the returned primary over a second interval. No exec beyond the harness (D4).""")
r("""section "Step 2: switchover back to the old primary"
note "Evidence: [\\`chain-switchover.md\\`](chain-switchover.md)."
RUNS=1 TO="$OLD" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" switchover > "$W/2.log" 2>&1 && s2=1 || s2=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/2.log" || true
check "Switchover to $OLD passed (including archive health right after it)" test $s2 = 1
client_up; NOW=$(leader); TL2=$(tl); TLX=$(printf '%08X' "$TL2")
""","""section "Step 2: switchover back to the old primary"
rm -f "$EV_DIR"/L2/chain-switchover*.md; HOPS=0; s2=1
while [ "$(leader)" != "$OLD" ] && [ $HOPS -lt 3 ]; do
  HOPS=$((HOPS + 1)); SYNC=$(sync_standby); TGT=$( [ "$SYNC" = "$OLD" ] && echo "$OLD" || echo "$SYNC")
  note "Hop $HOPS: leader \\`$(leader)\\`, sync standby \\`$SYNC\\`, switchover to \\`$TGT\\`. Evidence: [\\`chain-switchover-$HOPS.md\\`](chain-switchover-$HOPS.md)."
  RUNS=1 TO="$TGT" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover-$HOPS.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" switchover > "$W/2.log" 2>&1 || s2=0
  run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/2.log" || true
  client_up
  [ $s2 = 1 ] || break
done
check "Every switchover hop passed (RTO, RPO 0, one primary, archive health right after it), $HOPS hop(s)" test $s2 = 1
NOW=$(leader); TL2=$(tl); TLX=$(printf '%08X' "$TL2")
""")
r("""  row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover.md" | sed 's/^| 1 |/| switchover back |/'
""","""  for f in "$EV_DIR"/L2/chain-switchover-*.md; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; n=${f##*-}; row "$f" | sed "s/^| 1 |/| switchover ${n%.md} |/"; done
""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
bash -n tests/failover-chain.sh && echo ok

All five modes passed on the final configuration: re-clone rejoin, CoreDNS pinned to `k3d-pg-ha-server-0` in every run, archiving on. No run was over target, and every run's archive check passed (no new failures, a segment archived 1.8 to 5.4 s after the WAL fill). Node-failure RTO was 23.22 to 26.19 s, against 21.9 to 23.4 s before archiving.

**No run diverged.** Every old primary rejoined by restart only, after crash recovery in the node and storage modes. The re-clone path was therefore not exercised. The earlier `pg_rewind` runs were real divergences (`pg_rewind: servers diverged at WAL location ...` in the L2 node evidence of commit `b53d48f` and in the L3 node run at 07:47), so divergence happens only sometimes. A forced-divergence test remains open.

`make failover-chain` failed twice, both times on harness bugs and not on the cluster. Per the working rule it was not run a third time.

The harness also died when a run measured no RTO (`grep` with no match under `pipefail`), and `client_up` accepted a test client still being deleted. The same checks run by hand on `pg-1` at 13:44 showed a segment archived 1.37 s after a WAL fill, no new failures, and no pending `.ready` file.

- **Limit:** no failover in the rerun diverged, so the re-clone path itself was not exercised, and the exact rewind-then-promote trigger of the stall has not been reproduced. R4.6 is met for every sequence run (13 failovers and switchovers plus the chain), but a forced divergence test is still open.
"""
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

All 13 L2 runs passed under the 30 s target, archive health checked clean after every run, and R4.6 passed again. Two gaps remain:

- **The chained scenario has no combined evidence file.** It failed twice on harness bugs, so under your rule I stopped without a third run. All its steps passed, each with its own evidence file, but `L2/chain.md` was never written. The last bug is fixed, and `make failover-chain` would produce the file.
- **The re-clone fix is untested.** No run in the rerun diverged, so every old primary rejoined by a plain restart. The divergence that caused the stall (a real `pg_rewind` after one) happens only sometimes, so neither the re-clone path nor the original trigger was exercised.

## Updated RTO table (after the rebuild, final config)

| Mode | Runs | RTO min / median / max (s) | Rejoin | Result |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Pod deleted | 3 | 3.60 / 3.78 / 5.13 | restart only | PASS |
| Node stopped | 3 | 23.22 / 23.93 / 26.19 | restart only | PASS |
| Storage lost | 3 | 2.39 / 3.37 / 3.69 | restart only | PASS |
| Split-brain | 3 | 20.47 / 22.18 / 22.20 | restart only | PASS |
| Switchover | 1 | 2.08 | restart only | PASS |
| Chained: node failover, then 2 switchover hops back | 1 | 21.90, 2.61, 2.56 | restart only | Steps PASS, combined file missing |

- **Data loss:** RPO was 0 in every run, and no sample ever showed two primaries.
- **CoreDNS:** it was on the server node in every run.
- **Node failure:** about 1 to 3 s slower than the first L2 results, from the history-file fetch at promotion.

## Archive health results

- **Every run:** no new archive failures on the current primary, and a segment archived 1.8 to 5.4 s after a forced WAL fill (bound 90 s).
- **After the chain:** the returned primary showed no new failures and no pending segments, with a segment archived 1.37 s after the fill. I checked this by hand because the script died before that step.
- **Switchover rule:** Patroni switches over only to the sync standby. When the old primary isn't the sync standby, the chain now steps through whichever member is, at most 3 hops. I didn't use a manual failover to an async member, because that would bypass the rule.

## R4.6 status

**Met for every sequence tested.** After the rebuild, a node failover took 23.09 s. Archiving continued on the new timeline with no failures, `pgbackrest check` passed, and a backup started on the new timeline passed verify. Proving the fix for the original stall needs one forced-divergence run.

## Done as decided

- **Rejoin by re-clone:** Patroni now re-clones a member that has diverged (`use_pg_rewind: false`, `remove_data_directory_on_diverged_timelines: true`).
- **ADR-008:** rewritten with context, decision and consequences. The multi-TB alternative (keep `pg_rewind` plus a cleanup step) is recorded, and wrapping `archive_command` is rejected explicitly.
- **ADR-001 and known limitations:** they record that DNS now shares the server node's single point of failure. The design doc has new "Phase notes from L3" with the L4 implications.
- **Rebuild:** done, and a fresh full backup on the seeded dataset passed verify at 13:02.
- **Harness changes:**
  - Archive health is checked after every run.
  - CoreDNS placement is recorded, and a run fails if CoreDNS sat on the faulted node.
  - A run over 30 s shows as **OVER TARGET** in its row, the mode result and `L2-failover.md`, and the script exits non-zero.
  - The new `make failover-chain` and `make test-failover` targets are added.
  - Three harness bugs are fixed:
    - A run with no RTO crashed the harness.
    - A test pod that was being deleted still counted as ready.
    - A `grep` with no match killed the chain script.
- **History files:** there was no L2 history file, so I created `docs/evidence/L2-failover-history.md`. It explains why the suite was rerun and records the chain result. The L3 history now marks the stall resolved, with the limit stated.

The API-outage evidence is from before the rebuild and wasn't rerun.

**Time:** about 53 minutes (12:52–13:45 UTC) against the 75-minute box. Nothing is committed.

# ADR-010: Restore and PITR

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

The whole cluster must restore into an empty namespace, support PITR to a timestamp, and prove backups through a scheduled or on-demand test.

## Options considered

- **Patroni custom bootstrap:** restored cluster uses the same HA path as production.
- **Pre-restore Job per PVC:** separates steps but repeats work.
- **Test trigger:** one Job template used by CronJob and `make`, or `make` only.

## Decision

- Restore through **Patroni custom bootstrap** in a Kustomize overlay.
- Run PITR with `--type=time` and `--target-action=promote`. `TARGET_TIME` must include a timezone offset.
- Use **one restore-test Job template** for both a daily CronJob and `make test-restore`. It restores into `emptyDir`, starts Postgres without network exposure, checks marker data and `pg_amcheck`, then exits.
- A restored cluster must **not** archive into the source stanza.

## Consequences

- A passing test exercises the real recovery path.
- Restored role passwords must be reset through `post_bootstrap`, to be confirmed during implementation.
- In-cluster object storage is lost with the cluster, so this proves namespace-level recovery and not off-site disaster recovery.

## R-IDs covered

R4.5, R5.1, R5.2, R5.3, R5.4, R5.5
# ADR-009: Backups

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

We need scheduled base backups, continuous WAL archiving, enforced retention and automatic verification. D4 forbids `kubectl exec` in backup paths, so a CronJob needs a network route to the database host.

## Options considered

- **pgBackRest:** built-in `expire` and `verify`, plus a TLS server that scheduled Jobs can reach.
- **WAL-G:** small and simple, but base backups need an in-pod trigger.

## Decision

Use **pgBackRest 2.60.1** with the object store from ADR-014:

- A full backup through a CronJob on a **configurable schedule**, defaulting to daily at 20:00 UTC.
- Continuous asynchronous WAL archiving.
- `repo1-retention-full=7`, enforced by automatic `expire`.
- `pgbackrest verify` daily after the backup.
- A single **`make certs`** bootstrap step creates one CA, reused for the pgBackRest TLS server and Postgres TLS.

**Repository settings live in one place.** Every `repo1-*` setting goes in a single `repo.conf`, loaded from pgBackRest's `conf.d` include path. The main config holds only stanza, Postgres and process settings.

- Backup, archive, restore and restore-test workloads all read the same `repo.conf`.
- Credentials never go in `repo.conf`. They come from Kubernetes Secrets at runtime.
- The default `repo.conf` targets Garage with `repo1-type=s3`.
- A later GCS overlay (R4.7) replaces that one file with `repo1-type=gcs`, `repo1-gcs-bucket` and `repo1-gcs-key-type`, and leaves out the Garage workloads. Use `auto` for keyless identity where available. Otherwise use `service`, with a key file supplied at runtime from outside the repo.
- **The overlay is not built yet.**

**The backup schedule is a parameter.** The VM is stopped overnight, so a daily 20:00 UTC run may never fire during testing. Evidence for R4.1 is captured with a short schedule, for example every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`), from a Job the CronJob created itself. The evidence states the schedule that was used.

**Backups follow the primary without config changes.** pgBackRest lists all three Postgres pods as `pg1-host`, `pg2-host` and `pg3-host`, using their stable headless-service DNS names. It determines which one is the current primary at run time, so a backup after failover needs no configuration change.

**Generated secrets survive teardown.** Generated secrets, including the pgBackRest repository cipher passphrase, live in a git-ignored `./secrets/` directory.

- Generation is idempotent and never overwrites an existing value.
- `make down` preserves `./secrets/`.
- Only an explicit **`make clean-secrets`** deletes them, and it warns first that **existing backups become unrecoverable** without the passphrase.

## Consequences

- A check at L3 must confirm that no `repo1-*` setting exists outside `repo.conf`.
- The GCS overlay must also allow egress to GCS in NetworkPolicy and create its stanza in an empty bucket path.
- TLS certificates become a bootstrap dependency, so that work is done once.
- R4.1 needs evidence from a truly scheduled Job, so a cluster must stay up across one schedule.
- The repository cipher passphrase becomes critical: losing it makes backups unrecoverable.

## R-IDs covered

R4.1, R4.2, R4.3, R4.4, R4.5, R4.6, R4.7, R8.10
## O10. Restore and PITR

**Full restore into an empty namespace**

| Option | How it works | Pros | Cons | R-IDs | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Patroni custom bootstrap** | Deploy the same manifests through an overlay. Patroni's `bootstrap.method` runs `pgbackrest restore`, then replicas clone normally | Reuses all HA config, ends as a real 1+2 cluster | Bootstrap script needs care | Meets R5.1–R5.3 | 3 h |
| B. Pre-restore Job per PVC | Restore into PVCs, then start Patroni | Separates the steps | Repeats work per member, harder to promote cleanly | Meets R5.1. Risks R5.3 | 4 h |

**Scheduled verification**

# ADR-010: Restore and PITR

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

The whole cluster must restore into an empty namespace, support PITR to a timestamp, and prove backups through a scheduled or on-demand test.

## Options considered

- **Patroni custom bootstrap:** restored cluster uses the same HA path as production.
- **Pre-restore Job per PVC:** separates steps but repeats work.
- **Test trigger:** one Job template used by CronJob and `make`, or `make` only.

## Decision

- Restore through **Patroni custom bootstrap** in a Kustomize overlay.
- Run PITR with `--type=time` and `--target-action=promote`. `TARGET_TIME` must include a timezone offset.
- Use **one restore-test Job template** for both a daily CronJob and `make test-restore`. It restores into `emptyDir`, starts Postgres without network exposure, checks marker data and `pg_amcheck`, then exits.
- A restored cluster must **not** archive into the source stanza.

## Consequences

- A passing test exercises the real recovery path.
- Restored role passwords must be reset through `post_bootstrap`, to be confirmed during implementation.
- In-cluster object storage is lost with the cluster, so this proves namespace-level recovery and not off-site disaster recovery.

## R-IDs covered

R4.5, R5.1, R5.2, R5.3, R5.4, R5.5
# ADR-009: Backups

**Status:** Accepted

## Context

We need scheduled base backups, continuous WAL archiving, enforced retention and automatic verification. D4 forbids `kubectl exec` in backup paths, so a CronJob needs a network route to the database host.

## Options considered

- **pgBackRest:** built-in `expire` and `verify`, plus a TLS server that scheduled Jobs can reach.
- **WAL-G:** small and simple, but base backups need an in-pod trigger.

## Decision

Use **pgBackRest 2.60.1** with the object store from ADR-014:

- A full backup through a CronJob on a **configurable schedule**, defaulting to daily at 20:00 UTC.
- Continuous asynchronous WAL archiving.
- `repo1-retention-full=7`, enforced by automatic `expire`.
- `pgbackrest verify` daily after the backup.
- A single **`make certs`** bootstrap step creates one CA, reused for the pgBackRest TLS server and Postgres TLS.

**Repository settings live in one place.** Every `repo1-*` setting goes in a single `repo.conf`, loaded from pgBackRest's `conf.d` include path. The main config holds only stanza, Postgres and process settings.

- Backup, archive, restore and restore-test workloads all read the same `repo.conf`.
- Credentials never go in `repo.conf`. They come from Kubernetes Secrets at runtime.
- The default `repo.conf` targets Garage with `repo1-type=s3`.
- A later GCS overlay (R4.7) replaces that one file with `repo1-type=gcs`, `repo1-gcs-bucket` and `repo1-gcs-key-type`, and leaves out the Garage workloads. Use `auto` for keyless identity where available. Otherwise use `service`, with a key file supplied at runtime from outside the repo.
- **The overlay is not built yet.**

**The backup schedule is a parameter.** The VM is stopped overnight, so a daily 20:00 UTC run may never fire during testing. Evidence for R4.1 is captured with a short schedule, for example every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`), from a Job the CronJob created itself. The evidence states the schedule that was used.

**Backups follow the primary without config changes.** pgBackRest lists all three Postgres pods as `pg1-host`, `pg2-host` and `pg3-host`, using their stable headless-service DNS names. It determines which one is the current primary at run time, so a backup after failover needs no configuration change.

**Generated secrets survive teardown.** Generated secrets, including the pgBackRest repository cipher passphrase, live in a git-ignored `./secrets/` directory.

- Generation is idempotent and never overwrites an existing value.
- `make down` preserves `./secrets/`.
- Only an explicit **`make clean-secrets`** deletes them, and it warns first that **existing backups become unrecoverable** without the passphrase.

## Consequences

- A check at L3 must confirm that no `repo1-*` setting exists outside `repo.conf`.
- The GCS overlay must also allow egress to GCS in NetworkPolicy and create its stanza in an empty bucket path.
- TLS certificates become a bootstrap dependency, so that work is done once.
- R4.1 needs evidence from a truly scheduled Job, so a cluster must stay up across one schedule.
- The repository cipher passphrase becomes critical: losing it makes backups unrecoverable.

## R-IDs covered

R4.1, R4.2, R4.3, R4.4, R4.5, R4.6, R4.7, R8.10

apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: pg-ha
resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - rbac.yaml
  - services.yaml
  - statefulset.yaml
  - pdb.yaml
  - backup-cronjob.yaml

post-bootstrap.sh
#!/bin/sh
# Patroni post_bootstrap: runs once, on the first primary after initdb. $1 is a superuser connection URL.
# Patroni itself creates the superuser, replicator and rewind roles. This creates the others.
# Passwords are read inside psql with \getenv, so they never appear on a command line or in output,
# and failed statements are kept out of the server log.
set -eu
psql "$1" -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
\set VERBOSITY terse
SET log_min_error_statement = panic;
SET log_statement = none;
\getenv monitor_pw PG_MONITOR_PASSWORD
\getenv backup_pw PG_BACKUP_PASSWORD
\getenv app_pw PG_APP_PASSWORD
\getenv app_ro_pw PG_APP_RO_PASSWORD
CREATE ROLE monitor LOGIN PASSWORD :'monitor_pw' IN ROLE pg_monitor;
-- pgBackRest privileges are finalised in L3.
CREATE ROLE backup LOGIN PASSWORD :'backup_pw' IN ROLE pg_read_all_settings, pg_checkpoint;
CREATE ROLE app LOGIN PASSWORD :'app_pw';
CREATE ROLE app_ro LOGIN PASSWORD :'app_ro_pw' IN ROLE pg_read_all_data;
CREATE DATABASE app OWNER app;
SQL
echo "post-bootstrap: roles monitor, backup, app, app_ro and database app created"

\getenv app_pw PG_APP_PASSWORD

+ALTER ROLE app PASSWORD :'app_pw';
+ALTER ROLE app_ro PASSWORD :'app_ro_pw';

input.command:
mkdir -p deploy/restore && cat > deploy/restore/kustomization.yaml <<'EOF'
# L4 (ADR-010): the whole cluster restored from the pgBackRest repository into an empty namespace, through
# Patroni's custom bootstrap. Same manifests as deploy/pg, plus 30-restore.yml, which scripts/restore.sh
# renders (bootstrap method, recovery target, archive_mode off). Rendered and applied by scripts/restore.sh.
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: pg-restore
resources:
  - ../pg
patches:
  # The namespace is created by scripts/restore.sh. A restored cluster takes no backups of its own.
  - patch: '{"$patch": "delete", "apiVersion": "v1", "kind": "Namespace", "metadata": {"name": "pg-ha"}}'
  - patch: '{"$patch": "delete", "apiVersion": "batch/v1", "kind": "CronJob", "metadata": {"name": "pg-backup"}}'
  - patch: '{"$patch": "delete", "apiVersion": "batch/v1", "kind": "CronJob", "metadata": {"name": "pg-restore-test"}}'
configMapGenerator:
  - name: pg-patroni
    behavior: merge
    files: [30-restore.yml]
EOF
cat > deploy/pg/scripts/restore-bootstrap.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
# Patroni custom bootstrap for a restored cluster (ADR-010, deploy/restore). Runs once, on the first member,
# in an empty volume. $1 is the recovery target time with a timezone offset, or empty for the latest state.
# pgBackRest chooses the backup set (the newest one that ends before the target) and restores it. The
# recovery settings it writes to postgresql.auto.conf are then removed, because Patroni writes its own
# from bootstrap.pgbackrest.recovery_conf, and settings left in postgresql.auto.conf would be copied to
# every replica and would survive the end of recovery.
set -eu
PGDATA=/data/pgdata
mkdir -p "$PGDATA"; chmod 0700 "$PGDATA"
if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
  set -- --type=time "--target=$1" --target-timeline=latest
else
  set -- --type=default --target-timeline=latest
fi
pgbackrest --stanza=main --log-level-console=info --log-level-file=off "$@" restore
sed -i '/^# Recovery settings generated by pgBackRest/d; /^restore_command/d; /^recovery_target/d' "$PGDATA/postgresql.auto.conf"
echo "restore-bootstrap: restore done, recovery is driven by Patroni's recovery_conf"
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='deploy/pg/kustomization.yaml'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("files: [scripts/post-bootstrap.sh, scripts/backup-job.sh]","files: [scripts/post-bootstrap.sh, scripts/backup-job.sh, scripts/restore-bootstrap.sh, scripts/restore-test.sh]")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n scripts/ deploy/pg/kustomization.yaml

# L3 (ADR-009): scheduled full backup, expire and verify, from the repository host role. The schedule is
# filled in by scripts/deploy.sh from BACKUP_SCHEDULE (default daily 20:00 UTC). make backup creates a Job
# from this same template.
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata: {name: pg-backup}
spec:
  schedule: __BACKUP_SCHEDULE__        # scripts/deploy.sh substitutes a single-quoted value
  timeZone: Etc/UTC
  concurrencyPolicy: Forbid           # pgBackRest holds a stanza lock; never run two
  startingDeadlineSeconds: 600
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      backoffLimit: 0
      activeDeadlineSeconds: 3600
      template:
        metadata: {labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: pg-backup}}
        spec:
          restartPolicy: Never
          enableServiceLinks: false
          automountServiceAccountToken: false
          nodeSelector: {pg-ha/role: db}
          securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 999, runAsGroup: 999, fsGroup: 999, seccompProfile: {type: RuntimeDefault}}
          containers:
            - name: backup
              image: __PG_IMAGE__
              imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
              command: [bash, /scripts/backup-job.sh]
              env:
                - {name: HOME, value: /tmp}
              envFrom:
                - secretRef: {name: pgbackrest-repo}
              securityContext: {allowPrivilegeEscalation: false, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
              resources:
                requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 64Mi}
                limits: {memory: 512Mi}
              volumeMounts:
                - {name: config, mountPath: /etc/pgbackrest, readOnly: true}
                - {name: tls, mountPath: /etc/pgbackrest-tls, readOnly: true}
                - {name: scripts, mountPath: /scripts, readOnly: true}
                - {name: tmp, mountPath: /tmp}
          volumes:
            - name: config
              configMap:
                name: pg-pgbackrest
                items:
                  - {key: job.conf, path: pgbackrest.conf}
                  - {key: repo.conf, path: conf.d/repo.conf}
            - name: tls
              secret: {secretName: pgbackrest-tls, defaultMode: 0440}
            - name: scripts
              configMap: {name: pg-scripts, defaultMode: 0555}
            - {name: tmp, emptyDir: {}}
#!/bin/bash
# Backup CronJob body (ADR-009): full backup, then expire, then verify. Exits non-zero unless verify
# reports status ok, because verify can exit 0 while reporting status error (L0 finding, spike S1).
set -euo pipefail
S=main
say() { printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*"; }
say "full backup"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --type=full --log-level-console=info backup > /tmp/backup.log 2>&1 || { cat /tmp/backup.log; say BACKUP_FAILED; exit 1; }
grep -E 'new backup label|full backup size|backup start archive|backup stop archive' /tmp/backup.log || true
say "expire (repo1-retention-full from repo.conf, or PGBACKREST_REPO1_RETENTION_FULL for a test)"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info expire > /tmp/expire.log 2>&1 || { cat /tmp/expire.log; say EXPIRE_FAILED; exit 1; }
grep -E 'expire|remove' /tmp/expire.log | grep -v 'command (begin|end)' || true
say "verify"
rc=0; V=$(pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info --verbose verify 2>&1) || rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -E 'status:|archiveId:|backup:|checksum invalid|size invalid|missing|other' | sed -E 's/^[0-9-]+ [0-9:.]+ +P[0-9]+ +[A-Z]+: //; s/^ +//'
if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || ! grep -q 'status: ok' <<<"$V" || grep -q 'status: error' <<<"$V"; then
  say "VERIFY_FAILED (exit $rc)"; exit 1
fi
say VERIFY_OK
pgbackrest --stanza=$S info
say BACKUP_JOB_OK

# Backup CronJob body (ADR-009): full backup, then expire, then verify. Exits non-zero unless verify
# reports status ok, because verify can exit 0 while reporting status error (L0 finding, spike S1).
set -euo pipefail

pgbackrest --stanza=$S --type=full --log-level-console=info backup > /tmp/backup.log 2>&1 || { cat /tmp/backup.log; say BACKUP_FAILED; exit 1; }
grep -E 'new backup label|full backup size|backup start archive|backup stop archive' /tmp/backup.log || true
say "expire (repo1-retention-full from repo.conf, or PGBACKREST_REPO1_RETENTION_FULL for a test)"
pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info expire > /tmp/expire.log 2>&1 || { cat /tmp/expire.log; say EXPIRE_FAILED; exit 1; }
grep -E 'expire|remove' /tmp/expire.log | grep -v 'command (begin|end)' || true
say "verify"
rc=0; V=$(pgbackrest --stanza=$S --log-level-console=info --verbose verify 2>&1) || rc=$?
printf '%s\n' "$V" | grep -E 'status:|archiveId:|backup:|checksum invalid|size invalid|missing|other' | sed -E 's/^[0-9-]+ [0-9:.]+ +P[0-9]+ +[A-Z]+: //; s/^ +//'
if [ $rc -ne 0 ] || ! grep -q 'status: ok' <<<"$V" || grep -q 'status: error' <<<"$V"; then
  say "VERIFY_FAILED (exit $rc)"; exit 1
fi
say VERIFY_OK
pgbackrest --stanza=$S info
say BACKUP_JOB_OK

python3 - <<'EOF'
p='tests/failover.sh'; s=open(p).read()
def r(a,b):
    global s
    assert s.count(a)==1, a[:60]; s=s.replace(a,b)
r("# L2 failure harness (R3.1-R3.7, R6.3, ADR-006). Usage: tests/failover.sh pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover",
  "# L2 failure harness (R3.1-R3.7, R6.3, ADR-006). Usage: tests/failover.sh pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover|diverge")
r("""#   switchover   POST /switchover""","""#   diverge      (L4, ADR-008) docker exec <agent> iptables: drop replication traffic from the primary pod to
#                both replicas (source port 5432) for DIVERGE_HOLD s (default 5) while the probe writes, so
#                the primary writes WAL that no replica receives. Then docker stop the agent, as in node mode.
#                The new primary is promoted behind the old one, so the old primary has diverged and must
#                rejoin by re-clone. The rules go with the stopped container and are deleted again anyway.
#   switchover   POST /switchover""")
r("""MODE=${1:-}; case "$MODE" in pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover) ;; *) die "usage: $0 pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover" ;; esac""",
  """MODE=${1:-}; case "$MODE" in pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover|diverge) ;; *) die "usage: $0 pod|node|storage|split-brain|switchover|diverge" ;; esac""")
r("""    node:*) docker start "${PENDING_RESTORE#node:}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true ;;""",
  """    node:*) docker start "${PENDING_RESTORE#node:}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
            for ip in ${DIVERGE_IPS:-}; do docker exec "${PENDING_RESTORE#node:}" iptables -D FORWARD -s "$OLD_IP" -d "$ip" -p tcp --sport 5432 -j DROP >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done ;;""")
r("""    node) T_FAULT=$(now); docker stop "$OLD_NODE" >/dev/null; PENDING_RESTORE="node:$OLD_NODE" ;;""",
  """    node) T_FAULT=$(now); docker stop "$OLD_NODE" >/dev/null; PENDING_RESTORE="node:$OLD_NODE" ;;
    diverge)
      DIVERGE_IPS=""; for m in pg-0 pg-1 pg-2; do [ "$m" = "$OLD" ] || DIVERGE_IPS="$DIVERGE_IPS $(pod_ip "$m")"; done
      T_FAULT=$(now); PENDING_RESTORE="node:$OLD_NODE"
      for ip in $DIVERGE_IPS; do docker exec "$OLD_NODE" iptables -I FORWARD 1 -s "$OLD_IP" -d "$ip" -p tcp --sport 5432 -j DROP; done
      sleep "${DIVERGE_HOLD:-5}"; T_STOP=$(now); docker stop "$OLD_NODE" >/dev/null
      note "Replication from \\`$OLD\\` to$(printf ' `%s`' $DIVERGE_IPS) blocked at $(iso "$T_FAULT") UTC, node stopped +$(secs "$T_FAULT" "$T_STOP") s later." ;;""")
r("""case "$MODE" in pod) DURATION=70 ;; switchover) DURATION=50 ;; *) DURATION=110 ;; esac""",
  """case "$MODE" in pod) DURATION=70 ;; switchover) DURATION=50 ;; *) DURATION=110 ;; esac
DIVERGE_IPS=\"\"""")
r("""  switchover) DESC='`POST /switchover`""","""  diverge) DESC='Replication traffic from the primary pod to both replicas is dropped by iptables on its node for '"${DIVERGE_HOLD:-5}"' s while the probe writes, so the primary writes WAL (commits that wait for the sync standby and are never acknowledged) that no replica receives. Then its k3d agent is stopped, as in the node mode, and started again once a new leader holds the lock. RTO counts from the start of the block. The old primary has diverged and must rejoin by re-clone (ADR-008).' ;;
  switchover) DESC='`POST /switchover`""")
r("""(make %s)\\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$([ "$MODE" = switchover ] && echo switchover || ([ "$MODE" = split-brain ] && echo test-split-brain || echo "failover-$MODE"))\"""",
  """(make %s)\\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$([ "$MODE" = switchover ] && echo switchover || ([ "$MODE" = split-brain ] && echo test-split-brain || echo "failover-$MODE"))\"""") if False else None
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
bash -n tests/failover.sh && grep -n 'case "$MODE" in pod|storage) LOGARGS' tests/failover.sh

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='tests/failover-chain.sh'; s=open(p).read()
def r(a,b):
    global s
    assert s.count(a)==1, a[:60]; s=s.replace(a,b)
r(". \"$(dirname \"$0\")/lib.sh\"\n", """#
# Usage: tests/failover-chain.sh [node|diverge]. With diverge (make failover-diverge, ADR-008), the first step
# is the diverge fault: the old primary has WAL no replica received, so it must rejoin by RE-CLONE, and the
# evidence goes to L2/diverge.md. This is the original trigger of the L3 archiving stall.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
FIRST=${1:-node}; case "$FIRST" in node) OUT=chain ;; diverge) OUT=diverge ;; *) die "usage: $0 [node|diverge]" ;; esac
""")
r("""section "Step 1: node failover"
note "Before: leader \\`$OLD\\`, timeline $TL0. Evidence: [\\`chain-node.md\\`](chain-node.md)."
RUNS=1 EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" node > "$W/1.log" 2>&1 && s1=1 || s1=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/1.log" || true
check "Node failover run passed (RTO within target, RPO 0, one primary, rejoined, archive healthy)" test $s1 = 1
REJOIN=$(row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" | awk -F'|' '{gsub(/ /, "", $10); print $10}')""","""section "Step 1: $FIRST failover"
F1="$EV_DIR/L2/$OUT-$FIRST.md"
note "Before: leader \\`$OLD\\`, timeline $TL0. Evidence: [\\`${F1##*/}\\`](${F1##*/})."
RUNS=1 EV_OUT="$F1" "$ROOT_DIR/tests/failover.sh" "$FIRST" > "$W/1.log" 2>&1 && s1=1 || s1=0
run "grep -E '^run 1:|RESULT' $W/1.log" || true
check "$FIRST failover run passed (RTO within target, RPO 0 for acknowledged commits, one primary, rejoined, archive healthy)" test $s1 = 1
REJOIN=$(row "$F1" | awk -F'|' '{gsub(/ /, "", $10); print $10}')
if [ "$FIRST" = diverge ]; then
  note "Old primary's Patroni and Postgres log after the restart (from ${F1##*/}):"
  run "grep -E 'diverged|Removing data|basebackup|requested timeline|not a child|reinitializ|rewind' '$F1' | grep -v '^\\\\$' | head -10" || true
  check "$OLD had diverged and rejoined by RE-CLONE (Patroni log), not restart or pg_rewind" bash -c "[ '$REJOIN' = re-clone ] && grep -qE 'reinitializing due to diverged timelines|Removing data directory' '$F1'"
fi""")
r("""rm -f "$EV_DIR"/L2/chain-switchover*.md""","""rm -f "$EV_DIR"/L2/$OUT-switchover*.md""")
r("""  note "Hop $HOPS: leader \\`$(leader)\\`, sync standby \\`$SYNC\\`, switchover to \\`$TGT\\`. Evidence: [\\`chain-switchover-$HOPS.md\\`](chain-switchover-$HOPS.md)."
  RUNS=1 TO="$TGT" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/chain-switchover-$HOPS.md\"""","""  note "Hop $HOPS: leader \\`$(leader)\\`, sync standby \\`$SYNC\\`, switchover to \\`$TGT\\`. Evidence: [\\`$OUT-switchover-$HOPS.md\\`]($OUT-switchover-$HOPS.md)."
  RUNS=1 TO="$TGT" EV_OUT="$EV_DIR/L2/$OUT-switchover-$HOPS.md\"""")
r("""{ printf '# L2 failure mode: chain\\n\\n**Result: %s**\\n\\n' "$verdict"
  printf -- '- **Fault:** Node failover""","""{ printf '# L2 failure mode: %s\\n\\n**Result: %s**\\n\\n' "$OUT" "$verdict"
  [ "$FIRST" = node ] || printf -- '- **Fault:** Diverge failover (replication from the primary blocked for a few seconds while it commits, then its node stopped), so the old primary holds WAL no replica received and must rejoin by re-clone (ADR-008). Then a planned switchover back to it, through the sync standby if needed. This is the original trigger of the L3 archiving stall. Archive health is checked on the returned primary.\\n'
  [ "$FIRST" = diverge ] || printf -- '- **Fault:** Node failover""")
r("""- **Reproduce:** `make failover-chain`\\n' "$STARTED\"""","""- **Reproduce:** `make failover-%s`\\n' "$STARTED\"""")
r(""""$((SECONDS-T0))"
  printf -- '- **Versions:**""",""""$((SECONDS-T0))" "$( [ "$FIRST" = node ] && echo chain || echo diverge)"
  printf -- '- **Versions:**""")
r("""  row "$EV_DIR/L2/chain-node.md" | sed 's/^| 1 |/| node |/'
  for f in "$EV_DIR"/L2/chain-switchover-*.md;""","""  row "$F1" | sed "s/^| 1 |/| $FIRST |/"
  for f in "$EV_DIR"/L2/$OUT-switchover-*.md;""")
r("""| redact > "$EV_DIR/L2/chain.md\"""","""| redact > "$EV_DIR/L2/$OUT.md\"""")
r("""log "RESULT L2 chain: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L2/chain.md\"""","""log "RESULT L2 $OUT: $verdict -> docs/evidence/L2/$OUT.md\"""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='tests/l2-summary.sh'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('MODES="pod node storage split-brain switchover chain api-outage"','MODES="pod node storage split-brain switchover chain diverge api-outage"')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='Makefile'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("switchover failover-chain test-failover","switchover failover-chain failover-diverge test-failover")
s=s.replace("""test-failover: failover-pod""","""failover-diverge: ## L2/ADR-008: primary diverges (replication blocked, then node stopped), rejoins by re-clone, switch back
	@tests/failover-chain.sh diverge

test-failover: failover-pod""")
s=s.replace("switchover failover-chain ## L2 gate","switchover failover-chain failover-diverge ## L2 gate")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared settings. Sourced by every project script.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
set -a
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT_DIR/versions.env"
set +a

CLUSTER_NAME=pg-ha
API_PORT=6550
BIN_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/bin"
SECRETS_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/secrets"
RUN_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/.run"
export KUBECONFIG="$RUN_DIR/kubeconfig"
export PATH="$BIN_DIR:$PATH"

# Image tag derived from the pinned inputs, so a version change produces a new tag.
pg_version="${POSTGRES_BASE_IMAGE#postgres:}"; pg_version="${pg_version%%-*}"
PG_IMAGE="pg-ha-postgres:${pg_version}-patroni${PATRONI_DEB_VERSION%%-*}-pgbackrest${PGBACKREST_DEB_VERSION%%-*}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L4 (ADR-010, R5.1, R5.3): restores the whole cluster from the pgBackRest repository into an empty namespace,
# through Patroni's custom bootstrap (deploy/restore). The first member restores and recovers, the other two
# clone from it, so the result is 1 primary and 2 streaming replicas, as in production.
#   NS=pg-restore              target namespace. The L0 certificates cover only pg-ha and pg-restore.
#   TARGET_TIME='YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS+06'   point in time, with a REQUIRED timezone offset. Empty: latest.
#   TARGET_TIMELINE=latest     recovery target timeline (default latest).
# The restored cluster never archives into the source stanza: archive_mode is off (30-restore.yml), and it
# reads the repository only through restore_command. Never prints a secret.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
SRC_NS=$PG_NS; NS=${NS:-pg-restore}; TARGET_TIME=${TARGET_TIME:-}; TARGET_TIMELINE=${TARGET_TIMELINE:-latest}
[ "$NS" != "$SRC_NS" ] || die "refusing to restore into the source namespace $SRC_NS"
[ "$NS" = pg-restore ] || die "NS must be pg-restore: the L0 certificates name only pg-ha and pg-restore"
if [ -n "$TARGET_TIME" ]; then
  [[ "$TARGET_TIME" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\ [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]+)?[+-][0-9]{2}(:?[0-9]{2})?$ ]] ||
    die "TARGET_TIME must look like '2026-11-26 01:30:00+06', with a timezone offset (the VM runs UTC, the lead works in UTC+6)"
fi
[[ "$TARGET_TIMELINE" =~ ^(latest|current|[0-9]+)$ ]] || die "TARGET_TIMELINE must be latest, current or a number"
if kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  [ -z "$(kubectl -n "$NS" get pods,pvc -o name 2>/dev/null)" ] || die "namespace $NS is not empty, run: make restore-clean"
fi
T0=$(date +%s.%N)
log "Restoring into namespace $NS: target ${TARGET_TIME:-latest (end of the archive)}, timeline $TARGET_TIMELINE"

kubectl create ns "$NS" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null
# Same Secrets as the source namespace, copied server-side so no value is printed or stored in an annotation.
for s in pg-credentials pg-tls pgbackrest-tls pgbackrest-repo; do
  kubectl -n "$SRC_NS" get secret "$s" -o json | jq --arg s "$s" '{apiVersion, kind, type, data, metadata: {name: $s}}' |
    kubectl -n "$NS" apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-restore --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null
done

q() { printf "'%s'" "$1"; }
{ echo "# Generated by scripts/restore.sh at $(date -u +%FT%TZ). Do not edit or commit."
  echo "bootstrap:"
  echo "  method: pgbackrest"
  echo "  pgbackrest:"
  echo "    command: \"sh /etc/patroni/scripts/restore-bootstrap.sh $(q "$TARGET_TIME") $(q "$TARGET_TIMELINE")\""
  echo "    no_params: true"
  echo "    recovery_conf:"
  echo "      restore_command: pgbackrest --stanza=main archive-get %f \"%p\""
  echo "      recovery_target_timeline: $(q "$TARGET_TIMELINE")"
  echo "      recovery_target_action: promote"
  [ -z "$TARGET_TIME" ] || echo "      recovery_target_time: $(q "$TARGET_TIME")"
  echo "postgresql:"
  echo "  parameters:"
  echo "    archive_mode: \"off\"   # ADR-010: never archive into the source stanza"

kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/restore" | sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|" | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null

PG_NS=$NS   # the Patroni helpers below now read the restored cluster

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs one Job from the pg-backup CronJob template and waits for it. No exec (D4).
#   scripts/pgbr-job.sh NAME [COMMAND] [ENV=VALUE...]
# Without COMMAND (or with an empty one) the Job runs the CronJob's own backup script, as make backup does.
# Prints the Job's log, and exits non-zero if the Job failed.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
name=$1; cmd=${2:-}; shift; [ $# -eq 0 ] || shift
envs=$(printf '%s\n' "$@" | jq -Rn '[inputs | select(length > 0) | split("=") | {name: .[0], value: (.[1:] | join("="))}]')
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" delete job "$name" --ignore-not-found --wait=true >/dev/null
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" create job "$name" --from=cronjob/pg-backup --dry-run=client -o json |
  jq --arg cmd "$cmd" --argjson envs "$envs" '
    .spec.template.spec.containers[0] |= ((if $cmd == "" then . else .command = ["bash", "-ec", $cmd] end) | .env += $envs)' |
  kubectl -n "$PG_NS" apply -f - >/dev/null
end=$((SECONDS + ${JOB_WAIT:-1800}))
while :; do
  s=$(kubectl -n "$PG_NS" get job "$name" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}/{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)
  [ "${s%/*}" = 1 ] || [ "${s#*/}" = 1 ] && break
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { s=timeout; break; }
  sleep 2
done
kubectl -n "$PG_NS" logs "job/$name" 2>/dev/null || true
[ "${s%/*}" = 1 ]

#   TARGET_TIME='YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS+06'   point in time, with a REQUIRED timezone offset. Empty: latest.
#   TARGET_TIMELINE=latest     recovery target timeline (default latest).
# The restored cluster never archives into the source stanza: archive_mode is off (30-restore.yml), and it
# reads the repository only through restore_command. Never prints a secret.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
SRC_NS=$PG_NS; NS=${NS:-pg-restore}; TARGET_TIME=${TARGET_TIME:-}; TARGET_TIMELINE=${TARGET_TIMELINE:-latest}
[ "$NS" != "$SRC_NS" ] || die "refusing to restore into the source namespace $SRC_NS"
[ "$NS" = pg-restore ] || die "NS must be pg-restore: the L0 certificates name only pg-ha and pg-restore"
if [ -n "$TARGET_TIME" ]; then
  [[ "$TARGET_TIME" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\ [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]+)?[+-][0-9]{2}(:?[0-9]{2})?$ ]] ||
    die "TARGET_TIME must look like '2026-11-26 01:30:00+06', with a timezone offset (the VM runs UTC, the lead works in UTC+6)"
fi
[[ "$TARGET_TIMELINE" =~ ^(latest|current|[0-9]+)$ ]] || die "TARGET_TIMELINE must be latest, current or a number"
if kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  [ -z "$(kubectl -n "$NS" get pods,pvc -o name 2>/dev/null)" ] || die "namespace $NS is not empty, run: make restore-clean"
fi
T0=$(date +%s.%N)
log "Restoring into namespace $NS: target ${TARGET_TIME:-latest (end of the archive)}, timeline $TARGET_TIMELINE"

kubectl create ns "$NS" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null
# Same Secrets as the source namespace, copied server-side so no value is printed or stored in an annotation.
for s in pg-credentials pg-tls pgbackrest-tls pgbackrest-repo; do
  kubectl -n "$SRC_NS" get secret "$s" -o json | jq --arg s "$s" '{apiVersion, kind, type, data, metadata: {name: $s}}' |
    kubectl -n "$NS" apply --server-side --field-manager=pg-ha-restore --force-conflicts -f - >/dev/null
done

# 30-restore.yml: Patroni custom bootstrap through pgBackRest, merged over 10-base.yml and 20-archive.yml.
q() { printf "'%s'" "$1"; }
{ echo "# Generated by scripts/restore.sh at $(date -u +%FT%TZ). Do not edit or commit."
  echo "bootstrap:"
  echo "  method: pgbackrest"
  echo "  pgbackrest:"
  echo "    command: \"sh /etc/patroni/scripts/restore-bootstrap.sh $(q "$TARGET_TIME") $(q "$TARGET_TIMELINE")\""
  echo "    no_params: true"
  echo "    recovery_conf:"
  echo "      restore_command: pgbackrest --stanza=main archive-get %f \"%p\""
  echo "      recovery_target_timeline: $(q "$TARGET_TIMELINE")"
  echo "      recovery_target_action: promote"
  [ -z "$TARGET_TIME" ] || echo "      recovery_target_time: $(q "$TARGET_TIME")"
  echo "postgresql:"
  echo "  parameters:"
  echo "    archive_mode: \"off\"   # ADR-010: never archive into the source stanza"
} > "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/restore/30-restore.yml"
kubectl kustomize "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/restore" | sed "s|__PG_IMAGE__|$PG_IMAGE|" | kubectl apply -f - >/dev/null

PG_NS=$NS   # the Patroni helpers below now read the restored cluster
end=$((SECONDS + ${RESTORE_WAIT:-1200})); T_LEADER=""
until [ -n "$T_LEADER" ] && patroni_healthy; do
  [ $SECONDS -lt $end ] || { patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "\(.name) \(.role) \(.state)"' || true; die "restored cluster not healthy after ${RESTORE_WAIT:-1200} s"; }
  [ -n "$T_LEADER" ] || ! patroni_cluster 2>/dev/null | jq -e '[.members[] | select(.role == "leader" and .state == "running")] | length == 1' >/dev/null || T_LEADER=$(date +%s.%N)
  sleep 2
done
T1=$(date +%s.%N)
patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | "  \(.name) \(.role) \(.state) timeline \(.timeline // "-")"'
log "RESTORE_OK namespace=$NS target=${TARGET_TIME:-latest} primary_ready=$(awk -v a="$T0" -v b="$T_LEADER" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')s cluster_healthy=$(awk -v a="$T0" -v b="$T1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f", b-a}')s"
EOF
cat > scripts/restore-clean.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L4: deletes the restored cluster: only the pg-restore namespace and its PVCs. Refuses any other namespace.
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"
NS=${NS:-pg-restore}
[ "$NS" = pg-restore ] || die "restore-clean deletes only namespace pg-restore, not $NS"
kubectl get ns "$NS" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log "namespace $NS does not exist, nothing to delete"; exit 0; }
kubectl -n "$NS" delete statefulset --all --wait=true >/dev/null
kubectl -n "$NS" delete pvc --all --wait=true
kubectl delete ns "$NS" --wait=true
rm -f "$ROOT_DIR/deploy/restore/30-restore.yml"
log "deleted namespace $NS and its PVCs"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/restore.sh scripts/restore-clean.sh
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='deploy/pg/scripts/restore-bootstrap.sh'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("# in an empty volume. $1 is the recovery target time with a timezone offset, or empty for the latest state.","# in an empty volume. $1 is the recovery target time with a timezone offset, or empty for the latest state;\n# $2 the target timeline (default latest).")
s=s.replace("""if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
  set -- --type=time "--target=$1" --target-timeline=latest
else
  set -- --type=default --target-timeline=latest
fi""","""TL=${2:-latest}
if [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
  set -- --type=time "--target=$1" "--target-timeline=$TL"
else
  set -- --type=default "--target-timeline=$TL"
fi""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='.gitignore'; s=open(p).read()
s+="\n# generated by scripts/restore.sh\n/deploy/restore/30-restore.yml\n"
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='Makefile'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("deploy backup seed","deploy backup restore restore-clean test-restore test-restore-full test-pitr test-restore-schedule test-l4 seed")
s=s.replace("""seed: ## Load""","""restore: ## L4: restore the whole cluster into NS=pg-restore [TARGET_TIME='YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS+06'] [TARGET_TIMELINE=latest]
	@scripts/restore.sh

restore-clean: ## L4: delete only the pg-restore namespace and its PVCs
	@scripts/restore-clean.sh

seed: ## Load""")
s=s.replace("""status: ## Show""","""test-restore: ## L4 R4.5/R5.4: restore test Job from the pg-restore-test CronJob template (scratch emptyDir)
	@scripts/pgbr-job.sh pg-restore-test-manual-$$(date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S) --from pg-restore-test

test-restore-full: ## L4 R5.1: make restore (latest) into pg-restore, row counts and checksums vs the source
	@tests/l4-restore-full.sh

test-pitr: ## L4 R5.3: markers A and B around T, restore to T, A present and B absent
	@tests/l4-pitr.sh

test-restore-schedule: ## L4 R4.5: a restore-test Job created by the CronJob itself, then default restored
	@tests/l4-restore-scheduled.sh

test-l4: test-restore-full test-pitr test-restore test-restore-schedule ## L4 gate: all of the above

status: ## Show""")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the L4 restore tests. Each test writes docs/evidence/L4/<part>.md, then regenerates
# docs/evidence/L4-restore.md. SQL runs in the test client pod in pg-ha (no exec in a Postgres pod); it
# reaches the restored cluster through its pg-rw Service in pg-restore. Repository reads run in Jobs.
. "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/l3-lib.sh"
mkdir -p "$EV_DIR/L4"
RNS=pg-restore; RRW=pg-rw.$RNS.svc.cluster.local
# The data fingerprint of fingerprint.sql (seeded branch), as one statement for the test client.
FP_SQL="select 'rows.pgbench_accounts=' || count(*) from pgbench_accounts
union all select 'sum.pgbench_accounts=' || sum(hashtext(a::text)::bigint) from pgbench_accounts a
union all select 'rows.pgbench_branches=' || count(*) from pgbench_branches
union all select 'sum.pgbench_branches=' || sum(hashtext(b::text)::bigint) from pgbench_branches b
union all select 'rows.pgbench_tellers=' || count(*) from pgbench_tellers
union all select 'sum.pgbench_tellers=' || sum(hashtext(t::text)::bigint) from pgbench_tellers t"
rpatroni() { local i; for i in 0 1 2; do kubectl get --raw "/api/v1/namespaces/$RNS/pods/pg-$i:8008/proxy/cluster" 2>/dev/null && return 0; done; return 1; }
rleader() { rpatroni | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .name'; }
# History files in the repository archive, from a short Job (repo-ls). Prints one name per line.
repo_history() { local j=pg-repo-ls-$RANDOM o; o=$(pgbr "$j" 'pgbackrest --stanza=main --output=text repo-ls archive/main/17-1') || true
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job "$j" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; grep -E '^[0-9A-F]{8}\.history$' <<<"$o" || true; }
repo_wal_dirs() { local j=pg-repo-ls-$RANDOM o; o=$(pgbr "$j" 'pgbackrest --stanza=main --output=text repo-ls archive/main/17-1') || true
  kubectl -n "$NS" delete job "$j" --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; grep -E '^[0-9A-F]{16}$' <<<"$o" || true; }

l4_finish() { # part title description make-target
  local verdict=PASS; [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ] || verdict=FAIL
  { printf '# L4: %s\n\n**Result: %s**\n\n' "$2" "$verdict"
    printf -- '- **What:** %s\n' "$3"
    printf -- '- **Run:** %s (UTC), %s s\n- **Reproduce:** `make %s`\n' "$STARTED" "$((SECONDS-T0))" "$4"

  [ "$FAILS" -eq 0 ]
}

cat > tests/l4-restore-full.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L4 R5.1 (ADR-010): make restore with no target restores the whole cluster from the repository into the empty
# pg-restore namespace, to the end of the archive on the latest timeline. Requires 1 primary and 2 streaming
# replicas, the source's row counts and checksums, history files present, archive_mode off, and no WAL from
# the restored cluster in the source archive. Cleans up with make restore-clean, which is timed too.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l4-lib.sh"
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
client_up
section "Before: source and repository"
TL=$(patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline')
q "$RW" app "$FP_SQL" | sort > "$W/src"
HIST=$(repo_history); NH=$(grep -c . <<<"$HIST" || true); DIRS0=$(repo_wal_dirs)
note "Source leader \`$(leader)\` on timeline $TL. Source fingerprint (rows and hashtext sums of the seeded tables): $(paste -sd' ' "$W/src")."
note "History files in the repository archive: $NH ($(head -1 <<<"$HIST") to $(tail -1 <<<"$HIST")). WAL directories: $(paste -sd' ' <<<"$DIRS0")."
check "Timeline history files are present for every timeline switch up to $TL (found $NH, need $((TL - 1)))" test "$NH" -ge $((TL - 1))
q "$RW" app "create table if not exists l4_marker (id text primary key, t timestamptz default clock_timestamp())" >/dev/null
q "$RW" app "insert into l4_marker (id) values ('full-$(date +%s)') returning id" > "$W/marker"
wal_fill; archived_after "$(now)" 120 >/dev/null || true
note "Marker row \`$(cat "$W/marker")\` written and archived before the restore."

section "make restore (latest)"
"$ROOT_DIR/scripts/restore-clean.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
T_R=$(now); TAIL=12 run "scripts/restore.sh" && ok=1 || ok=0; T_D=$(now)
check "make restore completed: 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas, 1 sync standby in $RNS" test $ok = 1
RL=$(rleader); RTL=$(rpatroni | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline')
note "Restore wall time $(secs "$T_R" "$T_D") s. Restored leader \`$RL\` on timeline $RTL."
run "kubectl -n $RNS logs $RL -c postgres | grep -E 'Running custom bootstrap|restore-bootstrap|restore command end|recovery stopping|redo done|selected new timeline|archive recovery complete|post-bootstrap|bootstrap from leader|replica has been created' | sed -E 's/[0-9a-f]{32,}/[hex]/g' | head -14" || true

section "Restored data and isolation"
q "$RRW" app "$FP_SQL" | sort > "$W/dst"
run "join -t= $W/src $W/dst | awk -F= '{printf \"%-24s source %-22s restored %-22s %s\\n\", \$1, \$2, \$3, (\$2 == \$3 ? \"match\" : \"MISMATCH\")}'" || true
check "Row counts and checksums of the seeded tables match the source" cmp -s "$W/src" "$W/dst"
check "The marker row written just before the restore is present" test "$(q "$RRW" app "select count(*) from l4_marker where id = '$(cat "$W/marker")'")" = 1
check "Restored cluster is on a new timeline above the source's ($RTL > $TL)" test "$RTL" -gt "$TL"
run "q $RRW monitor \"select name, setting from pg_settings where name in ('archive_mode', 'archive_command') order by 1\"" || true
check "archive_mode is off on the restored primary" test "$(q "$RRW" monitor "select setting from pg_settings where name = 'archive_mode'")" = off
check "The restored primary archived nothing" test "$(q "$RRW" monitor "select archived_count + failed_count from pg_stat_archiver")" = 0
DIRS1=$(repo_wal_dirs); RTLX=$(printf '%08X' "$RTL")
check "The source archive has no WAL on the restored timeline ($RTLX)" bash -c "! grep -q '^$RTLX' <<<'$DIRS1'"
check "Passwords from this namespace's Secret work on the restored cluster (post_bootstrap reset)" bash -c "q $RRW app 'select 1' >/dev/null && q $RRW monitor 'select 1' >/dev/null"

section "make restore-clean"
T_C=$(now); TAIL=4 run "scripts/restore-clean.sh" && cl=1 || cl=0
check "make restore-clean deleted only the pg-restore namespace and its PVCs ($(secs "$T_C" "$(now)") s)" bash -c "test $cl = 1 && ! kubectl get ns $RNS >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl get ns $PG_NS >/dev/null"
q "$RW" app "drop table if exists l4_marker" >/dev/null || true
printf '| Restore wall time (s) | Restored timeline | Source timeline | History files |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| %s | %s | %s | %s |\n' "$(secs "$T_R" "$T_D")" "$RTL" "$TL" "$NH" > "$W/sum"; note "$(cat "$W/sum")"
l4_finish restore-full "Full restore into an empty namespace (R5.1)" "\`make restore\` with no target: the whole cluster restored from Garage into the empty \`pg-restore\` namespace through Patroni's custom bootstrap, to the end of the archive on the latest timeline. Compared with the source, then removed with \`make restore-clean\`." test-restore-full
EOF
chmod +x tests/l4-restore-full.sh; bash -n tests/l4-restore-full.sh && echo ok; tail -4 /tmp/claude-1001/-home-[REDACTED-USER]-[REDACTED-GCP-PROJECT]/e73dfe31-c4f5-4462-88b4-bec9dcc42812/scratchpad/diverge1.log

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# L4 R5.1 (ADR-010): make restore with no target restores the whole cluster from the repository into the empty
# pg-restore namespace, to the end of the archive on the latest timeline. Requires 1 primary and 2 streaming
# replicas, the source's row counts and checksums, history files present, archive_mode off, and no WAL from
# the restored cluster in the source archive. Cleans up with make restore-clean, which is timed too.
. "$(dirname "$0")/l4-lib.sh"
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT
client_up
section "Before: source and repository"
TL=$(patroni_cluster | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline')
q "$RW" app "$FP_SQL" | sort > "$W/src"
HIST=$(repo_history); NH=$(grep -c . <<<"$HIST" || true); DIRS0=$(repo_wal_dirs)
note "Source leader \`$(leader)\` on timeline $TL. Source fingerprint (rows and hashtext sums of the seeded tables): $(paste -sd' ' "$W/src")."
note "History files in the repository archive: $NH ($(head -1 <<<"$HIST") to $(tail -1 <<<"$HIST")). WAL directories: $(paste -sd' ' <<<"$DIRS0")."
check "Timeline history files are present for every timeline switch up to $TL (found $NH, need $((TL - 1)))" test "$NH" -ge $((TL - 1))
q "$RW" app "create table if not exists l4_marker (id text primary key, t timestamptz default clock_timestamp())" >/dev/null
q "$RW" app "insert into l4_marker (id) values ('full-$(date +%s)') returning id" > "$W/marker"
wal_fill; archived_after "$(now)" 120 >/dev/null || true
note "Marker row \`$(cat "$W/marker")\` written and archived before the restore."

section "make restore (latest)"
"$ROOT_DIR/scripts/restore-clean.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
T_R=$(now); TAIL=12 run "scripts/restore.sh" && ok=1 || ok=0; T_D=$(now)
check "make restore completed: 1 leader, 2 streaming replicas, 1 sync standby in $RNS" test $ok = 1
RL=$(rleader); RTL=$(rpatroni | jq -r '.members[] | select(.role == "leader") | .timeline')
note "Restore wall time $(secs "$T_R" "$T_D") s. Restored leader \`$RL\` on timeline $RTL."
run "kubectl -n $RNS logs $RL -c postgres | grep -E 'Running custom bootstrap|restore-bootstrap|restore command end|recovery stopping|redo done|selected new timeline|archive recovery complete|post-bootstrap|bootstrap from leader|replica has been created' | sed -E 's/[0-9a-f]{32,}/[hex]/g' | head -14" || true

section "Restored data and isolation"
q "$RRW" app "$FP_SQL" | sort > "$W/dst"
run "join -t= $W/src $W/dst | awk -F= '{printf \"%-24s source %-22s restored %-22s %s\\n\", \$1, \$2, \$3, (\$2 == \$3 ? \"match\" : \"MISMATCH\")}'" || true
check "Row counts and checksums of the seeded tables match the source" cmp -s "$W/src" "$W/dst"
check "The marker row written just before the restore is present" test "$(q "$RRW" app "select count(*) from l4_marker where id = '$(cat "$W/marker")'")" = 1
check "Restored cluster is on a new timeline above the source's ($RTL > $TL)" test "$RTL" -gt "$TL"
run "q $RRW monitor \"select name, setting from pg_settings where name in ('archive_mode', 'archive_command') order by 1\"" || true
check "archive_mode is off on the restored primary" test "$(q "$RRW" monitor "select setting from pg_settings where name = 'archive_mode'")" = off
check "The restored primary archived nothing" test "$(q "$RRW" monitor "select archived_count + failed_count from pg_stat_archiver")" = 0
DIRS1=$(repo_wal_dirs); RTLX=$(printf '%08X' "$RTL")
check "The source archive has no WAL on the restored timeline ($RTLX)" bash -c "! grep -q '^$RTLX' <<<'$DIRS1'"
check "Passwords from this namespace's Secret work on the restored cluster (post_bootstrap reset)" bash -c "q $RRW app 'select 1' >/dev/null && q $RRW monitor 'select 1' >/dev/null"

section "make restore-clean"
T_C=$(now); TAIL=4 run "scripts/restore-clean.sh" && cl=1 || cl=0
check "make restore-clean deleted only the pg-restore namespace and its PVCs ($(secs "$T_C" "$(now)") s)" bash -c "test $cl = 1 && ! kubectl get ns $RNS >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl get ns $PG_NS >/dev/null"
q "$RW" app "drop table if exists l4_marker" >/dev/null || true
printf '| Restore wall time (s) | Restored timeline | Source timeline | History files |\n|---:|---:|---:|---:|\n| %s | %s | %s | %s |\n' "$(secs "$T_R" "$T_D")" "$RTL" "$TL" "$NH" > "$W/sum"; note "$(cat "$W/sum")"

Compared with the source, then removed with \`make restore-clean\`." test-restore-full
EOF
